summary: Write, from the code, how a tester reaches each Desktop item, using the cheap model
logs: paths: 1748 items returned for 1744 asked; 0 areas returned nothing

items.where: Open AGI Desktop > Continue in browser (sign-in screen). On the web, /login > Log in or sign up
steps: Open the AGI Desktop app while signed out, so the sign-in screen with the line 'Sign in to' and the button Continue in browser shows.
Click Continue in browser.
In the browser that opens, sign in with your AGI account (email, or a provider).
Return to the Desktop app and wait for the handoff to finish.
Look for a signed-in app: the sign-in screen should be gone. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI account and a browser on the Mac
items.note: The Desktop sign-in is a browser handoff; the web sign-in form is the same email step.

items.where: Log in or sign up (sign-in screen) > type a new email > Continue
steps: On the sign-in screen, find the field labelled Email address.
Type an email address that has no AGI account yet.
Click Continue.
Look for the next step (a code or password step) that a new account goes through. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a new email address that has no AGI account
items.note: No separate sign-up screen was found; the same email step handles new and existing accounts. The string Create account exists in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/auth.json but I did not find where it is shown.

items.where: Log in or sign up > new email address > Continue > Confirm your email address
steps: Sign up with a new email address (see S3.02).
On the next screen, read the heading Confirm your email address.
Open the email inbox and find the message with the code.
Enter the code and confirm, then try to use the app before confirming to see that it is blocked.
Compare with Expected: the account is usable only after the email is confirmed.
items.needs: a new email address you can read
items.note: I did not trace which server state sends a new account to this step; the blocked-before-confirm check is not verified in code.

items.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Verify this device (code step)
steps: Enter an email address of an existing account and click Continue.
On the Verify this device screen, check the inbox for the emailed code.
Type the code into the field labelled Code and click Continue.
Click Resend code and watch for the countdown text Resend code in ... seconds.
Compare with Expected: the code is accepted, and resend works after the countdown.
items.needs: an account whose email you can read
items.note: The one-time-code autofill attribute was not checked in code.

items.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Forgot password?
steps: Enter the email of an account that has a password, then click Continue.
On the password screen, click Forgot password?.
Check what message appears and whether a reset email arrives.
Compare with Expected: a reset code or link is sent by email.
items.needs: an account with a password and an inbox you can read
items.note: The wording of the message shown after the click was not traced.

items.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Forgot password? > emailed code > Continue (new password step)
steps: Start a reset as in S3.06 and open the reset email.
Enter the code on the reset screen and click Continue.
On the new password screen, type a new password and click Continue.
Compare with Expected: you are signed in with the new password.
items.needs: an account with a password and an inbox you can read
items.note: The heading of the new password screen was not found; the labels above come from the step file.

items.where: Log in or sign up > Continue with Google (or Continue with GitHub)
steps: On the sign-in screen, look under the email field for buttons that start with Continue with.
Click Continue with Google (or Continue with GitHub).
Complete the provider's sign-in in the window that opens.
Compare with Expected: the app signs you in and returns you to it.
items.needs: an outside account (Google or GitHub)
items.note: Which providers appear depends on configuration in apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts, which I did not check.

items.where: Log in or sign up > work email > Continue (web). On AGI Desktop: Continue in browser, then sign in with your organization's single sign-on
steps: Enter the work email of an SSO-enabled organization on the Log in or sign up screen.
Click Continue.
Expect to be sent to your organization's sign-in page in the browser; complete it.
Compare with Expected: you land back in the app signed in.
items.needs: an account in an organization that uses single sign-on
items.note: No button is named for SSO. The redirect starts from the Continue step when the server reports an enterprise connection (apps/web/features/auth/IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx around line 393).

items.where: Log in or sign up > type a work email > Continue
steps: On the Log in or sign up screen, type a work email address of an organization that has its own sign-in.
Click Continue.
Compare with Expected: you are routed to that organization's sign-in page instead of a password screen.
Try a personal address on the same screen and compare: it should show the normal password or code step.
items.needs: a work email of an organization with single sign-on, and a personal email
items.note: The domain match itself is decided on the server through the sign-in factors; the client only follows the enterprise result. I did not trace the server domain lookup.

items.where: Settings > Security > Passkeys > Add a passkey
steps: Sign in, then open Settings and click Security.
Scroll to the Passkeys section.
Click Add a passkey and complete the system passkey prompt.
Look for the new passkey in the list, with its own rename and remove controls.
Compare with Expected: the passkey is registered and listed.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a Mac or device that supports passkeys
items.note: The same panel is used on the web settings screen as well as in the Desktop app.

items.where: Log in or sign up > Sign in with a passkey or security key
steps: Sign out, then open the sign-in screen.
Type the email of the account that has a passkey, or leave it blank if the button is shown without it.
Click Sign in with a passkey or security key.
Pick the passkey in the system prompt.
Compare with Expected: you are signed in without a password or code.
items.needs: an account with a registered passkey and a passkey-capable device

labels.text: Sign in with a passkey or security key

items.note: The button only appears when passkey sign-in is configured and the browser supports passkeys (apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts and AuthEmailStep.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Security > Authenticator app > Set up authenticator app
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the Authenticator app block.
Click Set up authenticator app.
Add the shown key or QR code to an authenticator app on your phone, then type the six-digit code.
Click Enable two-factor to confirm.
Sign out and sign in again: a second-factor step should appear. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an authenticator app on a phone
items.note: The screen can say Authenticator apps are temporarily unavailable; the exact QR and setup-key wording was not checked.

items.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > password (or code) > Confirm it is you
steps: With two-factor on (S3.13), sign out and sign in with the email and password.
Read the Confirm it is you screen and the factor it asks for.
Click Use a backup code to see the alternative, then go back and use the authenticator code.
Compare with Expected: the session starts only after the second factor.
items.needs: an account with two-factor on and its authenticator app
items.note: Which factor is asked first depends on the account; the other alternatives are text, email and authenticator codes in the same file.

items.where: Settings > Security > Authenticator app > Set up authenticator app (codes appear after the code is accepted)
steps: Finish the two-factor setup in S3.13 by entering a valid code.
Read the Backup codes list that appears.
Click Copy codes, Download codes or Print codes, and check each result.
Tick I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe and click Done.
Compare with Expected: the codes are shown once and cannot be read again.
items.needs: an account where two-factor is being set up, and an authenticator app

labels.text: I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe

items.note: The path for regenerating codes later was not traced.

items.where: Log in or sign up > email > Continue > Enter your password > Can’t reach this email? (or Lost the device with your codes? on the Confirm it is you step)
steps: On the password screen, click Can’t reach this email?.
Choose what you lost from the list (password, email access, or two-factor device and backup codes).
Fill in the text box to describe what happened and submit.
Compare with Expected: you see a confirmation that the request was sent.
items.needs: an account you can no longer fully sign in to

labels.text: Lost the device with your codes?

items.note: The recovery page at /recover is the same form. The request is handled as a support ticket, and the final submit result was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Security > Sign-in methods > Connect
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and click Security.
Find the Sign-in methods block.
Click Connect on a provider such as Google, and finish the outside sign-in.
Check that the row now shows the account and a Disconnect button.
Click Disconnect and confirm, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: an outside account (Google or GitHub) to link
items.note: Rows for sign-in methods also show a Remove button for identities; I did not trace which one unlinks.

items.needs: an existing account and a second email address
items.note: Searched apps/web/features/auth, apps/web/app/login and apps/web/app/signup for already exists, already registered, already linked, no account, not registered, sign in instead and sign up instead; no matching copy was found. The cited lines (AuthEmailStep.tsx:80, IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:301) hold no such message.

items.where: Log in or sign up > new email > Continue (sign-up gate on /signup shows the I agree to the checkbox)
steps: Sign up with a new email (S3.02) and reach the sign-up terms gate.
Read the line I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
Check that the continue button stays disabled until the box is ticked.
Tick the box and continue.
For a re-prompt, sign in to an account whose terms need review: the Sign out button on the review screen appears. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a new email for sign-up; a re-prompt needs a Terms version change, which you cannot cause from the UI
items.note: The re-prompt on a Terms change is enforced on the server (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts) and cannot be triggered from the UI.

items.where: Sign in as a new account > Welcome screen (/welcome) > Preferred name
steps: Sign in with a new account so the Welcome setup opens.
Type your name in the Preferred name field.
Click Continue, then pick a role and a first use (S3.23).
Open Settings > General and check that the name shows up.
Compare with Expected: the name is saved to the account.
items.needs: a new account (first run)
items.note: The save target of the name was not traced; the Settings > General check is inferred from the settings navigation keywords.

items.where: Sign in as a new account > Welcome screen (/welcome) > What best describes your work? > Continue > What do you want to do first?
steps: On the Welcome screen, type a name and open the What best describes your work? list.
Pick one role, then click Continue.
On What do you want to do first?, pick one option such as Write and debug code.
Read the starter prompts shown for that option, then click Finish.
Compare with Expected: the first chat reflects the chosen use.
items.needs: a new account (first run)

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

items.note: How the chosen role and use shape replies was not traced past the saved preferences.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Response style
steps: Open Settings and click Personalization.
Set Response style, Response length and Technical level.
Send a question in a new chat.
Compare the reply with the chosen style and length.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Welcome screen asks only for name, role and first use; personalization style is set in Settings > Personalization, not in onboarding.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Import memory from other AI providers > Start import
steps: Open Settings, click Personalization, and find the row Import memory from other AI providers.
Click the import button for that row, then pick a source (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other).
Click Copy prompt and paste the prompt into the other assistant; then paste or upload its answer.
Review the preview list, select items, and click Start import.
Compare with Expected: the chosen memories appear in your saved memories.
items.needs: an account on another assistant to copy memories from

labels.text: Import memory from other AI providers

items.note: MemorySection is placed under Personalization was not traced line by line; the path follows the settings screen mapping in WebSettingsModal.tsx.

items.needs: a new account
items.note: Searched apps/web for recommend (onboarding, connectors, settings, chat); no recommended-app list or guided connector flow was found. WebSettingsModal.tsx lines 309 and 337 only load the Connectors panel through the adapter, with no recommendations.

items.where: Settings > Computer use (AGI Desktop app only) > Allowed apps > Manage
steps: In the Desktop app, open Settings and click Computer use.
Read the hint Let AGI see your screen and use the mouse and keyboard in apps you allow.
Look at the Control block with the Any app setting.
Click Manage next to Allowed apps, add an app, and check the list.
When a macOS permission is needed, the Accessibility prompt opens. Compare with Expected: the grants are recorded in the list.
items.needs: the AGI Desktop app on a Mac
items.note: No Screen Recording guidance text was found; the macOS Accessibility prompt is opened from apps/desktop/electron/runtime/systemPermissions.ts.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Chrome
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities, then find the Chrome block.
If it says nothing has asked to pair yet, install the extension in Chrome.
In Chrome, open the Extension side panel, choose Connect to Desktop, and type the code the app shows in its dialog.
Check that the block reads Paired and answering.
Click Unpair and confirm Unpair this browser?, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: Chrome with the AGI extension and the AGI Desktop app on a Mac
items.note: The Pair button text on the Desktop side was not found; pairing starts from the Chrome side panel, and the code dialog is opened by Desktop.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone (desktop app only, paid plan)
steps: In the AGI desktop app, open Settings and choose Capabilities.
Scroll to the Remote Control section (the section is hidden in a browser and on a Free plan).
Click Pair a phone. A pairing QR code and a short pairing code appear.
On the phone, open AGI Mobile, go to AGI Code, choose Add device, and scan the QR code (or type the pairing code).

Look at the section: it should show the phone as connected (Connected to <phone name>) with a Disconnect phone button, and the pairing should be tied to the same signed-in account. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: the AGI desktop app on a paid plan, a phone with AGI Mobile signed in to the same account, phone camera for the QR code
items.note: The section returns nothing outside the desktop host and shows a paid-plan notice on Free; the owner memory says Remote Control is hidden in v1, and I did not find a v1 hide flag in this section. Account binding was not traced past the dispatcher (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:2659).

items.where: Chat > long-running answer > banner 'Get notified when the response is ready.' > Enable (or the X to dismiss). To change later: Settings > Notifications > Browser notifications
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Send a request that takes a while (for example a long answer or an agent work task).
While the response is still generating, look for the banner 'Get notified when the response is ready.' under the top bar of the chat.
Click Enable to get the browser permission prompt, or click the X labelled 'Dismiss notification prompt' to hide it.
Open Settings > Notifications and find Browser notifications to turn it on or off. Compare with Expected: the offer is optional and can be declined and changed later.
items.needs: none (a request long enough that the answer is still generating; the banner does not show again once the browser permission is decided or the banner was dismissed)

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

items.note: The banner shows only while browser permission is still 'default' and the banner was not resolved before (stored in localStorage), so a tester who already answered once will not see it again; the banner's position in the chat layout was not confirmed.

items.where: Sign in with a new account > welcome screen 'What should we call you?' > Continue > 'What do you want to do first?' > a prompt under 'Start with one of these' (or Skip for now)
steps: Sign in with a brand-new account that has not finished onboarding.
On the screen 'What should we call you?', type a name in Preferred name and click Continue.
On 'What do you want to do first?', read the line 'We will suggest a few prompts to get you started.' and the prompts under 'Start with one of these'.
Click one prompt. The app opens a chat with that prompt placed in the message box (it is filled in, not sent).
Look at the chat: it should show the starter prompt ready to send, leading into a first conversation. Compare with Expected. Clicking Skip for now instead opens the chat without a prompt.
items.needs: a brand-new account that has never finished onboarding
items.note: The wizard is the /welcome page (apps/web/app/welcome/page.tsx); the code that sends a new account to /welcome after sign-in was not found by grep, so the entry path is unconfirmed. Items S3.33 and S3.34 do not exist in the plan file and were skipped.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat
steps: Sign in and stay on the Chat screen with the left sidebar.
Click "New chat" in the sidebar (the same control is in the collapsed rail).
Look for an empty conversation with the message box ready to type in, then type a message and send it.
Compare with Expected: a new empty chat with a ready composer.
items.needs: none

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > a conversation title
steps: Sign in and look at the sidebar list under the "Recents" heading.
Click a past conversation title.
Look for its earlier messages (transcript) and a message box to continue the chat.
Compare with Expected: transcript shown and the chat can be continued.
items.needs: a past conversation in the sidebar

items.where: Sidebar > Search
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
In the box "Search your workspace", type a word from a past chat title or message.
Wait for matching past conversations to appear.
Click one result and check that its conversation opens.
items.needs: a past conversation with a known word in it
items.note: The code does not show whether results update while typing or only after Enter; the tester should try both. Command key plus K opens "Search Conversations" in the command palette as a second route.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Archived chats > Manage
steps: Open the account menu and choose "Settings", then "Privacy".
Find "Archived chats" and click "Manage".
Check the list of archived chats; try "Restore" on one and check it returns to the sidebar.
Try the sidebar "Archived (N)" button as a second route and compare with Expected: open, restore or delete.
items.needs: at least one archived chat (archive one from its row menu first)
items.note: The sidebar button appears only when at least one chat is archived. Delete moves a chat to "Recently deleted" and does not remove it at once.

items.where: Sidebar > Pinned section, set from a chat row's menu > Pin
steps: Open the menu of a chat row in the sidebar and click "Pin".
Look for the "Pinned" section at the top of the chat list.
Click the pinned chat and check that it opens.
Open its menu again and click "Unpin"; check that it leaves the Pinned section.
items.needs: at least two chats

items.where: Sidebar > Projects (left rail item "Projects")
steps: Click "Projects" in the left rail.
Look for the list of your projects.
Click "New project" and check that a create dialog opens.
Click an existing project card and check that it opens.
items.needs: none (one project helps)

items.where: Projects > a project card
steps: Click "Projects" in the left rail and open a project card.
Check the project name heading at the top.
Check the tabs "Chats", "Artifacts", "Work", "Sources", "Scheduled".
Compare with Expected: name, description or instructions, and entries to its chats and files.
items.needs: a project
items.note: The project home is a page with tabs; a description summary was not confirmed in the files read.

items.where: Projects > a project > Chats tab
steps: Open a project.
Click the "Chats" tab.
Check the list of this project's conversations.
Click one and check that it opens.
items.needs: a project with at least one chat in it

items.where: Projects > a project > Sources tab > Add sources
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources" and choose a file, Google Drive, or "Add text".
Check that the new item appears in the Sources list.
Look for a remove control on that item and check that it removes it.
items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: Project settings also has a "Files" section with a knowledge files panel. The remove control was not confirmed in the files read. Google Drive needs its connector.

items.where: Projects > a project > Project options > Project settings > Instructions
steps: Open a project and click "Project options".
Click "Project settings".
Type text in the "Instructions" box and click "Save".
Open a new chat in that project and check that the reply follows the instructions.
items.needs: a project
items.note: Whether the instructions change the reply is not checked by this code read.

items.where: Projects > a project > Project options > Share
steps: Open a project, click "Project options", then "Share".
Click "Add people" and pick a person from the workspace.
Choose "Can view" or "Can edit" for that person.
Check that the person appears in the member list; then check it from the second account.
items.needs: a second account in the same workspace
items.note: The owner is listed with the label "Owner". Only the owner can add or remove people, per Expected; not tested here.

items.where: Projects > a project > Project options > Project settings > Memory
steps: Open a project's "Project settings".
Scroll to the "Memory" section and read the "Project memories" list.
Add a memory in the box "Add a memory only this project uses".
Check it appears only in this project and that the "Use memories from outside this project" checkbox is shown separately from account memory.
items.needs: a project

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project

items.where: Chat screen > message box > mode "Work"
steps: On the new chat screen, open the mode control in the message box and choose "Work".
Type a goal for an autonomous task and send it.
Check that the screen shows the work run and that "Work history" is reachable from the command palette or the home screen.
Compare with Expected: a place to state a goal and reach recent work.
items.needs: a paid account (the code hides Work on a free trial)
items.note: The mode button is shown only when the plan allows AGI Work.

items.where: Work history (command palette "Work history", or the "Work history" link on the home screen when there are many runs)
steps: Press Command plus K and choose "Work history", or go to the home screen and click "Work history" if it appears.
Click the filter "Active".
Check that running work tasks show their live status.
Click "All" and check that finished tasks also appear.
items.needs: none (a work task helps)
items.note: The home link appears only above a set number of runs.

items.where: Work history > a task row
steps: Open "Work history" and click a task.
Check the "Task details" panel for the status, the "Task goal" and the "Task plan".
Look for any pending decision or approval on the panel.
Compare with Expected: status, step-by-step activity, outputs and pending decision.
items.needs: a work task
items.note: The outputs section was not confirmed in the detail panel file read.

items.where: Work history > filter "Needs you"
steps: Open "Work history" and click the filter "Needs you".
Check the tasks waiting for a decision and their approval cards.
Click the approve or deny button on one card.
Check that the card updates to show the decision.
items.needs: a work task that is waiting for approval
items.note: There is no separate approvals inbox; pending approvals are gathered under the "Needs you" filter.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
Click "Create a task" (or "New task") and fill in and save a schedule.
On a schedule card, use the menu item "Run now", then "Pause" or "Resume".
Click the edit control ("Edit Schedule") and the "Delete" menu item, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Status filters include Active, Paused, Completed, Failed and Expired.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > a schedule card > Run History
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
On a schedule card click the "Run History" button to expand its run history.
Click "Edit Schedule" to see the prompt and cadence.
Compare with Expected: prompt, cadence, next run and run history.
items.needs: a schedule that has run at least once
items.note: There is no separate routine page; the configuration is seen on the card and in the edit dialog. Next run display was not confirmed in the files read.

items.where: Sidebar > Code (surface switch: "Home" / "Code") > New
steps: Click "Code" in the sidebar switch.
Look for the "Cloud sessions" list.
Click "New" and choose a repository with "Select repository".
Click "Start the task" and check that a new session starts.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The page says Code is on paid plans.

items.where: Sidebar > Code > Cloud sessions > a session
steps: Click "Code" in the sidebar switch and open a session in the "Cloud sessions" list.
Check the session transcript.
Click "Changes" to see the file changes and the diff.
Look for a message box to send the next instruction and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Code session that has run
items.note: The message box label used for steering a running session was not confirmed in the files read.

items.where: Settings > Account > Linked devices
steps: Open the account menu, choose "Settings", then "Account".
Scroll to "Linked devices" and read each device's status.
Click "Rename", type a new name, click "Save", and check the new name.
Click "Unlink" and confirm "Unlink device"; check that the device leaves the list.
items.needs: at least one linked device
items.note: No pairing control was found in this web panel, although Expected lists pair.

items.where: Sidebar > Library
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Look at the filter tabs "All", "Images", "Videos", "Documents", "Artifacts", "Uploads", "Generated files".
Choose a file and open its menu or "Download" action.
Compare with Expected: files, images, videos, documents and artifacts, with filters and open or download.
items.needs: some uploaded or generated files
a second account in the same workspace
items.note: Found only the workspace console page "Sharing" (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx), which lists what the workspace shares, not what others share with the user. Shared projects show the label "Shared with you" on the project page (apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx). No list of items shared with the user was found.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Artifacts
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the filter "Artifacts".
Click one artifact to open it.
Compare with Expected: a gallery of generated artifacts that opens any one of them.
items.needs: at least one artifact
items.note: The old address /chat/artifacts redirects to the Library Artifacts filter.

items.where: A chat > artifact side panel > more menu (...) > Edit source
steps: Open a chat that produced a text document artifact and open it in the side panel.
Open the more menu and click "Edit source".
Change the text, then click "Save" (tooltip "Save as a new version").
Open the version history and check that a new version exists with the change.
items.needs: a chat with a text document artifact
items.note: "Edit source" appears only for some artifacts and not while a preview is shown.

items.where: Chat > the + button in the composer > Generate image (no separate studio page)
steps: Click Chat in the left rail to open a new chat.
Click the + button in the composer and choose Generate image.
Look for the Image chip in the composer, then open the aspect ratio control (Select aspect ratio) and the Add a style to the prompt control.

Type a description and send. Compare with Expected: the picture should appear in the chat. There is no studio page with prompt, style, size and history in one place; /chat/images only redirects to Library > Images.
items.needs: a signed-in account; image generation may depend on plan (not verified)
items.note: No dedicated image studio found: searched apps/web and packages/ui for 'image studio' and the image routes; apps/web/app/chat/images/page.tsx redirects to /chat/library?tab=images. The + button's own label was not found.

items.where: Library > Images
steps: Click Library in the left rail.
Click the Images tab.
Hover an image and look for its download control and any Remix action in its row menu (Remix shows only where the host supports it).
Check that generated and uploaded images both appear here, and compare with Expected: open, download and remix actions.
items.needs: a few generated or uploaded images in the account
items.note: Remix appears only when the host provides remixItem (LibraryView.tsx:701 and :294); the row-menu text was not located as a literal.

items.where: Library > Generations (section above the tabs)
steps: Click Library in the left rail.
Look for the Generations heading above the tabs.
Check the status words on each job: Queued, Generating, Failed, Done, Cancelled.
Open a finished job and see whether it links to its result, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: at least one image or video generation job in the account
items.note: Whether a job links to its result was not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Projects > (open a project) > Sources
steps: Click Projects in the left rail and open a project.
Click the Sources tab.
Click Add sources, add a text note or a file, and check it is listed.
Look at the Studio tiles (Briefing doc, Study guide and others) and compare with Expected: the sources are the notebook, and the outputs appear from them.
items.needs: a project; a file to upload (optional)
items.note: Studio tiles start a chat that makes the output; no separate reader or annotation view was found for sources.

items.where: Chat > a conversation with research sources > Open sources panel (title Research sources) > Library tab
steps: Open a conversation that ran Deep Research.
Hover the sources button; its title is Research sources, and click it to open the panel.
Click the Library tab, then open a report.
Check the report's sections (Report tab) and cited sources, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a conversation that has run Deep Research
items.note: The Library tab renders ResearchReportsGallery with a Load older reports control; the panel opens from the chat toolbar, not the rail.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Customize > Skills
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings.
Under Customize, click Skills.
Click New skill, fill in the editor, and click Create skill.
Check the list for installed and available skills and their controls, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account; skills may be limited by plan
items.note: Install, enable, disable and remove controls for skills were not found as literal labels; the account menu trigger was not traced.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Customize > Plugins
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Customize > Plugins.
Compare the installed and available plugin lists.
Click Install on an available plugin.
Open a plugin's remove action and look for the Remove plugin? confirmation, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Configure and Update controls were not found as literal labels.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Customize > Connectors
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Connectors under Customize.
Look at the Connected tab and the list of services.
Click Connect on one service, then Reconnect or Disconnect on a connected one (Disconnect asks to confirm).
Compare with Expected: the list should update to the new state.
items.needs: an outside account for the service to connect
items.note: Labels come from the shared SettingsModal; the web adapter path was not run.

items.where: Composer model picker (Models panel) and Settings > General > Preferences > Default model
steps: Open a new chat and open the model control in the composer.
Look for the Models panel with Search models, Context ceiling and Capabilities for each model.
Pick a model, then open Settings > General.
Under Preferences, check the Default model row, choose a model, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The composer model control's own label was not located; find it by the current model name.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Usage
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Usage.
Read Plan usage limits and Credit balances, and check the Resets section.
Scroll to Monthly spend limit and check its figure.
Scroll to Where your usage went, switch between By day, By week and By month, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with some usage
items.note: Plan usage limits heading shows an upgrade title on Free plans instead.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Billing
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Billing.
Check the plan name, Renews on date and the Payment section.
Check the Invoices table, then click Adjust plan (or Upgrade plan on Free) and look at the options.
Click Manage billing and compare with Expected (in Electron it opens outside the app).
items.needs: a paid account for the plan and invoice views (test checkout per the product note)
items.note: No separate cancel control was found; cancelling appears to go through Manage billing. The plan says this path is unfinished.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > General
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then General.
Under Profile, change Full name.
Scroll to Preferences and change Default model or Display Language.
Leave the screen, come back, and check the change was kept, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No Save control label was checked; appearance, personalization and notifications are separate panes.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace (then the workspace console: Members, Roles, Policy)
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Workspace.
Follow the link to the workspace console and look at Overview, Members, Roles, Identity and Policy.
On Members or Roles, check invitations and seats, and invite a second account.
Compare with Expected: an admin can manage members, roles, invitations and policy.
items.needs: an admin or owner account; a second account to invite
items.note: Non-admin users may see a different view; not checked.

items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The page exists at /developers (apps/web/app/developers/page.tsx, heading Developer console in apps/web/features/developers/components/DeveloperConsolePage.tsx) with API keys (apps/web/features/settings/components/Settings/ApiKeys.tsx). Searched for links to /developers and the navDeveloperConsole string in the signed-in nav, Settings and Account menu: none found, so no UI path was confirmed.

items.where: Account menu > Get help > Send feedback; Settings > Help
steps: Open the account menu and hover Get help.
Click Send feedback and choose a feedback type in the dialog, then send.
Open Settings > Help and check the links: Documentation, Help center, Contact support, Report a bug, Release notes, System status, Legal.
Compare with Expected: help links and a feedback path should both be there.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The account menu trigger was not traced; the Send feedback dialog's own opener was not traced beyond the menu item.

items.where: Open any chat that has messages, then look at the top bar (Share button and chevron menu at the top right)
steps: Sign in and click Chat in the left sidebar, then open a chat from Recents (or send a first message).
Look at the top bar of the chat page.
Click the Share button, then the chevron menu next to it, and check that the menu offers rename, move, share, print, export, branch and delete.
Compare with Expected: the top bar should show where you are and the main actions for this view.
items.needs: a chat that already has messages
items.note: The chat title is written in a screen-reader-only heading in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; I did not confirm a visible title text in the top bar.

items.where: Sidebar > Chat, Projects, Library, Sites, Health, Study (nav rows); and the Home | Code switch above the chat list
steps: Sign in; the left sidebar shows the nav rows.
Click Projects, then Library, then Sites, and watch the main area change.
Find the two-part switch with Home and Code (shown only when the Code option is enabled for the account) and click Code.
Compare with Expected: each click should move to that product area or mode.
items.needs: none (Health appears only when a health space is available; Home | Code only when Code is enabled)
items.note: The nav list is defined in apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts; Health is hidden unless requiresHealthSpace is met.

items.where: Sidebar bottom > account button (Account menu for your name) > Workspace > Personal / Enterprise
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Hover or click Workspace.
Look at the list: Personal (detail Only you) and any Enterprise workspaces; the active one is marked with a check icon.
Click a different workspace, read the switch warning, and check that the app reloads in that workspace (Expected).
items.needs: a second workspace (a team/enterprise membership) for switching; a Free account shows only Personal
items.note: The active workspace is not shown on the sidebar itself in the code I read; it appears only inside the Workspace submenu.

items.where: Sidebar header > Toggle sidebar button (keyboard: Cmd+B on Mac, Ctrl+B on Windows)
steps: Sign in on a wide window so the sidebar is open.
Click the Toggle sidebar button in the sidebar header (or press Cmd+B).
Check that the sidebar collapses to a narrow icon rail.
Click the same button again (or press Cmd+B) and check that the sidebar expands.
items.needs: a wide window (desktop width); on a phone the sidebar is a drawer instead

items.where: Sidebar > Search (row with a Search icon, shortcut shown as Cmd+Shift+F, or Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows)
steps: Click Search in the sidebar, or press Cmd+Shift+F.
A search panel opens over the app.
Type part of a chat title that you know exists.
Compare with Expected: matching conversations should appear as results and open when clicked.
items.needs: at least one saved chat with a known title
items.note: The sidebar search entry opens a search dialog (GlobalSearchDialog); it does not filter the sidebar list in place.

items.where: Sidebar > New Chat button at the top of the sidebar (shortcut Shift+Cmd+O, or Shift+Ctrl+O on Windows)
steps: From any page in the app, click New Chat at the top of the sidebar, or press Shift+Cmd+O.
Check that a blank chat opens with an empty message box.
Send a message, then click New Chat again and check that a second, fresh chat opens.
items.needs: none

items.where: Sidebar > Pinned (section at the top of the chat list)
steps: Hover a chat row in Recents and click its More options (three dots) button.
Click Pin.
Check that the chat moves into a section headed Pinned at the top of the list.
Click Unpin in the same menu and check that it returns to its date group.
items.needs: at least one saved chat

items.where: Sidebar > Recents (heading above the chat list)
steps: Create two or more chats by sending a message in each.
Look at the list under the Recents heading.
Click an older chat and check that it opens with its messages.
Compare with Expected: recent conversations are listed and open on selection.
items.needs: at least two saved chats

items.where: Sidebar > Recents heading > Organize chats (sliders icon) > By project or In one list
steps: Move a chat into a project: hover the chat, click More options, then Move to project, and pick a project.
Hover the Recents heading and click the sliders icon named Organize chats.
With By project selected (the default), check that the moved chat appears under its project row and not in Recents.
Choose In one list and check that all chats appear in Recents again.
items.needs: a project with at least one chat moved into it

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > date group headings
steps: Have chats from different days (or use an account with older chats).
Look at the group headings above the chat rows.
Click a heading to collapse or expand its group.
Compare with Expected: the headings should be Today, Yesterday, This week, Older.
items.needs: chats from several different dates
items.note: Expected says This week, but the code labels are Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days and Older; groups with no chats are not shown.

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > a chat row (click the title)
steps: Click a chat row in Recents.
Check that the chat opens in the main area with its title and messages.
Check that the row you clicked now has a highlighted background (it is marked as the current page).
Click a different row and check that the highlight moves.
items.needs: at least two saved chats

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > a project name
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar nav, then New project and create one.
Go back to the sidebar and find the project under the Projects section.
Click the project name and check that the project page opens (address /chat/projects/ with the project id).
Hover the project row and check the New chat in project and More options buttons.
items.needs: a project (create one first)
items.note: The Projects section in the sidebar appears only once the account has at least one project.

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > a row marked Work (a small dot with the word Work for screen readers)
steps: Find a row in Recents that carries the Work marker (a small dot, no chat-style row).
Click the row and check that it opens the task.
Compare with Expected: the row should be visibly different from a plain chat and show its state.
For the full task list, open the command palette (Cmd+K) and choose Work history.
items.needs: a Work task that already exists (how to start one was not confirmed in the code I read)
items.note: The Work marker is a small dot (session.agiWork), not a separate label; how a Work task is started was not traced.

items.where: Press Cmd+K > type a word > results show an icon and a type label for each row
steps: Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows).
Type a word from a chat title and from a project name.
Look at each result row: it has an icon and a hidden type label (Chat, Project, File, Artifact and so on).
Compare with Expected: the type should be recognisable from the icon and announced for screen readers.
items.needs: a chat and a project whose names match a word you type
items.note: The icons are in the command palette; sidebar rows use a dot and a screen-reader word instead.

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > the chat row whose reply is still running
steps: Send a question that takes a while to answer in a chat.
While the reply is still coming in, look at the chat row in Recents.
Check that a pulsing dot appears beside the title.
When the reply finishes, check that the dot disappears.
items.needs: an account that can send a message and get a reply

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > a chat row with an amber dot
steps: Start a run that asks you for approval or input (for example, a task that waits for you).
Leave the chat open or move to another chat.
Look at the chat row in Recents for an amber dot, and hover or inspect it for the word Needs you for screen readers.
Answer the question and check that the amber dot clears.
items.needs: a run that is waiting for your approval or input
items.note: The flag comes from server state (apps/web/lib/server/neon-chat.ts); there is no button that creates it, so the tester must trigger a run that waits.

items.where: Sidebar > Recents > chat row with a blue dot and bold title (set Mark as unread from More options)
steps: Hover a chat row in Recents, click More options, then Mark as unread.
Check that the row shows a blue dot and a bold title, and that the screen-reader text says Unread.
Click the row and check that the dot and bold title clear.
Compare with Expected: unread items are marked and clear when opened.
items.needs: at least one saved chat
items.note: I did not trace the code that clears the unread flag on open; the tester can confirm it by clicking.

items.where: Sidebar > hover a chat row > More options (three dots)
steps: Hover a chat row in Recents and click More options.
Check the menu order: Share, Rename, Pin, Mark as unread, Archive, Delete, Move to project.
Use Move to project (when projects exist) and check that the chat moves.
Use Delete and check that a confirmation dialog appears before anything is removed.
items.needs: at least one saved chat; a project for Move to project
items.note: Share and Move to project appear only when the matching action is provided; the list in Expected matches the code.

items.where: Sidebar > chat row > More options > Rename
steps: Hover a chat row, click More options, then Rename.
The title turns into a text field: type a new name and press Enter.
Check that the new title shows in the row, then reload the page and check it is still there.
Start a rename again, press Escape, and check that the old title comes back.
items.needs: at least one saved chat
items.note: Clicking away from the field also saves the new title (blur calls submitRename), which Expected does not mention.

items.where: Menu bar > History > Back and Forward (desktop app only; in the browser use the browser's back and forward buttons)
steps: Open two different chats, one after the other.
In the Electron desktop app, click History in the menu bar, then Back (shortcut Cmd+[).
Check that the earlier chat opens again.
Click History > Forward (Cmd+]) and check that the later chat returns.
items.needs: the Electron desktop app for the menu; a browser for the browser's own back button

items.where: Press Cmd+K anywhere (Ctrl+K on Windows) > command palette
steps: Press Cmd+K from any page.
Check that a dialog opens with the placeholder Search chats and actions.
Type settings and press Enter on Go to Settings.
Compare with Expected: the palette runs the command and opens that destination.
items.needs: none
items.note: The palette is opened by the capture-phase listener in apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPaletteProvider.tsx.

items.where: Account menu (bottom of sidebar) > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts (or press Cmd+/)
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar, then Get help, then Keyboard shortcuts.
Or press Cmd+/ (Ctrl+/ on Windows) from a chat page.
Check that a dialog titled Keyboard Shortcuts opens and lists the shortcuts with their keys.
Press Escape and check that the dialog closes.
items.needs: none

items.where: Sidebar top, next to the AGI wordmark > bell button (Notifications)
steps: Click the bell at the top of the sidebar.
Check the panel titled Notifications, with an unread count on the bell when there are unread items.
Click a notification row and check that it opens its target.
Click Mark all as read and check the unread dots clear and the count goes away.
items.needs: a notification (for example a finished run); an empty account shows the empty message
items.note: The empty-state text is: When a run finishes, a report is ready or something needs you, it shows up here.

items.where: Sidebar bottom > account button (Account menu for your name)
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Check that your email shows at the top of the menu.
Check the items: Workspace, Settings, Get help, Upgrade (only when offered), Log out.
Click Settings and check that the Settings page opens; then sign out with Log out and check you return to sign-in.
items.needs: none
items.note: The account menu is defined in apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx; the plan is shown as a badge on the footer, and Free accounts see a Free plan line with Upgrade.

items.where: Account menu (bottom of sidebar) > Get help
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar, then Get help.
Check the options: Get help, Email support, Send feedback, Keyboard shortcuts.
Click Send feedback and check that the feedback dialog opens.
Click Keyboard shortcuts and check that the shortcuts dialog opens.
items.needs: none
items.note: Learn more, Data use, Data rights and Terms and policies are in a separate Learn more submenu of the same account menu.

items.where: Sidebar account footer > "Free plan" row > Upgrade button; or the account menu ("Account menu for ..." in the sidebar) > Upgrade
steps: Sign in with a Free account and look at the bottom of the sidebar for the "Free plan" row.
Click the "Upgrade" button on that row.
Open the account menu from the sidebar and look for the "Upgrade" item (it is hidden when the plan has no self-serve upgrade path).

Click "Upgrade" and compare with Expected: an eligible user should reach the plan upgrade flow. Note that paid checkout is gated: while billing upgrades are closed, the flow shows the waitlist dialog instead of checkout.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: Code is partial: the owner-held billing waitlist (AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN, billing-waitlist-access.ts) decides whether Upgrade reaches checkout or the waitlist dialog, so the tester may see the waitlist instead of a plan flow.

items.where: Any screen > the status strip that drops in below the header (labelled "Network status indicator"); it appears on connection loss or a sync error, with no menu
steps: Sign in and stay on any screen.
Turn off Wi-Fi on the Mac (or disconnect the network) and wait a few seconds.
Look for the status strip under the header: it should show a connection state such as "Offline".
Check whether a reconnect control is offered; compare with Expected (it should offer reconnect when not connected).
items.needs: a Mac with Wi-Fi that can be switched off, and a signed-in account
items.note: The Retry button appears only in the error state (after a sync error), not while offline, so there is no reconnect control when the network is down; the code does not show a separate backend-connection indicator.

items.where: Any screen > turn off Wi-Fi; the status strip under the header appears; turn Wi-Fi back on
steps: Sign in and stay on any screen.
Turn off Wi-Fi on the Mac.
Look for the strip under the header showing "Offline" (with "pending" if changes are queued).
Turn Wi-Fi back on and wait; compare with Expected: the strip should clear once the app is back online.
items.needs: a Mac with Wi-Fi that can be switched off, and a signed-in account; queued items show "pending" only if some work is waiting
items.note: When back online the strip hides unless items are queued or syncing, so it clears rather than showing an "Online" message.

items.where: Menu bar > the app's own menu (the menu named after the app, far left, next to the Apple menu) > Check for Updates…
steps: Click the app's own menu in the Mac menu bar.
Click "Check for Updates…".
Read the dialog: if you have the latest version it says the app is up to date; if a newer one exists it offers "Download Installer" (or "Relaunch to update" once downloaded).
Compare with Expected: the dialog should say whether a new release is available and how to get it.
items.needs: a Mac desktop build; to see the update-available or update-ready dialog a newer published version must exist (otherwise only the up-to-date dialog appears)
items.note: The in-app check also exists as "Check for updates" in the Settings update row (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopUpdateRow.tsx) and a "Relaunch to update" banner (DesktopUpdateNotice.tsx); the Settings tab that holds that row was not confirmed.

items.where: Resize the app window narrower than 768 px > header button at top-left labelled "Open navigation" > navigation drawer slides in from the left
steps: Drag the window edge until the window is narrower than about 768 px wide.
Click the menu icon at the top-left of the header (accessible name "Open navigation").
Look for the navigation drawer sliding in from the left, with the sidebar items inside.
Press Escape or click outside the drawer, then check it closes and keyboard focus returns to the menu button; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a window narrower than 768 px
items.note: The header button is an icon with an aria-label, so no visible word is shown on it; the code path is the compact tier (app-shell-layout.ts, SHELL_TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = 768).

items.where: Resize the window to a width from 768 px to 1023 px; the sidebar layout is chosen by width and orientation (no control)
steps: Resize the window to between 768 and 1023 px wide with the window wider than tall (landscape).
Look: the navigation sidebar should stay beside the content (persistent).
Resize to a taller-than-wide (portrait) window at the same width.
Look: in portrait the sidebar shows only icons and expands over the content instead of sitting beside it; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a window that can be resized to tablet widths
items.note: Code (app-shell-layout.ts) keeps the sidebar persistent in landscape but uses a rail that expands over the content in portrait, which is not the side-by-side layout Expected describes.

items.where: Sidebar > the bell icon next to the wordmark (notifications) > click a notification about a chat, project or task
steps: Make sure an account has a notification that points at a chat or a task.
Open the notifications bell from the sidebar header.
Click that notification.
Look: the app should open that chat or task directly, and the address should point at the item; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a notification that links to a chat or task
items.note: Stable links use the path /open/<type>/<id> (packages/contracts/types/src/product-links.ts), and the desktop deep-link scheme is agiworkforce-cloud (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts); the bell's visible label was not confirmed, so the tester should locate it by icon.

items.where: Open a chat link whose chat was deleted (for example from a notification about it): the screen shows "Conversation not found"; the "Loading chat" screen appears while the chat resolves
steps: Delete a chat you own, or pick a link to a chat that no longer exists.
Open that link from the app (for example from a notification).
Look for the "Loading chat" screen while it resolves.
Look for the unavailable screen: a title such as "This chat isn’t available" with a "Back to chats" button; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free or paid account and a chat you can delete
items.note: The loading screen is brief, so capture it on a slow connection; the unavailable copy also varies by reason (deleted, no access, not found).

steps: Open Settings… from the Mac menu bar (AGI app menu) or press Cmd+,.
Go to Appearance and click Light, then Dark, then System under Theme.
Compare the page and panel backgrounds in each theme with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Colour tokens are defined in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; the effect is seen by switching Theme.

steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark.
Compare cards, menus and dialogs with the page background in each theme; open a menu or the Settings dialog itself to see the raised surface.
items.needs: none
items.note: Raised-surface token is set in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; no visible control of its own.

steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Switch Theme to Light, then Dark.
Read primary and muted text in chat and settings in each theme and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Text tokens are in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; contrast is verified by apps/web/shared/components/__tests__/theme-contrast.test.ts, not by a person.

steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark.
Look at card edges, dividers and input borders in Settings > General and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Subtle and strong border tokens are in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; no separate control.

items.where: Settings… (Cmd+,) > Appearance > Accent colour
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Click a colour under Accent colour (AGI amber, Green, Blue, Violet or Rose).
Look at selected controls and buttons, and check the text on them is readable, against Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Fill, text and on-fill roles are in CSS tokens; the swatch names come from apps/web/content/support/chat-basics.md.

steps: Trigger a status message, for example a failed or warning state, in the chat or settings.
Compare the success, warning, error or info text colour in Light and Dark Theme.
items.needs: none
items.note: Status colours are tokens in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; no single visible control, so the tester must find a screen that shows a status.

items.where: Settings… (Cmd+,) > Appearance > Chat font
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Click Chat font and pick Sans, Serif or Dyslexic friendly.
Look at message text in a chat; code should stay monospace.
items.needs: none
items.note: Font families are declared in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/chat.css and apps/web/app/globals.css.

steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Compare the page title Appearance with the row labels such as Theme and Motion.
items.needs: none
items.note: The heading scale is in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/tailwind.css; no control of its own.

items.where: Settings… (Cmd+,) > Appearance > Chat text size
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Choose Small, then Large under Chat text size.
Look at chat message text and compare with Default and Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Default is shown as Default in the options list.

steps: Open a chat and look at small metadata text such as timestamps or hint text under a Settings row, for example the hint under Contrast.
items.needs: none
items.note: The caption role is defined in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/tailwind.css; no single control of its own.

items.where: Settings… (Cmd+,) > Appearance > Chat font
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Set Chat font to Serif, then return to Default.
Open a chat with a code block and compare the code text with the body text.
items.needs: a chat that contains a code block
items.note: Monospace family is declared in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/chat.css; the support page says code stays monospace.

steps: Read a multi-line chat reply and compare line spacing between lines of the same paragraph and in headings.
items.needs: a chat reply with several lines
items.note: Line-height is set per text role in apps/web/app/globals.css; no control of its own.

steps: Ask for a reply with several paragraphs in a chat.
Look at the vertical gap between paragraphs and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a chat reply with several paragraphs
items.note: Paragraph gap is set in apps/web/app/globals.css; no control of its own.

steps: Ask for a reply containing a bulleted or numbered list, with a nested item.
Look at the indent of the list and the nested list.
items.needs: a chat reply with a list
items.note: List indentation is set in apps/web/app/globals.css; no control of its own.

items.where: Settings… (Cmd+,) > Appearance > Wrap long code lines
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Turn on Wrap long code lines, then turn it off.
Open a chat with a long code line and look at the code block padding and whether the line wraps.
items.needs: a chat that contains a code block with a long line
items.note: Padding itself is set in apps/web/app/globals.css; the toggle only changes wrapping.

steps: Open a chat reply or a data table that contains a table.
Compare the padding inside table cells.
items.needs: a chat reply with a table
items.note: Table-cell padding is applied in the shared layout rules; no control of its own.

steps: Send two or more messages in one chat.
Look at the vertical space between one turn and the next.
items.needs: a chat with several turns
items.note: Turn spacing is set in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx; no control of its own.

steps: Hover over a chat message to show its action toolbar.
Look at the distance between the message and its toolbar.
items.needs: a chat with a reply
items.note: Spacing is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/messageActionRow.ts; the toolbar appears on hover.

steps: Open a chat and click into the message box at the bottom.
Look at the space around the typed text and the send and attach controls.
items.needs: none
items.note: Composer padding is in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx; no control of its own.

steps: Open a chat page and resize the window width from wide to narrow.
