items.where: Chat > a reply with thinking steps > the button Thinking process (N steps) under the reply
steps: Open a chat whose reply includes thinking steps.
Click Thinking process under the reply.
Look for the list of thinking steps to open and the arrow to turn down.
Click again and check the list closes.
items.needs: a model that returns thinking steps
items.note: The button is shown only when the reply has thinking steps.

items.where: Chat > click the conversation title at the top (aria-label Conversation options) > menu items Rename, Add chat instructions
steps: Open any saved chat.
Click the chat title at the top with its small down arrow.
Look for a menu with Rename and Add chat instructions or Edit chat instructions.
Press the down arrow key, then Escape, and check the menu closes and focus returns to the title.
items.needs: a saved chat
items.note: Add chat instructions appears only when the onEditInstructions handler is passed.

items.where: Chat > click the conversation title > Move to project (opens a submenu of projects)
steps: Open a saved chat and click its title to open the menu.
Hover or click Move to project.
Look for a submenu listing your projects.
Click a project name and check the chat moves into it (the item changes to Change project).
items.needs: at least one project
items.note: The item is hidden when there are no projects.

items.where: Chat > hover over the pencil icon (aria-label Edit message) under one of your sent messages
steps: Open a chat and find one of your sent messages.
Move the mouse onto the pencil icon under it, or focus it with the keyboard.
Look for a small label Edit to appear.
Move the mouse away and check the label goes away.
items.needs: a sent message in a chat

items.where: Chat > composer Files menu (trigger aria-label Files) > panel with Search library files and Upload from device
steps: Open a chat and click the composer Files button.
Look for a floating panel above the composer with a search field and Upload from device.
Press Escape, and check the panel closes.
Open it again, click outside it, and check it closes.
items.needs: none
items.note: The visible text of the trigger button was not found; only its aria-label Files was located.

items.where: Chat > an answer with web citations > hover a small source chip under the answer
steps: Open a chat with a web-search answer that shows source chips.
Hover over a source chip.
Look for a card listing the source rows with the site name and a snippet.
Move the mouse away and check the card closes.
items.needs: an answer with web citations
items.note: The chip's aria-label is a template; the visible chip text was not found in code.

items.where: Chat > Research sources button (Globe icon) > count badge when sources exist and the panel is closed
steps: Open a chat with research sources and keep the sources panel closed.
Look at the Globe button in the top bar.
Check for a small count bubble on its corner.
Open the panel and check the bubble disappears.
items.needs: a chat with research sources
items.note: The badge count is code-driven; I did not locate other badges in the StepsCard header.

items.needs: a chat with a calculation answer
items.note: CalculationCard renders the unit as a Badge with dynamic text (apps/web/features/chat/components/cards/CalculationCard.tsx line 169-177), with no fixed visible label. I could not confirm this is a distinct tag rather than a status badge.

items.where: Chat transcript: your messages sit in a bubble, assistant replies are plain text; screen readers hear You said: and Assistant said:
steps: Open a chat with one message from you and one reply.
Look for the two messages to look different (your message in a bubble, the reply as plain text).
Turn on VoiceOver and move through the two messages; check each is announced with You said: or Assistant said:.
items.needs: a screen reader for the accessible-label step
items.note: apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx says the web chat shows no avatars, so the distinction is by layout and the hidden heading, not a picture.

items.where: Chat > a steps card > progress bar and percent text under its title; the loading spinner appears when a chat opens
steps: Open a chat that returns a steps card.
Tick off steps and watch the progress bar and the text N% complete.
Check the text changes to All steps completed! when all are done.
Open a chat and watch for the loading spinner labelled Loading chat.
items.needs: a steps card in a chat
items.note: The steps card depends on model output; the loading spinner shows only briefly.

items.where: Chat > open a conversation on a slow connection; grey placeholder message bubbles show before the messages load
steps: Throttle the network in the browser developer tools if available, or use a slow connection.
Open a saved chat.
Look for grey animated placeholder message bubbles before the real messages appear.
Check the placeholders are replaced by the real messages.
items.needs: a saved chat and a slow connection
items.note: Placeholder text is not visible; the skeleton component is apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubbleSkeleton.tsx. Visibility is brief.

items.where: Chat > composer model picker > choose another model while the save fails (toast at the bottom)
steps: Open a chat and turn off the network connection.
Open the model picker in the composer and choose a different model.
Look for the error toast with the message about the model not being saved.
Wait a few seconds and check the toast goes away on its own.
items.needs: a way to make the save fail (network off)

labels.text: Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.

items.note: The toast shows only when the model save fails; the desktop copy is Could not save this conversation’s model. Try again. in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.

items.where: Chat > a turn that fails shows an inline alert in the transcript with a recovery action
steps: Open a chat and send a message while the network is off.
Look for a red alert block in the conversation with an explanation.
Check that the alert offers a recovery action where one applies (for example a retry link).
items.needs: a way to make a turn fail (network off)

labels.text: Couldn't load this conversation. Check your connection and try again.

items.note: The exact alert text depends on the failure; the alert role is set on TranscriptNotice in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx near line 6888 and the banner at line 7556.

items.where: Chat > send a long message > the strip at the top of the chat: Get notified when the response is ready. with Enable
steps: Open a chat in a browser that has not granted notifications.
Send a message that takes a while to answer.
Look for the strip Get notified when the response is ready. with an Enable button.
Click Enable or the dismiss control and check the strip reacts.
items.needs: a long reply and notification permission not yet granted

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

items.note: The dismiss button text was not located.

items.where: Projects > the Projects list at the bottom > Show more
steps: Open Projects from the sidebar.
Scroll to the bottom of the list.
Click Show more.
Look for the Loading projects text while loading, then more projects appear.
items.needs: an account with more projects than one page
items.note: Sidebar label for the Projects entry was not verified.

items.where: Chat > Artifacts panel with no artifacts yet
steps: Open a chat with no artifacts.
Open the Artifacts panel.
Look for the empty message No artifacts yet with the line Renderable code and generated files will appear here.
items.needs: an account or chat with no artifacts
items.note: The control that opens the Artifacts panel was not located.

items.where: Projects > the Projects list fails to load > Retry
steps: Open Projects while the network is off or the list cannot load.
Look for the error message and the Retry button.
Turn the network back on, click Retry, and check the list loads.
items.needs: a way to make the list fail (network off)
items.note: Chat-level error text is Couldn't load this conversation. Check your connection and try again. (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx).
Not in range; ignore.

items.where: Chat composer > Work mode > "Files" in the work bar above the message box > "Search library files"
steps: Turn on Work mode from the composer mode choice labelled "Work".
Click "Files" in the work bar under the message box.
Type part of a file name in the box "Search library files".
Look: the list shows only files whose names match what you typed, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with Work available (not a Free trial) and at least two library files
items.note: The Files menu is also reachable from the plus button, which offers "Add photos & files"; the search box only appears in the Files menu.

items.where: Chat composer, bottom row > the model name button (screen-reader name ends "Change model") > "Models" list > "Search models"
steps: Open a new chat.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box.
Type a model name in "Search models" and click a different model.
Look: the model name on the button changes to the one you picked, compared with Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat composer > plus button (screen-reader name "More composer options") > "Deep Research" > "Research plan" panel > "Add a source"
steps: Click the plus button and choose "Deep Research".
Send a research question so the "Research plan" panel opens.
In "Add a source" pick a kind: "Only this site", "Never this site", "My files" or "Connected app", type or choose a value, then click "Add".
Look: the chip list "Sources for this run" shows the added source, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with Deep Research; a connected app for the Connected app option
items.note: The source choice is part of the research run plan, not a picker on the first screen of a normal chat.

items.needs: a connector with two linked accounts
items.note: Searched for account pickers ("Choose account", "Select account", "accounts.map", "Connected account") under apps/web/features and packages/ui. Found only a read-only list of accounts, "Connected account" heading, in apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx, with no control to pick one.

items.where: Account menu for your name (sidebar) > "Workspace" > "Personal" or a team workspace name
steps: Open the account menu from the sidebar.
Hover or click "Workspace".
Look at the list: "Personal" and any team workspaces.
Click a different workspace; a confirmation may appear, then check the active workspace changed, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a team workspace on the account
items.note: The account button's screen-reader name is "Account menu for <name>" in apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx.

items.where: Chat composer > "Project" in the work bar (reads "Project or folder" in Work mode) > "Search projects..."
steps: Turn on Work mode in the composer.
Click "Project" in the work bar under the message box.
Type a project name in "Search projects...".
Click a project and look: the button shows that project name, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with Work available and at least one project

items.where: Code (sidebar) > composer > "Select repository" chip > "Search repositories" or the URL box
steps: Open Code from the sidebar.
Click the "Select repository" chip.
Type in "Search repositories" to narrow the list, or type a URL such as the placeholder "https://github.com/owner/repository".
Click a repository and look: the chip shows its name, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a connected GitHub account with repositories, or a public repository URL

items.where: Code (sidebar) > choose a repository > branch chip (screen-reader name "Change the branch") > "Search or type a branch name"
steps: Choose a repository in Code.
Click the branch chip.
Look at the "Branches" list, then type in "Search or type a branch name" to filter.
Click another branch and look: the chip shows that branch, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a repository with more than one branch

labels.text: Search or type a branch name

items.where: Chat > "Start voice mode" > "Audio output" button in the voice screen
steps: Click "Start voice mode" in the composer.
Click the "Audio output" button.
Look at the list "Audio output device" with "System default" and any other speakers.
Pick a device and look: the button shows that device, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone and a second audio output device to see a real choice
items.note: Only an audio output picker was found. No microphone or camera picker was found in AudioRoutePicker.tsx or VoiceComposer.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Account > "API keys" > "Generate Key" (scope checkboxes); also chat composer > "Tool approvals" in Work mode
steps: Open Settings > Account and click the "API keys" row.
Click "Generate Key".
Look at the scope list: "Read model catalog", "Run inference", "Read usage", and tick only some of them.
Create the key and look at the key list: it shows only the scopes you ticked, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account; creating a key is only needed to see the result
items.note: Once-versus-always choices are on the approval card: "Allow", "Allow for this chat" and "Deny" in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts. Site automation scope was not found.

items.where: Projects (sidebar) > open a project > the more-options menu > "Share" > "Share <project name>" dialog
steps: Open Projects and open one of your projects.
Open the more-options menu and click "Share".
Look at the dialog: the list "People with access to <project>", each person with a Read, Write or None choice, and the sharing select "Everyone in the workspace can view" or "Only people you invite".
Change one person's access and look: the choice is saved and shown, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a second account in the same workspace
items.note: No search-by-name or email input was found. Only a list of existing members with per-person access choices, so the picker part of Expected is not present.

items.where: Scheduled (sidebar) > "New task" > "Frequency"
steps: Open Scheduled and click "New task".
Fill "Schedule Name" and "Task Instructions".
Open "Frequency" and choose "One Time", "Daily", "Weekly", "Monthly", "Interval", "Custom Cron" or "Recurrence Rule"; the fields below change to match.
Save and look at the schedule row: its cadence matches what you chose, compared with Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Library (sidebar) > "All" tab
steps: Open Library.
Look at the tabs: "All", "Images", "Videos", "Documents", "Artifacts", "Uploads", "Generated files".
Type a name in "Search the library by name".
Click a file and look: it opens in the file viewer ("Close file viewer"), compared with Expected.
items.needs: a few uploaded or generated files

items.where: Settings > Skills (under the Customize group) > open a skill > "Skill files" tree
steps: Open Settings and click "Skills".
Open a skill that has folders.
In the "Skill files" tree, click a folder row to expand it, then click again to collapse it.
Look: the folder opens and closes and the file inside is reached, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a skill with folders in its files

items.where: Chat > open a spreadsheet artifact ("Open artifacts panel") > click a column heading
steps: Ask for a spreadsheet in a chat and open the artifact.
Open the artifacts panel if it is closed.
Click a column heading; its title reads "Sort by <column>". Click again to reverse, then clear.
Look: the rows reorder by that column, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a spreadsheet artifact
items.note: The sort is reached through a title on the heading, so a tester may need to hover to see it.

items.where: Library (sidebar) > "Grid view" button in the toolbar
steps: Open Library.
Click the "Grid view" button in the "Library layout" group.
Look: files and artifacts appear as cards with a preview.
Click "List view" to switch back, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a few library items

items.where: Library (sidebar) > "Images" tab (or "Videos")
steps: Open Library and click the "Images" tab.
Look at the picture tiles in the grid.
Click one picture to open it in the larger viewer.
Look at the enlarged picture, then click "Close file viewer", compared with Expected.
items.needs: at least one image in the library

items.where: Chat in Work mode > run a task > "Agent activity" section
steps: Turn on Work mode and send a task that uses tools.
Look at the "Agent activity" section while it runs.
Check the steps are listed in order, each with its state and a running seconds counter where shown.
Compare with Expected once the run finishes.
items.needs: a paid account with Work available

items.where: Settings > Account > "Recent activity"
steps: Open Settings and click "Account".
Scroll to the bottom to the "Recent activity" panel.
Make a small change elsewhere in settings, then come back.
Look: the newest event is at the top, compared with Expected.
items.needs: an account with some activity

items.where: Work (sidebar) > "Work history" > "Task layout" > "Board"
steps: Open Work from the sidebar to reach "Work history" (or go to /tasks).
Click "Board" in the "Task layout" control.
Look: columns with headings "Queued", "Running", "Needs approval", "Done" (and others with runs) and a count per column.
Click "List" to switch back, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a few work runs in different states
items.note: The sidebar label "Work" comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json; the sidebar entry itself was not traced.

items.where: Gallery page (/gallery) > "Create artifact" > pick a type > "Next" steps
steps: Open /gallery and click "Create artifact".
Look at the step counter text "Step <n> of <total>" and the step dots.
Click "Next" to move forward; the counter and dots advance.
Look: the counter matches the step shown, compared with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: No "Back" control was found in GalleryClient.tsx, so going back is not visible; Expected says it should be.

items.where: New account sign-up > welcome page (/welcome) > "What should we call you?"
steps: Create a new account and reach the welcome page.
Look for "Step 1 of 2" and the "Preferred name" field.
Type a name and continue; check "Step 2 of 2" with "What do you want to do first?".
Finish and check the name appears, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a new account

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

items.note: The wizard has two steps (name, first task). No model or sign-in choice step was found in OnboardingWizard.tsx.

items.where: Chat > "Open artifacts panel" > separator "Resize artifacts panel" between chat and artifact
steps: Open a chat that has an artifact and click "Open artifacts panel".
Drag the separator named "Resize artifacts panel" left or right.
Or click the separator and press the Left or Right arrow key.
Look: the artifact pane gets wider or narrower and the chat pane adjusts, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a desktop-width window and an artifact

items.where: Chat > open an artifact > version counter "Version <n> of <total>" > "Version history"
steps: Open an artifact that has been edited more than once.
Click the version counter (screen-reader name "Version <n> of <total>. Show version history").
Look at the "Version history" panel: each saved version and its count.
Click "Restore version <n>" on an older one and look: the artifact shows that version, compared with Expected.
items.needs: an artifact with at least two versions

items.where: Code > a coding session with file changes > "Changes" in the header
steps: Open a coding session that has changed files.
Click "Changes" in the header; the panel opens.
Use "Filter changed files" if needed and click a file to read its diff.
Look: added and removed lines are marked, compared with Expected. Do not click "Discard" controls.
items.needs: a coding session with uncommitted or committed changes

items.where: Chat > send a question that uses web search > under the answer, click Sources > click a source row
steps: Sign in and ask a question that needs web search, such as a current news topic.
Wait until the answer finishes, then click the Sources button under the answer.
In the research panel, read the Sources tab: each row shows the title, the publisher and date line (with Retrieved date) and a short snippet.
Click a source row; it opens the page in a new tab. Compare with Expected: title, origin, excerpt, and open.
items.needs: a web-search answer (a question that triggers web sources)
items.note: Whether a web-search answer is produced depends on the model and the question; the Sources button only appears when the answer has sources.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings, then click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look at each bar: Current session, This week and, when shown, Most capable models. Each shows a percent used.
Read the reset line under a bar (Resets at ... or a time left until reset) and compare with Expected: percent, window and reset time.
items.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees Upgrade for higher capacity instead)
items.note: The meter is labelled for assistive tech with '<name> usage' and the percent as its value; screen-reader output was not checked.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Usage > Credit balances
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the rows Bonus credits and Purchased credits with their amounts.
Click Buy credits and see that it opens the Billing section. Compare with Expected: balance and an add-credits button in one place.
items.needs: a paid account (the card is hidden on Free plans and on contract-priced accounts)
items.note: The card only appears once the usage data has loaded; the Buy credits button uses the billing settings section.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connector that uses sign-in > Permissions requested
steps: Open Settings, then click Connectors.
Click a connector that asks for sign-in permissions.
Find the Permissions requested box and read each permission sentence with its Read or Write badge.
Click Connect; the dialog Connect <name>? repeats the list with Deny and Allow buttons. Compare with Expected: what the connector may do and whether it is read or write.
items.needs: a connector that uses OAuth permissions; an outside account (for example Google) to finish connecting
items.note: Connectors with no OAuth scopes show a note instead: This provider does not use OAuth scopes.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals > Ask before every action, then in chat send a request that uses a tool
steps: Open Settings, click Capabilities, find the Tool approvals box and choose Ask before every action.
Go to a chat and send a request that makes the assistant use a tool (for example a connected app or site action).
When the action pauses, read the inline line that says the tool requires approval, and the buttons Allow, Allow for this chat and Deny.
Click Deny and check that the run stops; repeat and click Allow and check that the run continues. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a tool that asks for approval (the policy setting above must be on); a paid account may be needed for some tools

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

items.note: Which tools trigger an approval card was not confirmed from the code; Allow for this chat is hidden for high-risk tools.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connector
steps: Open Settings, click Connectors, then click a connector that is not connected.
Read the notice You're not connected to <name> yet. and the Connect button.
Click Connect and finish the sign-in; the button should change to Connected.
Open the remove control for a connected card (Disconnect) and check that the state returns to not connected. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an outside account for the connector (for example Google)
items.note: No Expired word exists in the code; a connection that needs signing in again shows the notice '<name> needs reconnecting' and a Reconnect button (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts).

items.where: Chat > choose a model that cannot read images (model picker under the message box) > attach an image > read the notice above the message box
steps: In a chat, choose a model from the model picker below the message box.
Attach an image file to the message, without sending.
Read the notice above the message box that says the chosen model cannot read images.
Change to a model that reads images and check the notice disappears. Compare with Expected: warning shown before sending.
items.needs: a file to upload (an image); a model that cannot read images in your list

labels.text: cannot read images, so the images in this conversation will be ignored.
Older messages will be left out of the next reply.

items.note: Which models lack image or tool support depends on the live model catalogue, so the tester must pick one from the list; the notice is a visible line, its aria label Model compatibility is not visible.

items.where: Chat > start a task that runs several steps > open the Progress panel at the bottom of the chat
steps: Send a request that makes the assistant run a multi-step task.
While it runs, click the Progress panel at the bottom of the chat.
Read the count (for example 1/4) and the current action line; wait and see them change.
When the task ends, check the final state and the count. Compare with Expected: state, progress and latest action updating.
items.needs: a task that runs several steps (agent or work mode)
items.note: The count only shows when the task has steps; which tasks produce steps depends on the model and request.

items.where: Chat > ask a question the assistant needs to clarify > pick options on the card > Send answers
steps: Ask a vague request that needs a choice, such as planning a trip without a destination.
When a card with options appears in the answer, click one or more options.
Click Send answers and check that the card shows Sending, then that the answer continues using your choice.
items.needs: none
items.note: Showing the card depends on the assistant deciding to ask; other interactive cards (map, answer cards) also render in InteractiveCardBlock.tsx and were not separately tested.

items.where: Sidebar > the bell icon next to the app name > Notifications
steps: Click the bell icon in the sidebar next to the app name.
Read the Notifications list: newest first, unread items in bold with a dot.
Click one unread item; it opens its page and is marked read.
Click Mark all as read and check that the unread marks go away. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: at least one notification (for example a finished scheduled run)
items.note: Unread state is also announced to screen readers with the hidden text ', unread'; the screen-reader output itself was not checked.

items.where: Any signed-in screen > press Command+K (Ctrl+K on Windows or Linux) > type in the box Search chats and actions > press Return
steps: Press Command+K on the Mac keyboard.
Type part of a command or chat name, such as Settings.
Check that the list narrows as you type.
Use the arrow keys and press Return on Go to Settings and check that the app opens Settings.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Return key behaviour was not confirmed in the file; the shortcut is handled as metaKey or ctrlKey plus k in CommandPaletteProvider.tsx.

items.where: Projects page > New project > Create project dialog
steps: Sign in and open the Projects page (apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx).
Click "New project".
In the "Create project" dialog, type a name and click "Create project".
Check that the new project appears in the Projects list, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The sidebar control that opens this page was not confirmed; WebAppShell.tsx has a comment about the New project control, not its label.

items.where: Chat title (Conversation options button) > Rename, or sidebar row > Rename
steps: Open a conversation.
Click the conversation title in the header to open the menu, then click "Rename".
Or hover a row in the sidebar, open its menu and click "Rename".
Type a new title, press Enter, and check the new title is shown in the header and sidebar.
items.needs: a conversation in the account

items.where: Chat title menu > Move to project, or sidebar row > Move to project
steps: Open a conversation that is not in a project.
Open the title menu or the row menu and hover "Move to project".
Click a project name in the submenu.
Check the conversation now shows under that project in the sidebar.
items.needs: at least one project in the account
items.note: The item is shown only when the account has at least one project; once in a project the label reads "Change project".

items.where: Chat title menu > Duplicate as branch
steps: Open a conversation with at least one message.
Open the title menu and click "Duplicate as branch".
Look for the new copy in the sidebar and for any message saying where it is.
Compare with Expected: an independent copy that names its location.
items.needs: a conversation with messages
items.note: The menu wording is "Duplicate as branch", a fork of the chat; no project-duplicate control was found in the menu. I did not confirm the success message.

items.where: Sidebar row > Archive
steps: Hover a conversation in the sidebar and open its menu.
Click "Archive".
Look for the toast "Chat archived" with "Undo" and "View archived".
Compare with Expected: archiving confirms, offers undo and points to archived items.
items.needs: a conversation in the account
items.note: Archive has no confirm dialog; it confirms with the toast. The sidebar archive filter label was not found in the files checked.

items.where: Sidebar row > Delete
steps: Hover a conversation in the sidebar and open its menu.
Click "Delete".
Look for a dialog titled "Delete conversation?" that shows the conversation title in quotes.
Click Cancel first and check nothing is removed; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a conversation in the account

items.where: Sidebar row > Delete (the dialog says it cannot be undone)
steps: Open a conversation's row menu and click "Delete".
Read the dialog "Delete conversation?" for the words "This cannot be undone."
Check whether a second confirmation appears before anything is removed.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a conversation in the account
items.note: No separate permanent-delete control was found; the one delete dialog carries the irreversible warning. Whether a second confirmation exists is not shown in the code I read.

items.where: Chat title menu > Share…, or the Share button in the chat header
steps: Open a conversation with messages.
Click "Share…" in the title menu (or the header Share button).
Read the dialog title "Share conversation" and the audience text, for example "Anyone with the link".
Click "Copy" and check the link is copied and the dialog states who can open it.
items.needs: a conversation with messages
items.note: The header Share button is referred to in a code comment; its visible label was not checked.

items.where: Artifact panel > Publish, then Share
steps: Generate an artifact in a chat so the artifact panel opens.
Click the "Publish" action in the artifact panel.
Click the "Share" button in the panel to see the sharing choices.
