items.needs: an image on the clipboard
items.note: The paste handler is in code with no visible text of its own, so no label is given.

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files.
In the file chooser, pick two or more photos (use Command+click) and confirm.
Check that every photo appears as a thumbnail above the message box.
items.needs: two or more photos
items.note: No separate photo-library picker was found in code; the photo route is the same file chooser that the Mac shows.

items.where: Desktop menu File > Screenshot to Chat (or its keyboard shortcut)
steps: In the Electron desktop app, open the File menu.
Click Screenshot to Chat, or press the screenshot shortcut.
Wait for the capture to finish, then look at the chat composer for a new image thumbnail.
Send the message and check the screenshot is attached to it.
items.needs: the Electron desktop app and Screen Recording permission for the app on macOS
items.note: The composer's own More composer options menu did not show a screenshot row in code; the capture is the File menu item. The Capture screen button in the feedback dialog is for feedback, not chat attachments.

items.where: Keyboard shortcut Window to Chat (no menu item)
steps: Open another app window and bring it to the front, with the desktop app behind it.
Press the Window to Chat shortcut.
Wait for the notice and then look for a new image thumbnail in the chat composer.
Send the message and check the window capture is attached.
items.needs: the Electron desktop app, Screen Recording permission, and a second app window in front
items.note: Code captures the window in front of the app, not a window the user picks from a list. No picker was found.

items.where: More composer options > Add from library
steps: Make sure the Library holds at least one file (Library in the sidebar).
Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add from library and choose a file from the list.
Check that the file chip appears above the message box and is sent with the next message.
items.needs: a file already in the Library

items.where: Code page > Select repository (repository chip in the code composer)
steps: Open the Code page of the app.
Click the Select repository chip.
Pick a repository from the list that opens.
Check that the chosen repository is shown as the context for the task.
items.needs: a connected code account with at least one repository (not checked)
items.note: The sidebar entry that opens the Code page was not found in app-nav-items.ts, so the path to the Code page is unverified.

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files.
In the file chooser select several files at once and confirm.
Check that all of them appear as chips or thumbnails above the message box.
items.needs: several files

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose an image)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose an image file.
Look above the message box for a small square thumbnail of the image.
items.needs: an image file

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a PDF, spreadsheet, code or other file)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a PDF, a spreadsheet and a code file.
Compare the icon on each chip with the file type.
items.needs: a PDF, a spreadsheet and a code file
items.note: The kind names PDF, Spreadsheet, Code, Document, Text, Presentation and File are in AttachmentPreview.tsx; the icon glyphs were not checked on screen.

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose any file.
Look at the chip above the message box for the file name and its size (for example KB or MB).
items.needs: any file

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a large file)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a large file.
Watch the chip: it should show Preparing, Uploading or Verifying text under the file name while the upload runs.
items.needs: a large file, and a slow connection helps the status stay visible

items.where: Projects > open a project > project settings > Files (Indexing for search status on each file)
steps: Open Projects in the sidebar and open a project.
Open the project's settings and find the Files section.
Upload a file with the Upload button.
Watch the status next to the file: Indexing for search while it runs, then Keyword search only or Not indexed when it finishes.
items.needs: a project you own
items.note: The button that opens project settings was not confirmed; the Projects page mounts the settings dialog, and a failed status shows Not indexed or Keyword search only, with a retry control, not a separate Failed word.

items.where: Composer chip after a file finishes uploading
steps: Attach a file with Add photos & files.
Wait until the chip stops showing Uploading or Preparing text.
Check that the Send button is enabled and sends the message with the file.
items.needs: any file
items.note: Code hides the progress line when a chip is ready, and no Ready word is shown; the tester can only see the absence of progress text.

items.where: Under your sent message (notice reads Only part of NAME was read because it is too long to read in full.)
steps: Attach a long text or PDF file with Add photos & files.
Send the message.
Look under your own message bubble for the notice that starts with Only part of.
Compare with Expected: the notice names the file.
items.needs: a long file (text or PDF)

labels.text: was read because it is too long to read in full.

items.note: The notice comes from a response header after sending, so it appears after the send, not in the composer.

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a file type the chat cannot read)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a file of an unsupported type.
Look for the notice that names the file and says it has an unsupported file type.
items.needs: a file the chat cannot read (for example an unusual binary type)
items.note: The chooser may block some types through the accept attribute, so the tester may need to force a type that the chooser still allows.

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a password-protected PDF), then send
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a PDF that has a password.
Send the message and read the reply area.
Check for the notice that says the file is password protected and to remove the password and upload it again.
items.needs: a password-protected PDF

labels.text: is password protected. Remove the password and upload it again.

items.note: The notice is produced on the server when the message is sent; where it appears on screen was not traced.

items.where: Attachment chip under the message box (Retry on a failed upload)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options, then Add photos & files and choose a file.
Make the upload fail, for example by turning Wi-Fi off straight after choosing the file.
Look at the chip for Upload failed and a Retry button under the file name.
Turn Wi-Fi back on, click Retry, and check the upload runs again.
items.needs: a way to make an upload fail (for example turning Wi-Fi off)

items.where: Attachment chip under the message box, the X button while Uploading shows
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options, then Add photos & files and choose a large file.
While the chip shows Uploading, click the X button on that chip.
Check that the upload stops and the chip is removed.
Send a message and check the cancelled file is not sent.
items.needs: a large file so the upload lasts long enough to cancel
items.note: The X button's accessible name is Cancel upload of NAME while uploading; its visible glyph is an X icon.

items.where: Attachment chip under the message box, the X button (Remove NAME)
steps: Attach two or more files with Add photos & files.
Click the X button on one chip.
Check that only that chip disappears.
Send the message and check the removed file is not in the sent message.
items.needs: two or more files

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose the same file twice)
steps: Attach a file with Add photos & files.
Attach the same file again with Add photos & files.
Look for the notice that says the file is already attached.
Check the file is listed only once when you send.
items.needs: one file

items.where: Attachment chip under the message box (error text under the failed file)
steps: Attach a file that will fail, for example an image over the image size limit or a file that cannot be uploaded.
Look at the failed chip for the error text under its file name.
Hover the error text to see its full reason in the tooltip.
Check that the error names that file, not a general message.
items.needs: a file that fails (for example an image larger than the image limit)

items.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose several files, with one that is refused)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and select several files, including one that will be refused (for example a duplicate or an unsupported file).
Read the single notice that follows.
Check that it says how many files were attached and lists the refused files.
items.needs: several files, including one that will be refused
items.note: The notice reads Attached N of M files. Not attached: ... or None of the M files were attached: ...

items.where: More composer options > hover Add photos & files (tooltip)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Hover the mouse over the Add photos & files row and wait for the tooltip.
Read the tooltip for whether files are kept and for how long.
Open a temporary chat and repeat, then compare with the text that says files are deleted with the temporary chat.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Saved to your Library until you delete them.

items.note: The retention text is a hover tooltip on the row, not visible text in the menu; the number of days comes from RESOURCE_RECOVERY_WINDOW_DAYS.

items.where: New chat screen > attach a document or image with the attach control in the composer > choose a model that cannot read that file type from the model picker > the alert appears above the text box, with the buttons "Use Auto", "Remove attachments" and "Choose a compatible model"
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Attach a PDF or other document with the attach control in the composer (the menu label was not verified in code).
Select a model that cannot read documents or images (the model picker location was not verified in code).
Look above the text box for the warning that starts "The selected model can't read the attached document." (or "image" for pictures).
Check that the "Use Auto" button is present and that clicking "Choose a compatible model" lists models that can read the file, compared with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, a file to upload (PDF for document, PNG or JPG for image), a model that cannot read that file type
items.note: The warning is shown only when the selected model cannot read the file, and it is a warning with a fix button, not a block before sending. The attach menu and model picker labels were not found by search, so the tester must find them on screen. The free-plan variant of this warning uses "Use Free Auto" instead of "Use Auto".

items.where: New chat screen > select a local model (on-device) from the model picker > attach a file in the composer > the alert appears above the text box with "Switch to a cloud model" and "Remove attachment"
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Select a local model that runs on this device (the picker location was not verified in code).
Attach any file with the attach control in the composer.
Look for the alert that says "Local models on this device cannot read attachments." with the text "Switch to a cloud model or remove the attachment."
Compare with Expected: the alert names the alternative (switch to a cloud model) and the removal option, and the message is not sent through the local model.
items.needs: a local model available on the device (desktop app), a file to upload

labels.text: Local models on this device cannot read attachments. Switch to a cloud model or remove the attachment.

items.note: The local-model alert was located in code, but how a person selects a local model was not verified; the free-plan alert ("This free model accepts text only..." with "Use Free Auto") is a related alternative path that appears for restricted free models. The "Switch to a cloud model" text appears twice in ChatComposerNew.tsx, once for a local-model project conflict and once for the local-attachment conflict.

items.where: New chat screen > the composer at the bottom > the model button beside the send button (its name shows the current model); tap it to open the Models panel
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Look at the composer at the bottom of the screen and find the model button; note the model name shown on it.
Tap that button to open the panel titled Models.
Pick a different model, close the panel, and check the composer shows the new model's name.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The model name is data, so no fixed label is shown; the panel title is the only fixed word found.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > model developer rail
steps: Open a new chat and tap the model button in the composer.
In the Models panel, tap All models.
Look at the row of developers under the search box, under the label Model developers.
Open a model row and compare the provider shown with the developer rail.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Each row shows the provider as the fallback guidance text when no other description exists (model.provider in ComposerFooter.tsx).

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > model developer rail, and the About card's Family line
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer and tap All models.
Look at the list: versions of one model line should sit together.
Tap the About button on a model row and find the Family line in the card.
Compare the family shown with the other versions listed next to it.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Grouping is built in ModelCatalogue.tsx (groups by line label); I did not confirm a visible group heading for each family.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Search models box
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the box with the placeholder Search models.
Type part of a model name.
Check that the list shrinks to matching models, and that No models match appears when nothing fits.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > star button on a model row, then the Favourites rail
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the star button on a model row; its label changes to Remove <model> from favourites.
Tap the Favourites rail entry.
Check the starred model is listed on its own.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The code spells it Favourites; the rail count shows how many are starred.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Recent rail
steps: Use two or three different models in chats.
Open the Models panel from the composer and tap All models.
Tap the Recent rail entry.
Check the models you used most recently appear there.
items.needs: a signed-in account with some past model use

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > section labelled Recommended
steps: Sign in with a paid plan.
Open the Models panel from the composer.
Look for the section labelled Recommended above the rest of the list.
Compare the models listed there with what Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The Recommended section appears only when the account is on a paid plan (paidPlan check in ComposerFooter.tsx).

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > top row Auto
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find the top row, which shows the guidance text Picks the best model for each message.
Tap it and send a message.
Check the composer label shows Auto and the answer discloses which model was chosen (Auto chose ...).
items.needs: a signed-in account; a Free account sees Auto (free) instead

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

items.where: Settings > General > Default model
steps: Open Settings and tap General.
Find the row labelled Default model.
Open the select and choose a model; the hint under the row says New chats start with this model.
Open a new chat and check the composer shows the chosen model.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: How Settings is opened from the main screen was not traced; the General and Default model labels were found.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > tap a model row
steps: Tap the model button in the composer.
In the Models panel, tap a model row.
Check the composer model button now shows that model's name.
Send a message and check the answer is labelled with that model.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > each model row's guidance line, and the About button on a row
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Read the one-line text under each model name.
Tap the About button on a row to open its card.
Compare the text with the short description in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The guidance line falls back to the provider name when no guidance is defined (ComposerFooter.tsx).

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Filter by capability chips (Vision, Audio in)
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Look at the chips under the search box: Vision, Tools, Search and others.
Tap Audio in or Vision to filter the list.
Check the models shown accept that input.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Capability chips filter the list; the per-row icons are capability marks, which I did not trace further.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Filter by capability chips (Image out, Video out, Audio out)
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the chip Image out.
Check the models shown produce images.
Repeat with Video out and Audio out and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Tools chip
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the Tools chip under Filter by capability.
Check that only models with tool support are listed.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > About button on a model row > Context ceiling
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the About button on a model row.
Find the line Context ceiling and the line Output ceiling in the card.
Compare the numbers with the model's documented context size.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Values are shown only when the catalogue has a positive number for that model.

items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No visible wording about relative speed (faster or slower) was found in ModelCatalogue.tsx, ComposerFooter.tsx or packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelPicker.ts; the only speed text found is the Fast mode toggle (see S15.23). The cited lines are no longer there.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > About button on a model row > Credits per 1M tokens and Typical message
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the About button on a model row.
Read the lines Typical message and Credits per 1M tokens.
Compare the cost lines with the price band shown on the row.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The row price band is an aria and title text Price band N of M (ComposerFooter.tsx and ModelCatalogue.tsx).

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a locked model row shows its plan and an Upgrade button
steps: Sign in on a Free plan.
Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find a model row marked with a lock; its text shows the plan that unlocks it, and it has an Upgrade button.
Tap What each plan includes to see the plan list.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The lock text comes from the server row lock; the default text when none is set is Requires upgrade.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a model row with a stage badge (Preview, Experimental) or the Beta or Coming soon tag
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Look for a row carrying a badge: Preview or Experimental.
Also look for the Beta or Coming soon tag on other rows.
Compare the badges shown with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account; whether a Preview model is listed depends on the catalogue
items.note: The Preview and Experimental words come from the routing package, not the web app; I did not check whether any preview model is in the live catalogue.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a model row within 30 days of retirement shows Leaving on <date>
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Look at the status line of each row for the text Leaving on followed by a date.
Compare the date with the retirement date.
Check the row is still selectable before the date passes.
items.needs: a model whose retirement date is within 30 days (a test or live catalogue entry)
items.note: The notice only shows inside the 30-day window (DEPRECATION_WARNING_WINDOW_DAYS); outside it nothing shows.

items.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a model row marked Temporarily unavailable or Unavailable right now
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find a row with the text Temporarily unavailable (catalogue) or Unavailable right now (chooser row).
Try to tap that row.
Check the row cannot be chosen and the composer model does not change.
items.needs: a model that is marked unavailable in the live catalogue (may not occur in a normal account)

items.where: New chat > pick a reasoning model in the composer model button > the composer control labelled Reasoning effort (its slider shows Off or the level)
steps: Choose a reasoning model from the Models panel.
Look at the composer for the control labelled Reasoning effort.
Tap it and move the slider to another level.
Send a message and check the answer used the chosen level (compare with Expected).
items.needs: a reasoning-capable model; a paid plan may be needed for higher levels
items.note: The control is hidden for models without reasoning; the value Off is shown when the slider is off.

items.where: New chat > pick a model that offers a fast tier > the Reasoning effort control > the Fast mode switch
steps: Choose a model that offers faster serving from the Models panel.
Tap the Reasoning effort control in the composer.
Find the switch labelled Fast mode and turn it on; a Fast pill appears.
Read the help text and compare the extra usage with Expected.
items.needs: a model with a fast tier and an account allowed to use it (a paid plan is likely)
items.note: The Fast mode switch is placed inside the same panel as the effort control (located by line position in ComposerFooter.tsx, not by a full trace).

items.where: New chat > composer Style control (labelled Style) > Response Length row of buttons
steps: Tap the Style control in the composer.
Find the heading Response Length and the row of length buttons below it.
Tap a different length and close the panel.
Send the same question and compare answer length with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The length option names come from RESPONSE_LENGTH_OPTIONS in apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts; I did not read their words.

items.where: Desktop app > New chat > composer model button > Models panel > section On this device (Use models on this device; Manage local models)
steps: Start the Desktop app on a paid plan with Ollama or LM Studio running and a model loaded.
Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find the section On this device; if asked, allow Use models on this device.
Pick a local model, send a message and check the composer shows the local model name with the Local badge.
items.needs: the Desktop app; a paid account (the section is hidden on Free); Ollama or LM Studio with a model loaded
items.note: The section appears only when the account is not on the Free plan; the local-runtime dispatcher is apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts.

items.where: Composer, model button (shows the model name) > pick a model in the list (under "Models")
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the model name button under the message box (its label ends in "change model").
In the "Models" list, click a different model such as one shown in the list.
Close the list, press Cmd+R or quit and reopen the Desktop app, then open a new chat.
Compare: the composer still shows the model you picked, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account; the model must be one your plan can use
items.note: The choice is saved in the browser's local storage under the key agi-model-store (apps/web/shared/stores/model-store.ts:376), so it is per device, not per account; a tester must reopen the app to confirm. The Desktop shell shows the hosted web app, so a reopen check is the same as in the browser.

items.where: Open a chat > Composer, model button (ends in "change model") > pick a model in the "Models" list
steps: Sign in, open an existing chat or start one and send a message.
Click the model name button under the message box.
In the "Models" list, click a different model.
Open a different chat, then come back to this chat.
Compare: this chat still uses the model you picked, while the other chat keeps its own model, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account; two chats

labels.text: Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.

items.note: The per-conversation save is wired in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx (handleConversationModelChange, passed as onModelChange); the list confirms the choice only through the saved state, and the error toast names the failure.

items.where: Chat > under an answer, hover it and click "Regenerate response" (the arrow icon) > "Try again with" list
steps: Open a chat that has at least one answer.
Hover the answer so the action icons appear under it.
Click the "Regenerate response" button.
In the menu, look at the list under "Try again with" and click a different model.
Compare: a new answer appears from that model, and the chat's own model in the model button does not change, as Expected says.
items.needs: a chat with an answer; a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The menu appears for a reply (not on the user's own message); the check that the chat's model stays the same is inferred from the code path onRegenerateWithModel, not from a visible label.

items.where: Chat > hover an answer from the assistant > small line under the answer that names the model (for example "Auto chose" followed by the model name)
steps: Open a chat and send a message to get an answer.
Move the mouse over the answer so the line under it appears (it is hidden until hover, or shown by touch on a touch screen).
Read the line under the answer that names the model.
Compare: the name shown is the model that wrote this answer, with "Auto chose" in front when Auto was used, as Expected says.
items.needs: none beyond a Free account or a paid account; a message that has an answer
items.note: The name text comes from getManagedModelPresentationLabel in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelInfo.ts; the line is hidden until hover, so a tester must hover before reading it. The text "Answered by" appears only inside a tooltip for on-device answers (MessageBubble.tsx:467), not as a label on the main line.

items.where: Chat > under an answer, a grey notice box that says why another model answered (with a "Dismiss" button)
steps: Start a chat and send a message.
Look under the answer for a grey notice box with the words from the substitution text.
Click "Dismiss" to remove the notice, then send another message if one appears again.
Compare: the notice says a different model answered and gives the reason, and "Dismiss" hides it, as Expected says.
items.needs: a situation where the chosen model fails and another model answers; a tester cannot force this from the menus alone
items.note: The reason text comes from describeFallbackReason in apps/web/lib/chat-fallback-reason.ts and was not read in full; the notice shows only when a substitute answered, so the tester may not reach it on demand.

items.where: Composer, model button (ends in "change model") > pick a model that cannot read the current chat (such as a text-only model when an image is attached) > the box that says "Switch to <model name>?"
steps: Open a new chat and attach an image using the attach control in the message box.
Click the model name button under the message box.
Click a model that cannot read images, if one is listed.
Read the box that says "Switch to" followed by the model name, and the reason under it.
Compare: the box names what will be lost and gives "Switch anyway" and "Keep <your current model>" buttons, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account; an image file to upload; a model in the list that cannot read images
items.note: The reasons come from evaluateModelCompatibility in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts; the box sits inside the model picker, not as a separate popup, and the exact model that triggers it depends on the account's plan and the list.

items.where: Composer, a red-grey box above the message box after you attach a file a model cannot read > buttons "Use Auto" or "Choose a compatible model" or "Remove attachments"
steps: Open a new chat and attach an image or document with the attach control.
Click the model name button and choose a model that cannot read that file type.
Read the box above the message box that starts with "The selected model can't read the attached".
Click "Choose a compatible model" to see the list of models that can read it, or click "Use Auto" to switch.
Compare: you can keep the file by switching to a model that can read it, or remove it with "Remove attachments", as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account; an image or document file to upload; a model in the list that cannot read it
items.note: The box text differs for free plans ("This free model accepts text only..." or "accepts images only...") and uses "Use Free Auto" instead of "Use Auto"; the box is the same conflict surface as S15.34 and is shown only when the chosen model cannot read the file.

steps: Sign in, start a new chat, type a short message and press Send.
Look at the message: it sits as a right-aligned bubble, and the assistant reply is a flat left-aligned column with no avatar or name, so the two authors are told apart by alignment and bubble style.
items.needs: none
items.note: There is no avatar or visible name. The only author text is a screen-reader-only heading 'You said:' in MessageBubble.tsx, so the visual part is alignment only.

items.where: Start a new chat, type in the message box at the bottom of the chat screen, press Send
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Type a short sentence in the message box at the bottom and press Send.
Look at the transcript: the sentence you typed should appear in your message bubble above the reply.
items.needs: none
items.note: The exact visible label of the Send control was not confirmed in the files; the transcript bubble is in MessageBubble.tsx.

items.where: Start a new chat, attach a file or image to the message box, press Send
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Attach an image or a file to the message box (use the attach control at the bottom of the chat screen), type a short text and press Send.
Look at the sent message: image thumbnails or a named file chip should appear on that message. Click a thumbnail to open it full size.
items.needs: a file to upload, and optionally an image
items.note: The attach control's visible label was not confirmed. The thumbnail is labelled 'View <name> full size' (a template, not a fixed word).

items.where: Chat screen, a sent message with a skill, a connector prompt or a connector resource attached
steps: Sign in and open a chat where a skill or a connector (MCP) prompt or resource is available.
Use the skill, prompt or resource in the message box and press Send.
Look under the sent user message: chips such as '/<skill name>', 'Prompt:' or 'Resource:' should appear, grouped as 'Context sent with this message'.
items.needs: a connector with prompts or resources, or a skill
items.note: Only skill, connector prompt and connector resource chips were found. Chips for quoted text, page, editor selection and @mentions were not found in MessageContextChips.tsx or MessageBubble.tsx.

items.where: Hover over the sent user message > 'More message actions' (the three-dot button) > 'Sent at'
steps: Sign in, send a message in a chat.
Hover over your sent message (on touch screens the actions stay visible).
Click the 'More message actions' button under the message.
Look at the top of the menu: 'Sent at' followed by the time should be shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The time is shown on demand inside the menu, not inline. Only the time (no date) is displayed in the menu.

items.where: Hover over a sent user message > 'Edit message' > save the edit > a version pager appears under the message
steps: Send a message, then hover over it and click 'Edit message'.
Change the text and click 'Save & Retry'.
Look under the edited message: a version pager with 'Previous version' and 'Next version' arrows appears, and its label should read 'Edited message, version n of m'.
items.needs: none
items.note: The text 'Edited message, version n of m' is in VariantPager.tsx; the code did not show whether it is visible or only a screen-reader label. The pager (not a separate 'Edited' tag) is the only marker found.

items.where: Hover over the sent user message > 'Copy message' button (tooltip 'Copy')
steps: Send a message and hover over it.
Click the copy button (tooltip 'Copy') in the action row under the message.
Paste into the message box or another app. The icon should change to a check and the label to 'Message copied'. Compare the pasted text with the sent text.
items.needs: none
items.note: The copy button is inside a condition named hasReadableTurn; it was not confirmed that this condition is true for user messages.

items.where: Hover over the sent user message > 'Edit message' (pencil button, tooltip 'Edit')
steps: Send a message and hover over it.
Click the pencil button 'Edit message' in the action row.
The bubble becomes an editor with 'Cancel' and 'Save & Retry' buttons. Change the text and click 'Save & Retry'.
Look at the thread: the edited message replaces the old one and a new reply appears.
items.needs: a sent message

items.where: Hover over the sent user message > 'Retry this message' (circular arrow button, tooltip 'Retry')
steps: Send a message and wait until the reply finishes (the button is disabled while a reply is running).
Hover over your sent message and click 'Retry this message' in the action row.
Look at the thread: a new reply should appear for the same unchanged message.
items.needs: none
items.note: The plan calls this 'Resend', but the control is labelled 'Retry' (tooltip 'Retry'). It is not shown in voice mode.

items.where: Hover over the sent user message > 'More message actions' > 'Branch conversation from here'
steps: Open a chat with at least two exchanges.
Hover over an earlier user message and click 'More message actions'.
Click 'Branch conversation from here' (it shows 'Creating branch…' while running).
Look at the new conversation: it should contain the thread up to that message, and the original chat should stay unchanged.
items.needs: a chat with several messages

items.where: Hover over an edited user message > 'Previous version' / 'Next version' arrows under the message (appears only after the message has more than one version)
steps: Send a message, then edit it with 'Edit message' > 'Save & Retry' so it has two versions.
Look under the edited message for the pager arrows.
Click 'Previous version' and 'Next version' and check the page position changes (n of m), and the thread below follows the chosen version.
items.needs: a sent message that you can edit
items.note: The plan records this item as unfinished in the UI. The gate in apps/web/features/chat/lib/message-variants-gate.ts was not read and may hide the pager.

items.where: Chat screen, a long sent user message (collapsed) > 'Show more' button under the message
steps: Send a long message (several paragraphs of text).
Look under the message: it should be cut short and a 'Show more' button appears under it.
Click 'Show more' and check the full message is visible.
items.needs: a long message to paste or type
items.note: The collapse threshold is a fixed height; the exact length that triggers it is not stated in the files.

items.where: Chat screen, an expanded long sent user message > 'Show less' button under the message
steps: Follow S16.12 to expand a long message.
Click 'Show less' under the expanded message.
Check the message shrinks back to the collapsed height with 'Show more' visible again.
items.needs: a long message to paste or type

items.where: Message box at the bottom of the chat screen, after a send fails (for example with the network off)
steps: Sign in, open a chat, and turn off the Wi-Fi or network.
Type a message and press Send.
Look at the message box and the transcript: a notice "Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again." should appear above the composer, with the text restored in the box.
items.needs: a way to make the network fail (turn off Wi-Fi)

labels.text: Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again.

items.note: The code restores the failed text to the composer with this notice. No failed state on the user's own bubble in the transcript was found, which differs from the Expected line.

items.needs: a way to make the network fail (turn off Wi-Fi)
items.note: Searched MessageBubble.tsx, ChatMessageList.tsx and ChatComposerNew.tsx for a Retry or Resend control on a failed user send; found none. The only 'Try again' is for a stopped response in ChatMessageList.tsx. A failed send is restored to the composer (see S16.15), where the tester presses Send again, but there is no Retry control that re-sends the same text and attachments.

items.where: Message box at the bottom of the chat screen, while a reply is still running > 'Queued' row above the box
steps: Send a message that starts a long reply.
While the reply is still streaming, type a second message in the message box and press Send.

Look above the message box: a row labelled 'Queued' (or 'Queued 1 of 2:' with more than one) with 'Edit queued message' and 'Cancel queued message' buttons should appear, and it should disappear when the reply goes out.
items.needs: a reply that takes time to finish

items.where: Chat screen: type text in the message box, switch to another chat in the sidebar, then come back to the first chat
steps: Open chat A and type a sentence in the message box but do not press Send.
Open a different chat, then go back to chat A.
Look at the message box: the unsent sentence should still be there, while the sent messages stay in the transcript as sent messages.
Send a message while the network is off (see S16.15): the text should return to the box with the notice 'Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again.'
items.needs: two chats, and optionally the network off to test a failed send

labels.text: Couldn't send. Restored here so you can try again.

items.note: Per-conversation draft sync is in apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-conversation-draft-sync.ts; the sidebar label for switching chats was not confirmed.

items.where: Any answer > the "More message actions" button (the three dots under the answer). The top of that menu shows which model answered.
steps: Send any question in a new chat and wait for the answer.
Click the "More message actions" button under the answer.
Look at the label at the top of the menu: it should name the model that answered, and the answer should look different from your own message.
items.needs: none
items.note: The model name comes from answeredByLabel in MessageBubble.tsx; the sr-only headings "You said:" and "Assistant said:" are for assistive tech only.

items.where: Shown automatically while an answer is being written; there is no control for it.
steps: Send a question that needs a longer answer.
Watch the answer area while it is being written.
Check that text appears in pieces as it arrives and that markdown (bold, lists, code) is formatted once it shows.
items.needs: none
items.note: No single control; the streaming render is in MessageBubble.tsx and useChatStream.ts. Not verified in a browser.

items.where: Shown automatically between sending and the first text: the wait shows "Preparing", then "Generating response…".
steps: Send a question and look at the answer area right away.
Check for the "Preparing" or "Generating response…" text before text appears.
items.needs: none
items.note: The announced status is set in ChatMessageList.tsx; I did not confirm the screen-reader announcement itself.

items.where: An answer that has thinking > "Thought process" row (or "Thought for <time>") > click to expand.
steps: Use a model that shows reasoning and send a hard question.
Find the "Thought process" row under or above the answer.
Click the row and check that the reasoning text and step summary open, and that clicking again closes it.
items.needs: a model that returns reasoning (which models do this depends on the plan)
items.note: The row only appears when the model returns reasoning. The expand control has the aria-label "Expand reasoning" in the same file.

items.where: An answer that used a tool > "Used tools" section above the answer text ("Used N tools" when there are several).
steps: Send a question that needs a tool, for example a question that needs a web search.
Find the "Used tools" section on the answer.
Open the section and check each tool's name, its status and its result.
items.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant call a tool
items.note: The tool timeline component is apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ToolTimeline.tsx.

items.where: An answer that used web sources > numbered citation markers in the text > click a marker.
steps: Send a question that needs current web information.
Find the small numbered markers inside the answer text.
Click or hover a marker and check that it names the source and opens its link.
items.needs: a prompt that triggers a web search
items.note: Marker behaviour is in MessageBubble.tsx and the citation helpers; I did not confirm the exact hover text.

items.where: A finished answer that used sources > "View N sources" control at the end of the answer.
steps: Send a question that uses web sources and wait until the answer finishes.
Find the "View N sources" control at the bottom of the answer.
Click it and check that the source list opens and each source link can be opened.
items.needs: a prompt that uses web sources
items.note: While the answer is still streaming the control reads "View N sources so far". The control component is SourcesControl in apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx.

items.where: An answer that produced a file > file card under the answer > "Download".
steps: Ask the assistant for a file, for example a spreadsheet or a text document.
Find the file card under the answer, with the file name and type.
Click "Download" and check that the file saves with the name shown on the card.
items.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant produce a file
items.note: Downloads are labelled by DELIVERABLE_DOWNLOAD_ACTION in DeliverableCard.tsx.

items.where: An answer that created an artifact > "Open artifact: <title>" card under the answer > click it.
steps: Ask for a document, a code file or a web page.
Find the artifact card under the answer.
Click the card and check that the artifact panel opens with the artifact shown.
items.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant create an artifact
items.note: The card's aria-label is "Open artifact: <title>" and the button turns into "Hide artifact" when the panel is shown.

items.where: An answer that generated an image > the image shows inline in the answer > open or download it from the image card.
steps: Ask the assistant to create an image.
Look for the image inline in the answer.
Open or download the image from its card and check that it matches the picture shown.
items.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant create an image
items.note: The image card is apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ImageToolCard.tsx, but my search found no visible button text in it, so the exact control words are unknown.

items.where: Composer > switch to video generation (the video mode) > send a prompt > the video plays in the answer > "Download video".
steps: Turn on video generation in the composer and type a short prompt.
Send it and wait for the video to appear in the answer.
Press the play control on the video, then click "Download video" and check that the video plays with controls and downloads.
items.needs: a plan and deployment that allow video generation
items.note: I found the composer's exit control (aria "Exit video generation mode" in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx) but not the exact words of the control that turns video mode on.

items.where: An answer that shows interactive blocks (cards with choices, tables, buttons) > operate them inside the answer.
steps: Ask for options laid out as cards or a choice list, for example "show my options as cards with buttons".
Find the cards in the answer.
Click a choice or button and check that the answer responds in place.
items.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant build interactive answer blocks
items.note: The block types come from apps/web/lib/services/answer-ui-tool-service.ts; I did not find fixed visible words for the blocks.

items.where: Settings > General > "Show follow-up suggestions in chats" (switch on).
steps: Open Settings and go to General.
Turn on "Show follow-up suggestions in chats".
Send a question, wait for the answer, and check that suggested follow-up prompts appear below it and can be clicked.
items.needs: a Free or paid account
items.note: The setting is off by default in ChatMessageList.tsx (the default constant is false), so the suggestions do not show until the switch is turned on. The deploy-level switch-on noted in the plan was not re-checked.

items.where: Under any answer > the copy icon (tooltip "Copy").
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the copy icon under the answer.
Paste into a text app and check that the full answer text is pasted, and that the icon briefly changes to "Message copied".
items.needs: none
items.note: The aria-label changes between "Copy message" and "Message copied".

items.where: Under an answer > "More message actions" (three dots) > "Read message aloud".
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click "More message actions" under the answer.
Click "Read message aloud" and check that the answer is spoken.
items.needs: none (a speaker is needed to hear it)
items.note: The menu item is replaced by a reason text when read-aloud is unavailable; playback is in apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts.

items.where: Under an answer > "More message actions" > "Stop reading message" (shown while the answer is being read aloud).
steps: Start read-aloud as in S17.17.
While it speaks, click "More message actions" under the answer again.
Click "Stop reading message" and check that the speech stops.
items.needs: none (a speaker is needed to hear it)
items.note: The unified-chat ActionBar in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ActionBar.tsx uses the same words for other surfaces.

items.where: Under a finished answer > the regenerate icon (tooltip "Regenerate"); with several models available it opens a menu with "Try again".
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the regenerate icon under the answer (aria "Regenerate response").
Check that a new attempt replaces the answer and that the variant pager (see S17.28) now shows two attempts.
items.needs: none
items.note: The aria-label is "Regenerate response" in MessageBubble.tsx.

items.where: A failed answer > "Retry" button on the notice under it (aria "Retry this response").
steps: Make an answer fail, for example by losing the connection during a send or by a refusal notice.
Find the "Retry" button on the failure notice.
Click "Retry" and check that the failure is replaced by a new answer for the same question.
items.needs: a way to make a turn fail, such as a dropped connection
items.note: Retry is wired in useChatStream.ts; I did not run a failure to see the notice.

items.where: An answer cut off by the length limit > "Continue generating" button under the answer.
steps: Ask for a very long answer, for example a long report.
Wait for the answer to stop part way.
Click "Continue generating" and check that the same answer carries on from where it stopped.
items.needs: a prompt long enough to reach the output limit
items.note: The button's aria-label is "Continue generating this response".

items.where: Under a finished answer > regenerate icon ("Regenerate") > "Try again with" > choose a model.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Open the regenerate menu under the answer.
Choose a model under "Try again with" and check that a new attempt from that model replaces or joins the answer.
items.needs: an account with more than one model available
items.note: The model list only appears when regenerateModelOptions has entries; the plan tier that allows it was not confirmed.

items.where: Under an answer > the branch icon (tooltip "Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged"); also in "More message actions" on your own messages.
steps: Have a conversation with at least two exchanges.
Click the branch icon under an earlier answer.
Check that a new conversation opens with history up to that answer, and that the original conversation is unchanged.
items.needs: a conversation with several messages
items.note: The aria-label is "Branch conversation from here" and changes to "Creating branch…" while it runs.

items.where: Under an answer that has several attempts > the pager "Previous response" / "Next response" with the position text "Response 2 of 3".
steps: Regenerate an answer (see S17.19) so it has two attempts.
Find the pager under the answer, which shows the position.
Click the next and previous buttons and check the answer changes and the text reads "Response N of M".
items.needs: an answer with at least two attempts
items.note: The position text is built in VariantPager.tsx as "Response {position} of {total}".

items.where: Under a finished answer > thumbs-up icon (aria "Good response"; tooltip "Good response", or "Remove rating" once rated).
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the thumbs-up icon under the answer.
Check that the icon shows as selected with tooltip "Remove rating", and that clicking again removes the rating.
items.needs: none
items.note: The rating is saved to the message through the feedback path; I did not confirm where it is stored.

items.where: Under a finished answer > thumbs-down icon (aria "Bad response"; tooltip "Bad response", or "Remove rating" once rated).
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the thumbs-down icon under the answer.
Check the rating is recorded on that answer (selected icon, tooltip "Remove rating") and, if the details panel opens, that it can be filled in.
items.needs: none
items.note: The details panel is ResponseRatingDetails.tsx; I did not confirm when it opens.

items.where: Under an answer > "More message actions" (three dots) > "Report this response".
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click "More message actions" under the answer.
Click "Report this response" and check the menu item changes to "Reporting…" then "Reported", with the toast "Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it."
items.needs: none
items.note: The toast text is set in MessageBubble.tsx; the report is sent to the feedback intake, which I did not trace further.

items.where: Open a chat that has messages > top bar "Share" button (its label is "Share conversation") > dialog titled "Share conversation". For one answer: hover the answer > "More message actions" > "Share answer".
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has at least one question and answer.
Click the "Share" button in the top bar (on narrow windows only the icon shows; hover it to read "Share conversation").
In the "Share conversation" dialog, read the text and look for a link or workspace option that can be copied or shared.
To share one answer: hover the answer, click "More message actions", then click "Share answer".
Compare: the conversation dialog opens with its own title and a shareable link; the answer action opens the system share sheet, or shows "This answer could not be shared" if it fails.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that has messages
items.note: The dialog's link-creation control text was not found in the code, and the answer share fallback when the system share sheet is missing was not traced.

items.where: Hover an answer > "More message actions" > the usage block at the bottom of the menu (tokens and time). The model name shows under "Sent at" in the answer header.
steps: Sign in, send a message and wait until the answer has finished.
Hover the answer and click "More message actions".
Scroll to the bottom of the menu and read the token usage block and the duration line.
Look at the answer header: find the "Sent at" time and read the model name shown just below it.
Compare: the menu shows usage for that answer and the header names the model that answered.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a finished answer
items.note: The usage block appears only when the answer carries token data, so it may be missing on some answers; the cost figure and its exact wording were not traced.

items.where: In the chat transcript, under the partial answer that stayed on screen, as a row starting "Response failed:".
steps: Start a long answer.
While text is still arriving, interrupt the connection (for example turn off Wi-Fi briefly).
Look under the partly written answer for a row starting "Response failed:" followed by the reason.
Compare: the text that arrived stays visible above the row and the row gives the reason it stopped.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a way to drop the connection during an answer

labels.text: the response stopped part way through; the part that arrived is kept above.

items.note: The network-drop step is an untested guess at a trigger; the code shows the reason text but not which failure produces it.

items.where: Send a prompt the model refuses; the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons." appears under the last answer, with a "Retry" action.
steps: Sign in and send a prompt that the safety layer is likely to refuse.
When the answer ends, look under it for the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons."
Read the "Retry" action and the report/appeal control next to it (its text was not found in the code).
Compare: the refusal is shown as its own notice, not as a normal answer or a generic error.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a refusal cannot be forced on demand

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

items.note: A refusal depends on the model's decision, so the tester may not be able to reproduce it on demand.

items.where: Send a message, then press the stop control while the answer is still being written. The notice "Response stopped." appears with a "Try again" button.
steps: Sign in, send a message that gives a long answer.
While the answer is still being written, press the stop control in the message box.
Look for the notice "Response stopped." under the partial answer and keep the text that arrived.
Click "Try again" and compare: a new attempt for the same question replaces the stopped one.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The stop control's visible label was not found in the code, so the tester must find it by its position in the message box.

items.where: Only when a reply comes back empty: a row starting "Response failed:" with the reason "no response was returned." and a "Retry" action, shown in place of an empty bubble.
steps: Sign in and send a message.
If the reply comes back empty, look for a row starting "Response failed:" under the question.
Read the reason "no response was returned." and the "Retry" action beside it.
Compare: there is no empty answer bubble, and Retry sends the turn again.
items.needs: a signed-in account; an empty reply cannot be forced on demand
items.note: The empty-reply case depends on the service returning nothing, so the tester may not be able to reproduce it on demand.

items.where: No control. The title is written by the server after the first message; check the conversation's row in the sidebar list.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat without naming it.
Send one message and wait for the reply.
Look at the sidebar row for this chat and at the title at the top of the chat. Compare with Expected: a meaningful title, not a placeholder.
items.needs: none
items.note: The title is generated in apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts; there is no visible control for it, so the tester only sees the result.

items.where: Chat screen > conversation title at the top > Rename
steps: Open a conversation that has messages.
Click the conversation title at the top of the chat.
Click Rename in the menu, type a new name and press Enter.
Open the sidebar and check that the row shows the new name; reload the page and check it again.
items.needs: none
items.note: A double-click on a sidebar row also starts renaming (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx) but that row has no visible label.

items.where: Sidebar > the row's More options button (three dots, hover the row) > Pin; later the same menu > Unpin
steps: Hover a conversation row in the sidebar and click its three-dot More options button.
Click Pin.
Check that the row now shows a pin mark and moves to the top of the list (the move to top was not confirmed in the code read).
Repeat the menu and click Unpin; check the pin mark is gone.
items.needs: none

items.where: Sidebar > a row's More options button > Archive; to bring it back open Show archived chats and use the row's More options > Restore
steps: Hover a conversation row, click its three-dot More options button and click Archive.
Check that the chat leaves the main list and a toast says Chat archived.
Click Show archived chats in the sidebar to list archived chats.
Click More options on the archived chat, click Restore, and check it returns to the main list. The chat screen menu also offers Archive and Unarchive.
items.needs: none
items.note: The toast text Chat archived and its Undo button exist in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json.

items.where: Sidebar > a row's More options button > Delete, or chat screen > conversation title > Delete
steps: Hover a conversation row, click its three-dot More options button and click Delete.
Read the dialog title Delete conversation? and its text; click Cancel first and check the chat is still there.
Click Delete again, then the Delete conversation button in the dialog.
Check the chat is gone from the sidebar and that opening its old link shows it as not found.
items.needs: none
items.note: 'Disappears everywhere' (other devices) was not checked in the code read.

items.where: Chat screen > conversation title at the top > Duplicate as branch
steps: Open a conversation that has messages.
Click the conversation title at the top of the chat and click Duplicate as branch.
Check that a new conversation opens with the same messages.
Send a message in the new one and check the original conversation is unchanged.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu says Duplicate as branch, not Duplicate; the code calls the fork action for it.

items.where: Sidebar > a row's More options button > Move to project > the project name; or chat screen > conversation title > Move to project
steps: Make sure at least one project exists (the menu item appears only when a project exists).
Hover a conversation row, click its three-dot More options button and open Move to project.
Click a project name.
Open that project and check the conversation is listed there.
items.needs: a project created first

items.where: Composer (bottom of the chat) > second row > the Chat / Work switch
steps: Open a new or existing conversation and look at the switch under the message box.
Click Work, then send a message.
Check the reply uses the work mode: the Work session panel opens from Panels.
Click Chat, send another message, and check it behaves as a chat reply.
items.needs: none
items.note: The switch is disabled while a reply is still running.

items.where: Composer + button > Use incognito (switch to Exit incognito); the same menu shows End temporary chat
steps: Click the + button in the message box.
Click Use incognito and read the explanation under it: Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.
Send a message and check the chat is not in the sidebar history after you leave it.
Open the + menu again and click Exit incognito (or End temporary chat) and check the state changes.
items.needs: none
items.note: The + button's own label was not located in the code read; the explanation text is in apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts.

items.where: Keyboard: Command+F (Ctrl+F on Windows/Linux) in an open chat > Search messages box
steps: Open a conversation with several messages.
Press Command+F.
Type a word that appears in the chat and check the Search messages... box opens.
Check the match count next to the box (N of M matches or No matches) and that matches are highlighted.
items.needs: a conversation with repeated words

items.where: Search messages box (after Command+F) > Next match and Previous match arrows
steps: Search for a word that has several matches.
Press Enter or click the Next match (Enter) arrow; check the view scrolls to the next match.
Press Shift+Enter or click the Previous match (Shift+Enter) arrow; check the view goes back.
Check the count in the box changes with each move.
items.needs: a conversation with repeated words

items.where: Chat screen > round down-arrow button labelled Scroll to bottom (appears when you scroll up)
steps: Open a long conversation and scroll up to an older message.
Look for the round down-arrow button at the bottom of the message area.
Click it and check the view jumps back to the latest message.
items.needs: a long conversation
items.note: The rule for when the button appears was not traced in full.

items.where: Hover an assistant reply > Branch conversation from here; then the branch arrows on that message (Previous branch, Next branch)
