Start a work task from a chat in this project (the way to switch a chat to Work was not confirmed in code).
Return to the Work tab and look at the task's state.
items.needs: a project with a chat that can run Work
items.note: The empty-state text is in ProjectWorkPanel.tsx; the control that starts a Work task was not located.

items.where: Projects > open a project > Scheduled
steps: Open a project and click the Scheduled tab.
Look for scheduled routines listed for this project.
Use the create control for a routine on this tab (its exact label was not found).
Look: the new routine is listed on the project's Scheduled tab.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The routine creation control on this tab was not found in the code; the Scheduled tab and SchedulesPage.tsx were.

items.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Default model
steps: Open a project and choose Project settings from its menu.
Find the Default model field and choose a model.
Save the settings.
Start a new chat in the project.
Look: the new chat starts with the model you chose.
items.needs: none

items.where: Projects (sidebar) > search box
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar and make sure you have several projects.
Click the box labelled Search projects... and type part of a project name.
Look: only matching projects stay in the list.
Type a word from a project's description and look whether it matches.
items.needs: several projects, one with a description

items.where: Projects > open a project > Share > (member list)
steps: Open a project and click Share from its menu.
Look at the sharing dialog for the owner and the list of people with access.
Sign in as a second account in the same workspace and look at the project list.
Open the shared project and look for the Shared with you label.
items.needs: a second account in the same workspace

items.where: Projects > open a project > Share > member role
steps: Open a project shared with a second account and click Share.
Open the access choice for a member.
Look at the choices: Can view, Can edit and No access.
Set a role, then sign in as that member and check what they can do.
items.needs: a second account in the same workspace
items.note: Server enforcement is not checked here; the role labels were found in ProjectSharingControls.tsx.

items.where: Projects > open a project > Share > Add people
steps: Open a project and click Share.
Click Add people and choose a person in the workspace.
Look: the person appears in the member list with a role.
Remove the person from the project (the remove control was not located in code) and look that they lose access.
items.needs: an owner account and a second account in the same workspace

labels.text: Everyone in the workspace can view

items.note: Partial: the add control was found; the remove control's visible words were not found in the sharing files.

items.where: Projects > project card menu > Share > Copy link
steps: On the Projects page, open a project card's menu and click Share.
Click Copy link in the dialog.
Open the copied link in a new private window signed in as a shared member.
Look: the project opens for that member.
items.needs: an owner account and a second account in the same workspace

items.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Duplicate
steps: Open a project as its owner and choose Project settings from its menu.
Click Duplicate.
Look: a copy appears in the Projects list.
Open the copy and check its settings, instructions and files.
items.needs: a project owner account
items.note: A code comment near the buttons says Duplicate and Export had no caller, but a Duplicate button is present in the code, so the comment looks out of date.

items.where: Projects > project card menu > Archive; then Archived (n) > Unarchive
steps: On the Projects page, open a project card's menu and click Archive.
Look: the project leaves the active list.
Click the Archived button at the top of the page.
Click Unarchive on the project and look: it returns to the active list with its chats and files.
items.needs: a project to archive

items.where: Projects > project card menu > Delete; or Projects > open a project > Project settings > Delete project
steps: Open a project's menu and click Delete (or use Delete project in Project settings).
Read the confirmation dialog and check what it says about files and chats.
Confirm the deletion.
Look: the project is gone, and its chats still appear (not in a project).
items.needs: a project owner account and a project you can delete
items.note: Conflict: the ProjectCard.tsx confirmation says its chats, files and memories are deleted with it, while the Project settings confirmation says conversations are moved to All Chats. Expected says chats are kept, so the tester should compare both.

items.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Memory > Use memories from outside this project
steps: Open a project and choose Project settings from its menu.
Find the Memory section and turn off Use memories from outside this project.
Save and start a new chat in the project.
Look at the helper text: it says chats here use only this project's memories.
items.needs: a signed-in account with some account-wide memories

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project

items.note: The toggle's helper text covers memories only; the code does not show a visible control that excludes other chats.

items.where: Projects > open a shared project (as a member)
steps: Sign in as a member of a project shared with you and open it from the Projects page.
Look for the Shared with you label under the project name.
Read the explanation under it.
Look: it says instructions and files are shared, and chats and memories stay private.
items.needs: a second account in the same workspace and a project shared with it
items.note: The explanation text is in apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx near line 1030.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Uploads
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Uploads tab in the row of tabs under the search box.
Look that only files you uploaded are listed (no files the assistant made).
items.needs: a file to upload (upload one first with New > Upload file if the Library is empty)
items.note: The tab is labelled Uploads, not an uploaded-files view name; the filter is origin uploaded.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Generated files
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Generated files tab in the row of tabs under the search box.
Look that only files the assistant produced are listed, and that uploads are not.
items.needs: an account that already has a generated file (for example an image or document made in a chat)

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Artifacts
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Artifacts tab.
Click a tile labelled Open followed by an artifact name; the artifact opens in the Library viewer.
Look that the list shows only your artifacts and that each one opens.
items.needs: an account with at least one artifact made in a chat
items.note: The tile label is built as Open <name> in code, so the exact tile text depends on the artifact name.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Images
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Images tab.
Click an image tile (its label is Open followed by the file name). The image opens in a viewer dialog named after the file, with Zoom in and Zoom out buttons.
Look that the image is shown in the viewer and that the Images tab lists images only.
items.needs: an account with at least one image

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Videos
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Videos tab.
Click a video tile (label Open followed by the file name).
In the viewer, press the play control on the video and look that it plays.
items.needs: an account with at least one video
items.note: The video player is a standard video element with controls (test id library-video-player).

items.where: Chat composer > (+) menu > Add from library
steps: Open a chat (or New chat) and click the + button beside the message box.
Hover or click Add from library.
Look at the list: it shows your most recently changed library files, newest first.
Click Browse all at the bottom to compare with the full Library sorted by Modified.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a few library files
items.note: No separate Recent view exists in the Library; the recent list is the Add from library submenu, sorted by modified. The exact label of the + button was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Grid view / List view (icon buttons at the top right, in the group Library layout)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar and note that files show as tiles.
Click the List view icon button at the right of the filter row.
Look that files now show as rows with a name, date and size.
Click the Grid view icon button and look that tiles return.
items.needs: an account with a few files
items.note: These are icon-only buttons; their names come from the title and aria labels.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > search box (Search files and projects)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the box that says Search files and projects and type part of a file name.
Wait a moment; the list narrows to matching names.
Clear the box and look that all files return. A search with no match shows No matches.
items.needs: an account with several named files

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Images / Videos / Documents (tabs)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click Documents, then Images, then Videos in the row of tabs.
Look that each tab shows only that file type.
Click All to return to everything.
items.needs: an account with an image, a video and a document

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Uploads / Generated files (tabs)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click Uploads, then Generated files in the row of tabs.
Look that each tab shows only files from that source.
Click All to return to everything.
items.needs: an account with both uploaded and generated files
items.note: Only upload and generated origins are filters. No connector or provider filter was found in LibraryView.tsx.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > sort button (shows Modified) > Name / Size / Type
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the sort button at the top right of the filter row (it shows Modified on wide screens).
Choose Name, then Size, then Type from the menu.
Look that the order changes each time; Modified sorts newest first.
items.needs: an account with several files of different names, sizes and types
items.note: On narrow screens only the icon shows; its name is Sort by plus the current option.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > (row) Actions for <file name> > Add to project
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
On a document row, click the three-dot button labelled Actions for <file name>.
Click Add to project. A dialog titled Add to project opens.
Click a project in the list, then open that project and look for the file.
items.needs: a document file in the Library and at least one project (the dialog says you have no projects if none exist)
items.note: The menu item appears only for document types the app accepts as project files.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > (row) Actions for <file name> > Add to chat
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Actions for <file name> button on a file row, then Add to chat.
Look that a new chat opens with the file attached in the message box.
Alternatively, in any chat click the + button, then Add from library, then Attach <file name>.
items.needs: a file in the Library
items.note: The attach row label is built as Attach <file name> in code.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > (row) Actions for <file name> > Open chat
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Click the Actions for <file name> button on a file that came from a chat.
Click Open chat.
Look that the chat the file came from opens.
items.needs: a file that was created inside a chat (an uploaded or generated file from a conversation)
items.note: The item is shown only when the file has a conversation id.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > the line under the Library heading (storage used)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Read the small line under the Library heading, for example 'X of Y file storage used'.
Read the second line about file downloads used this month if it is shown.
Upload or delete a file, return to Library, and look that the number changes.
items.needs: a signed-in account (the numbers come from the account's plan)
items.note: The line is shown only when the server returns a storage figure; the allowance part is shown only when a limit is returned.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Recently deleted (trash icon) > Restore
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Open a file's Actions for <file name> menu and click Delete; confirm in the dialog.
Click the trash icon labelled Recently deleted in the filter row.
Open the file's Actions menu, click Restore, then return to All and look that the file is back.
items.needs: a file in the Library that you are willing to delete and restore

labels.text: Deleted files wait here for 30 days before they are removed for good.

items.note: Delete asks for confirmation first; the copy says deleted files stay restorable for 30 days.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Recently deleted (for Kept until); a file row that cannot load (for the unavailable message)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar, then the trash icon labelled Recently deleted.
Look at each deleted file's line for Kept until and a date.
For a file whose content cannot be loaded, look for the line This file is unavailable right now. Try again later, or remove this entry.
items.needs: a deleted file (for Kept until); a file whose stored copy is missing (for the unavailable message), which is hard to set up

labels.text: This file is unavailable right now. Try again later, or remove this entry.

items.note: No word 'expired' is shown; the expired state appears as Kept until and as the unavailable message. The unavailable case is hard to reproduce on purpose.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a PDF row
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a PDF file row.
Look for the in-app PDF reader filling the viewer, instead of a download.
items.needs: a PDF file in the Library
items.note: The PDF reader is an iframe with test id library-pdf-reader and no visible label; the row opens the viewer only when the file is previewable.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a .txt row
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a plain-text file row.
Look for the text shown in a readable preformatted block inside the viewer.
items.needs: a plain-text file in the Library
items.note: The Library text view is a plain pre block (FileTextPreview.tsx). A separate viewer under Project settings also shows text (FilePreviewModal.tsx).

items.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Files > Preview <file name>
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar and open a project that has a Markdown file in its Files.
Open its Project settings dialog and scroll to the section titled Files.
Click Preview on the Markdown file row.
Look for headings and formatting rendered as Markdown, not raw # and ** characters.
items.needs: a project with a Markdown file in Files
items.note: The Library viewer shows Markdown as plain text, not formatted. The control that opens Project settings was not found in the code, so the step to open it is unverified.

items.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Files > Preview <file name>
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar and open a project that has a source-code file in its Files.
Open its Project settings dialog and go to the section titled Files.
Click Preview on the source-code file row.
Look for the code shown with syntax colouring for its language.
items.needs: a project with a source-code file in Files
items.note: The code view is in FilePreviewModal.tsx; the Library text view does not colour syntax. The path to Project settings is unverified.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Images > click an image row
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Images tab.
Click an image row.
Look for the image shown in the viewer with its file name as the alt text and a zoom group in the top bar.
items.needs: an image file in the Library

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Videos > click a video row
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Videos tab.
Click a video row.
Look for a video player with playback controls in the viewer, and press play.
items.needs: a video file in the Library

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a spreadsheet row
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a spreadsheet file row (for example .xlsx or .csv).
Look for the sheet shown as a table with a header row and data rows.
items.needs: a spreadsheet file in the Library
items.note: The table is drawn in FileTextPreview.tsx; the Project settings > Files preview also reaches it. The Library path is inferred from code, not traced to a spreadsheet type.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a .docx row
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a Word (.docx) file row.
Look for the document text shown in the viewer, formatted as text.
items.needs: a .docx file in the Library
items.note: The text is extracted on the server (file-text-preview.ts), so layout and images are not kept.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Images > click an image row, then use the Zoom group in the viewer top bar
steps: Open an image from Library > Images as in S25.05.
Look at the top bar of the viewer for the group labelled Zoom with the percentage shown.
Click Zoom in and Zoom out, and watch the percentage and the image size change.
Look for the buttons to stop at their limits (disabled).
items.needs: an image file in the Library
items.note: Zoom appears only for images; the group has no visible label, only an aria-label of Zoom.

items.needs: a file in the Library
items.note: The Library viewer has no full-screen control. ArtifactPreview.tsx has a button with title Fullscreen and aria-label Enter fullscreen / Exit fullscreen (lines 2939 and 3568), but the path from Library to that panel was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > click any previewable file row > Download button in the viewer top bar
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click a file row that opens the viewer, such as an image or PDF.
In the top bar, click the download icon (aria-label Download <file name>).
Look for the browser saving the original file with its own name and type.
items.needs: a file in the Library
items.note: The top-bar button has only an icon and an aria-label; the visible words Download to view appear only when inline preview is unavailable.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a PDF or .docx row > Download as text button in the viewer top bar
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab and open a PDF or Word file so the text loads.
Hover the icon button in the top bar; its title is Download as text.
Click it and look for a .txt file saved with the extracted text.
items.needs: a PDF or .docx file in the Library
items.note: The button shows only when the text is loaded and the file is not already text/*.

items.needs: a file with text in the Library
items.note: Searched LibraryView.tsx, FileTextPreview.tsx and FilePreviewModal.tsx for copy controls and user-select rules: no copy button or copy action found. Only the browser's own selection may apply.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > click a file row whose inline preview fails (no inline preview)
steps: Sign in, then click Library in the sidebar.
Click a file row that cannot be shown inline.
Look for the text Preview isn’t available for this file inline. with a Download to view button.
Click Download to view and check that the file downloads.
items.needs: a file with no inline preview (for example a .zip)
items.note: Library rows open the viewer only when the file is previewable, so the fallback may show only if a preview fails to load; the Project settings viewer shows Preview is not available for this file type. instead (FilePreviewModal.tsx:440).

items.where: Chat > send a prompt that asks for a document or an HTML page > the card in the assistant reply > "Open artifact"
steps: Sign in and open Chat.
Ask for a short document or a small HTML page, for example "write a one-page HTML landing page".
Wait for the reply. A card for the artifact appears under the reply.
Click the card, or its "Open artifact" button.
Compare: the artifact opens in the viewer with its content.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The card list is labelled "Artifacts" in InlineArtifactCards.tsx; the Code-line line numbers are stale but the feature is present.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact card > read the title at the top of the viewer header
steps: Ask Chat for an artifact, then wait for the card.
Read the title on the card.
Click the card to open the viewer.
Compare: the viewer header shows the same title.
For the fallback, open an artifact with no title and look for "Untitled" in the header.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The title is set in the viewer through More artifact actions > Rename; the fallback word "Untitled" is in ArtifactPreview.tsx. Whether a card shows the fallback was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact card > the muted line under the viewer title
steps: Ask Chat for an HTML page, a document and a spreadsheet, in three replies.
Open each artifact card in turn.
Look at the muted line under the title in the viewer header.
Compare: the kind shows as a label such as "HTML", or as an extension label such as "CSV" or "MD".
Look at the card: its type label is taken from the same source.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The card-side label was not read in full; the extension labels come from artifactExtensionLabel in ArtifactLabels.tsx.

items.where: Chat > ask for an artifact > watch the card and viewer while the reply is still streaming > "Writing…"
steps: Ask for a long document so the reply takes time.
While the reply is still arriving, look at the artifact card or viewer.
Compare: the state shows "Writing…".
Wait until the reply ends and check the state changes away from "Writing…".
Stop the reply part way (Stop control) and look for the interrupted notice in the viewer.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: "Writing…" is confirmed; the stopped notice text and any failed state were not read, so the exact finished and failed wording is unknown.

items.where: Chat > an assistant reply with an artifact card > "Open artifact"
steps: Open a conversation that has an artifact card.
Click the card or its "Open artifact" control.
Compare: the viewer opens and shows the artifact content.
Open the "Artifacts" panel from the "Artifacts" button and open an artifact from the list.
Compare: the same content shows in the viewer.
items.needs: a conversation with an artifact

items.where: Chat > open an artifact > top-right X "Close artifact viewer"
steps: Open an artifact in the viewer.
Click the X button at the top right of the viewer, labelled "Close artifact viewer".
Compare: the viewer hides.
Click the "Artifacts" button or the artifact card again.
Compare: the same artifact is still listed and opens again.
items.needs: a conversation with an artifact
items.note: The close button for the whole panel is "Close artifacts panel"; the no-deletion behaviour was not verified by reading the delete path.

items.where: Chat > "Artifacts" button (panel toggle) or the artifact card in the reply > "Open artifact"
steps: Open an artifact, then close the viewer with "Close artifact viewer".
Click the "Artifacts" button (tooltip "Artifacts") to open the panel.
Pick the same artifact again.
Reload the page with the browser reload, then open the conversation again.
Compare: the artifact opens again after the reload.
items.needs: a conversation with an artifact
items.note: The panel toggle location in the chat header was not confirmed in the code read; the artifact card path is confirmed.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact (card "Open artifact" or the "Artifacts" button) > the panel appears to the right of the conversation
steps: Ask for an artifact on a wide window, then click "Open artifact" on its card.
Look at the screen.
Compare: the conversation stays visible on the left and the artifact panel is docked on the right.
Click "Close artifacts panel" to hide it and check the conversation fills the window again.
items.needs: a wide window (desktop layout)
items.note: The docked width applies only in the desktop layout (ArtifactsPanel.tsx sets width only when layout is desktop); on narrower widths it is a sheet.

items.where: Chat > docked artifact panel > the left edge handle "Resize artifacts panel"
steps: Open an artifact so the docked panel shows.
Drag the thin handle on the panel's left edge left or right with the mouse.
Compare: the panel gets wider or narrower.
Click the handle, then press the Left or Right arrow keys.
Close the panel, open it again, and compare the width.
items.needs: a wide window (desktop layout)
items.note: Keyboard resizing is in apps/web/features/chat/components/SidePanelResizeHandle.tsx; I did not find a storage call there that keeps the width, so whether the width is kept after reopening is unknown.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact > header button "Expand"
steps: Open an artifact in the docked panel.
Click the expand icon in the viewer header, tooltip "Expand".
Compare: the artifact fills the screen.
Click the same control, now "Exit fullscreen", to return.
Compare: the layout returns to the docked panel.
items.needs: an artifact open in the viewer
items.note: The button's aria-label is "Enter fullscreen"/"Exit fullscreen" and its tooltip is "Expand".

items.where: Chat > open an HTML or SVG artifact > More artifact actions > "Open in new tab"
steps: Ask for an HTML page artifact and open it.
Click the "More artifact actions" button (the three-dot button).
Click "Open in new tab".
Compare: a new window or tab opens showing the rendered page.
In the Electron desktop app, check the new window shows the rendered artifact.
items.needs: an HTML or SVG artifact
items.note: The window handling is in apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts (blob pages are allowed as detached pages); the artifact-specific line numbers in the Code line were not found there.

items.where: Chat > a conversation with two or more artifacts > the "Artifacts" panel > click another artifact
steps: Ask Chat for two artifacts in one conversation (for example a document and an HTML page).
Open the "Artifacts" panel.
Click the first artifact, then click the second.
Compare: the viewer switches to the second artifact without closing the panel.
Use the tabs or the list to switch back to the first.
items.needs: a conversation with two artifacts

items.where: Chat > a conversation with two or more artifacts > the tab row above the viewer (each tab shows its title)
steps: Ask Chat for two or more artifacts in one conversation.
Open the "Artifacts" panel.
Look for a tab per artifact in the top row. Each tab shows the artifact's title.
Ask for another artifact while the first is still writing.
Compare: the one being written also appears as a tab.
items.needs: a conversation with two or more artifacts
items.note: Tabs show artifact titles, so no fixed tab label exists. Tabs render from ArtifactTab in ArtifactsPanel.tsx; whether a tab appears for the one being written is not confirmed by reading the code.

items.where: Chat > open an HTML, React or SVG artifact > the two icon buttons "Preview" and "Source" in the viewer header
steps: Open an HTML page artifact in the viewer.
Click the icon button labelled "Preview".
Compare: the rendered page shows.
Click the icon button labelled "Source".
Compare: the code of the artifact shows.
items.needs: an HTML, React or SVG artifact
items.note: The two buttons are icon-only; their words are aria-label and title.

items.where: Chat > open a document or code artifact (latest version) > header "Edit" button, or More artifact actions > "Edit source"
steps: Open the latest version of a document or code artifact.
Click "Edit" in the viewer header (or More artifact actions > "Edit source").
Type a change in the text.
Click "Save" (tooltip "Save as a new version").
Compare: a new version is created, and the version chip shows one more version.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, an artifact written in chat
items.note: The Save button's tooltip is "Save as a new version" in the same file.

items.where: Chat > open an older version of an artifact, or a PDF, Word or image artifact: the header has no "Edit" button
steps: Open an artifact that has at least two versions.
Use "Previous version" to move to an older version.
Compare: the "Edit" button is not shown and the content cannot be changed there.
Open a PDF or image artifact and check that no "Edit" button appears.
items.needs: an artifact with at least two versions
items.note: The rule is in ArtifactPreview.tsx (canEditSource: panel variant, stored, latest version, not PDF, DOCX or image). Shared-copy read-only was not traced.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact with edits > the version chip in the muted line under the title > "Version history"
steps: Open an artifact that has been edited so it has several versions.
Read the chip, for example showing "Version N of M" in the header.
Click it, or the "Version history" control.
Pick another "Version N" from the list.
Compare: the viewer shows that version and the chip number changes.
items.needs: an artifact with several versions (edit it first)
items.note: The chip text comes from an aria-label template in ArtifactPreview.tsx; the list rows read "Version N" in ArtifactVersionHistory.tsx.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact with several versions > "Previous version" and "Next version" arrow buttons beside the version chip
steps: Open an artifact with at least two versions.
Click "Previous version".
Compare: the viewer shows the earlier version and the chip number goes down by one.
Click "Next version" to step forward.
Compare: the chip returns to the later version.
items.needs: an artifact with several versions (edit it first)

items.where: Chat > open an older version (Previous version) > More artifact actions > "Restore version" with the number, then confirm "Restore"
steps: Open an artifact with several versions and step back with "Previous version".
Click "More artifact actions", then the item that starts with "Restore version" and shows the number.
In the dialog, confirm with "Restore".
Compare: that version becomes the current one.
Open "Version history" and check the versions in between are still listed.
items.needs: an artifact with several versions (edit it first)
items.note: The menu label is a template that adds the version number; the confirm dialog title is "Restore version N?".

items.where: Chat > open an artifact in the panel > More artifact actions > "Duplicate"
steps: Open an artifact in the docked panel.
Click "More artifact actions" and choose "Duplicate".
Compare: the toast "Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original." appears.
Edit the copy, then open the original.
Compare: the original is unchanged.
items.needs: a stored artifact in the panel
items.note: The copy appears in the same panel as the current artifact; where it is listed was not traced.

items.where: Chat > open a text or code artifact > More artifact actions > "Save to Library"
steps: Open an artifact that is not an image, PDF or Word file.
Click "More artifact actions" and choose "Save to Library".
Compare: the toast "Saved to your Library" appears.
Open Library from the app's navigation (the Library page is at /chat/library).
Compare: the artifact is listed in the Library.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The navigation label for Library was not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact > More artifact actions > group "Save to project" > pick the project name
steps: Make sure you have at least one project (Chat > Projects).
Open an artifact and click "More artifact actions".
Find the group "Save to project" and click a project name.
Compare: the artifact is added as a source of that project.
Open that project and check the file is listed.
items.needs: a paid account or a Free account with a project
items.note: The menu only shows when the account has projects; the saved item is a copy of the file, not a move.

items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: Searched the artifact viewer, artifacts panel and apps/web/features/library for a continue, handoff or new-chat control on an artifact; found only stageLibraryItemForNewChat in apps/web/features/library/lib/library-chat-handoff.ts used by the Library view, and no label that matches an artifact taking a new chat.

items.where: Chat > open an artifact > header "Download" button > pick a format such as "Download as HTML"
steps: Open an artifact in the viewer.
Click the "Download" button in the header.
Look at the menu of formats: for example "Download as HTML", "Download as Markdown", "Download source" and, for a document, "Download as Word (.docx)" or "Download as PDF".
Pick one, then check the file saved to the downloads folder opens in that format.
For a CSV-type artifact, check "Download as CSV" is shown.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The menu items depend on the artifact type; the header button's aria-label is "Download artifact".

items.where: Chat > open an artifact > header "Copy" button
steps: Open an artifact in the viewer.
Click the "Copy" button in the header.
Compare: the button changes to "Copied" to confirm.
Paste into a text editor.
Compare: the pasted text is the artifact's own content.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account

items.where: Open an artifact in the chat artifact viewer > click the Publish button (globe icon) in the viewer header, or open the More menu > Publish. After publishing, the bar under the header shows the link, a Copy link button, and a Who can open this menu. To take a link down: Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts > Unpublish artifact.
steps: Send a message that makes an artifact, then open it from the chat card so the viewer opens.
Click the globe Publish button in the viewer header (or More menu > Publish) and wait for the Published message.
Click Copy link in the bar that appears under the header and check that a Link copied message shows.
Open the Who can open this menu and check the three choices: Anyone with the link, Everyone in this workspace, Only people you invite.
Open Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts, click Unpublish on the artifact, then click Unpublish artifact in the confirm dialog, and check the row is gone and the link stops working.
items.needs: a signed-in account and an artifact that can be published (not a file type that is blocked from publishing); a second workspace member if testing Everyone in this workspace
items.note: Taking a link down is only in Settings > Shared links, not in the viewer; the Settings entry path was confirmed from the section file and its heading, but the path from the first screen to Settings was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts. Each row shows its audience label. The same audience choice also appears in the artifact viewer under Who can open this after publishing.
steps: Publish an artifact (see S26.31) so that it has a link.
Open Settings > Shared links and find the Published artifacts list.
Check the audience text on the artifact row: Anyone with the link, Everyone in this workspace or Only people you invite.
Open the same artifact in the viewer and check that the Who can open this menu shows the same choice.
Compare with Expected: each place shows the same visibility state.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one published artifact; a workspace for the Everyone in this workspace choice
items.note: No explicit Private label was found: an artifact that is not published shows only the Publish button, so the private state is seen as the absence of a link.

items.where: Open an artifact that fails when it runs (for example an HTML artifact whose script throws an error) in the artifact viewer. The viewer replaces the preview with an error panel with the buttons View source and Retry.
steps: Ask the chat for an HTML artifact whose script throws an error on load, such as one that calls an undefined function.
Open the artifact in the viewer and wait for the preview to load.
Look for the error panel: the title says it could not be rendered, with the error text below it.
Click View source and check that the code tab opens.
Go back, click Retry, and check that the error panel shows again or the preview renders.
items.needs: an artifact that fails to render (you must make one in the chat)
items.note: The panel title in the file is written with an HTML apostrophe entity, which shows as an ordinary apostrophe on the page; the error text itself comes from the sandbox page as a Render error prefix.

items.where: Open a React artifact in the artifact viewer. While the runtime loads, the preview shows the text Loading React… and a spinner with the label Loading the preview.
steps: Ask the chat for a React component artifact.
Open it in the viewer and look right away for the spinner and the text Loading React….
Wait until the component appears, and check the loading text is gone.
To see a failed load, the tester must block the React script address with a network blocker; without that, the failure cannot be produced by a normal user step.
Compare with Expected: loading is shown, and a failed load shows an error with the message The React runtime could not be loaded from.
items.needs: a React artifact; a network blocker or an offline setting to see a failed load

labels.text: The React runtime could not be loaded from

items.note: The failed-load message is produced in the sandbox page only when the React script fails to load; the loading text shows only briefly on a fast connection.

items.where: Gallery (public route /gallery): click an artifact card to open its drawer, then click Open chat. The Open chat link appears only when the artifact has a source conversation.
steps: Open the gallery at the /gallery page.
Click an artifact card to open its drawer.
Look for the Open chat link in the drawer header area.
Click Open chat and check that the conversation that made the artifact opens.
Compare with Expected: the user lands in the originating chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a gallery artifact that came from a conversation
items.note: The in-app link that leads to the gallery was not found; only the /gallery route and its drawer were confirmed, and the library entry point was not checked.

items.where: Chat: send a message that asks for an artifact (for example an HTML page). The artifact panel opens while the reply is still writing, shows the status Writing… and the title Generating artifact, and the code updates as it arrives.
steps: Type a request such as Make a one-page HTML landing page and send it.
Watch the artifact panel open while the reply is still being written.
Check the status text Writing… next to the artifact title.
Watch the code body scroll and grow line by line.
Compare with Expected: the artifact view updates live until the reply is finished, then the status changes.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can send chat messages
items.note: The title Generating artifact shows only until the real title arrives, so the tester may see it briefly.

items.where: Chat > open a conversation that has a document > the document card in the reply shows its title. Open it: the viewer header shows the same title.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has a document made by Claude.
Look at the document card in the reply: it shows the document title.
Click the card to open the document in the side panel.
Look at the viewer title. Compare with Expected: a title shows, and a document with no title shows Untitled.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: The fallback text is Untitled in the card and viewer; the card uses artifactTitle() and the viewer uses artifact.title || 'Untitled'.

items.where: Chat > open a document > Preview tab > Edit (Edit document). Or More menu > Edit source. Then Save or Cancel.
steps: Open a document made in chat in the side panel. Stay on the Preview tab.
Click Edit in the header (or open the More menu and choose Edit source).
Change the text in the editor.
Click Save. Compare with Expected: the text is saved as a new version and the viewer shows it.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat (not a code artifact)
items.note: Edit opens the rich editor, which falls back to a plain Markdown text view for content it cannot keep (math, footnotes, raw HTML); there is no separate raw-source toggle found for normal Markdown documents.

items.where: Chat > open a document > Preview tab > Edit > select text > formatting toolbar: Bold, Italic, Link.
steps: Open a document in the side panel and click Edit.
Select some words.
Click Bold, then Italic, then Link (Link asks for a web address and adds it to the selection).
Look at the text. Compare with Expected: bold and italic show, and the link is set. Underline was not found in the toolbar.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: Underline has no control in DocumentFormattingToolbar.tsx, and the editor extensions list did not show it, so the Expected underline part is not met by the code.

items.where: Chat > open a document > Preview tab > Edit > formatting toolbar: Bulleted list, Numbered list, Checklist.
steps: Open a document in the side panel and click Edit.
Click Bulleted list, then Numbered list, and type items.
Click Checklist and type a few items.
Tick a checklist box in the Preview tab. Compare with Expected: all three list types appear and checkboxes toggle.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: Checklist ticks in the Preview tab save as a new version after a short pause, according to CHECKLIST_COMMIT_IDLE_MS.

items.where: Chat > open a document > Preview tab > Edit > formatting toolbar: Insert table.
steps: Open a document in the side panel and click Edit.
Click Insert table in the formatting toolbar.
Type text into the table cells.
Look at the table. Compare with Expected: a table is inserted and it can be edited.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: Table rendering is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/remarkPlugins.ts; the tester should check that cell editing and row/column controls exist, since the code only shows the insert control.

items.needs: a document that has an image link
items.note: Images render in the Markdown preview (MarkdownContent.tsx renders img and asks approval for external hosts), but no insert-image control was found in DocumentFormattingToolbar.tsx or ArtifactPreview.tsx; searched for Insert image and label="Image" under apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts and packages/ui/unified-chat.

items.where: Chat > open a document > Preview tab > Edit > formatting toolbar: Code block (also under the Text style menu).
steps: Open a document in the side panel and click Edit.
Click Code block in the toolbar and type a few lines of code.
Click Save and go to the Preview tab.
Look at the code block. Compare with Expected: it shows as a code block. Math has no toolbar control.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: Math equations have no insert control; remarkMath is enabled for rendering only, and the editor says math documents open as Markdown.

items.where: Chat > open a document with 3 or more headings > Preview tab > Outline.
steps: Open a document that has at least 3 headings in the side panel.
Stay on the Preview tab and click Outline.
Click one heading in the list.
Look at the page. Compare with Expected: the view jumps to that section.
items.needs: a document with 3 or more headings
items.note: The Outline control appears only when the document has at least 3 headings (OUTLINE_MIN_HEADINGS = 3).

items.where: Chat > open a document > Preview tab > Edit > type text > look at the header next to Save.
steps: Open a document in the side panel and click Edit.
Type a sentence.
Look at the header next to Save: it shows Draft kept on this device, or Draft not kept.
Click Save and check that a new version is listed in Version history. Compare with Expected: the document saves on its own and shows saving and saved states.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: The code keeps a local draft on the device and shows Draft kept on this device or Draft not kept; there is no Saving or Saved state, and a version is created only on Save (or a checklist pause).

items.where: Chat > open a document with more than one version > side panel header: Undo last change and Redo change buttons (also in the More menu as Undo and Redo).
steps: Open a saved document that has been edited at least once, in the side panel.
Click Edit, change text, and click Save so a new version exists.
Click the Undo last change button in the header.
Click Redo change, and compare with Expected: the previous text returns and then the newer text returns.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document with more than one saved version
items.note: Undo and Redo step through saved versions, not each keystroke, and show only in the side panel for saved documents; keyboard undo inside the editor was not verified.

items.where: Chat > open a document with more than one version > Version history button in the header > click Version 1 (or any version) > Restore.
steps: Open a document that has several versions in the side panel.
Click the Version history button in the header.
Read the list: each version shows its number, Latest on the newest, and its date and time.
Click a version to open it, click Restore, confirm Restore in the dialog, and compare with Expected: the restored text shows and a new version is added.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document with several versions
items.note: The date and time use the browser locale (toLocaleString, medium date and short time).

items.where: Chat > open a document > Download (the Download artifact button) > Download as Word (.docx).
steps: Open a document in the side panel.
Click the Download button in the header (aria label Download artifact).
Click Download as Word (.docx).
Open the saved file in Word or Pages. Compare with Expected: a .docx file with the document text opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: The item appears only for text documents (isTextDocument).

items.where: Chat > open a document > Download (the Download artifact button) > Download as PDF.
steps: Open a document in the side panel.
Click the Download button in the header.
Click Download as PDF.
Open the saved PDF. Compare with Expected: a PDF file with the document text opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: The same label also appears for deck export; for a text document it is the document PDF export.

items.where: Chat > open a document > Download (the Download artifact button) > Download as Markdown.
steps: Open a document in the side panel.
Click the Download button in the header.
Click Download as Markdown.
Open the saved .md file in a text editor. Compare with Expected: the file is Markdown text with the document content.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a document made in chat
items.note: For a Markdown document the file contains the document text as is; for other artifacts it wraps the code in a fenced block.

items.where: Artifact panel > Source (tab) > More artifact actions > Edit source
steps: Start a chat and ask for a short code file, for example a Python script, so a code artifact opens in the side panel.
Click the Source tab (icon with title Source) in the artifact header.
Click More artifact actions, then Edit source.
Change a line in the code editor, then click Save (title Save as a new version).
Compare: the edited code stays, and the version counter shows a new version (for example v2/2).
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Edit source only appears on the latest version and not for PDF, DOCX or image artifacts; the Save text is hidden on a narrow panel, so use its icon (title Save as a new version).

items.where: Chat > open an HTML artifact in the side panel > Preview (eye icon)
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Ask for a single-page web page in HTML, such as a page with a button and a text box.
Open the artifact from the chat so it shows in the side panel.
Make sure the Preview (eye icon) is selected in the artifact header.
Click the button or type in the text box on the page; compare: the page is live and responds.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Without NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN the code uses a fallback frame where scripts may not run (apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:336-347), so the live result depends on the build; the plan says the sandbox switch-on is unfinished.

items.where: Chat > open a React artifact in the side panel > Preview (eye icon)
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Ask for a React component, such as a counter with two buttons.
Open the artifact in the side panel and make sure Preview (eye icon) is selected.
Click the buttons; compare: the component renders live and its state changes.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Same sandbox dependency as S28.10: without NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN the fallback frame may not run React scripts (apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:336-347).

items.where: Chat > open an HTML artifact that throws an error > Preview > error message in the panel
steps: Ask for an HTML page whose script calls a function that does not exist as soon as it loads.
Open the artifact in the side panel with Preview selected.
Look for the message This artifact couldn't be rendered. with a detail line under it.
Click Retry to reload, or View source to open the code; compare: a way to recover is shown.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Expected says overlay; the code replaces the preview area with a message panel (data-testid artifact-render-error) and also writes the error into the frame (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:374-380). The message text is written with an HTML entity for the apostrophe.

items.where: Artifact panel > More artifact actions > Refresh preview
steps: Open an HTML or React artifact in the side panel with Preview selected.
Click More artifact actions.
Click Refresh preview.
Compare: the preview reloads and shows the same content again, with any error message cleared.
items.needs: none
items.note: The same action is also an icon button with aria-label Refresh preview in a different header layout.

items.needs: none
items.note: No control named Restart or a restart of the runtime was found. I searched Restart and restart in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts, apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts and apps/desktop/src. Closest are Refresh preview (ArtifactPreview.tsx, which only bumps a refresh key) and Refresh data (apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/LiveArtifactControls.tsx, which reloads connected-app data, not the runtime).

items.where: Artifact panel > Download artifact (button) > Download source (.<language>)
steps: Open a code artifact, such as a Python script, in the side panel.
Click the Download artifact button (download icon) in the header.
If a menu opens, click Download source (.<extension>), where the extension matches the artifact language.
Open the saved file and compare: it holds the same code as the artifact.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu item text is built as Download source followed by the file extension in brackets; the button opens a menu only when the artifact has more than one download option.

items.where: Chat > Artifacts (button, title Artifacts) > Download all
steps: Create at least two artifacts in a chat, such as a code file and an HTML page.
Click the Artifacts button to open the artifacts panel.
Click Download all (title Download all artifacts as zip).
Open the downloaded artifacts.zip and compare: it contains the artifacts from the panel.
items.needs: two or more artifacts in one account
items.note: The button shows only when there are more than one artifacts, and the zip holds every artifact as a flat set (apps/web/features/chat/utils/downloadArtifacts.ts:157-162), not a project tree; the first step to open the panel was taken from the code's button title, not checked on screen.

items.where: Artifact panel > Publish (button) or More artifact actions > Publish
steps: Open a finished HTML or document artifact in the side panel.
Click Publish (on a narrow panel use More artifact actions, then Publish).
If a dialog asks about sharing, read it and confirm; the audience choice includes Anyone with the link.
Look for the message Published · link copied to clipboard, then open the link in a private window.
Compare: the shared artifact opens without signing in.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a private window for the last step
items.note: The dialog and audience option text were found in the file, but I did not confirm the exact order of the dialog and the toast.

items.where: Artifact panel > Version history (version counter, for example v2/2) > Restore
steps: Open an artifact that has at least two versions, for example after one Save in Edit source.
Click the version counter button (title Version history).
In the version list, click Restore on an earlier version.
Click Restore in the confirmation dialog titled Restore version N?.
Compare: the content goes back to the earlier version and the counter shows one more version.
items.needs: an artifact with two or more versions
items.note: Restore adds the old version as a new latest version; Undo and Redo in More artifact actions also step between edits.

items.needs: none
items.note: No insert-chart button, menu or dialog found. Charts are built by the assistant only when asked for an .xlsx workbook: managed-workbook-builder and managed-office-file-service take a per-sheet chart (bar, line, pie) from the sheet's own cells. Searched 'Insert chart', 'Add chart', 'Chart type' and 'chart' in the chat and artifact files.

items.where: Artifact panel for a slide deck with a chart > Edit chart data > Chart type
steps: Ask the assistant for a slide deck that contains a chart, and wait for the deck to appear in the artifact panel.
Click the button labelled Edit chart data (appears only when the deck has a chart).
Open the Chart type select and choose Line, then Pie, then Bar.
Look at whether the chart preview changes to the chosen type, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a request to the assistant for a slide deck with a chart
items.note: The selector exists only in the slide-deck chart editor, not for charts in a spreadsheet or the chart artifact. Options are Bar, Line and Pie.

items.where: Artifact panel for a slide deck with a chart > Edit chart data
steps: Open a slide deck that contains a chart, as in S29.18.
Click Edit chart data.
Read the table of rows and columns (the first column is the label column, then one column per series).
Change a value, add or remove a row, and click the apply control; then compare the chart with Expected.
items.needs: a request to the assistant for a slide deck with a chart
items.note: The editor shows a table of data rows, not a cell range such as B2:B5; the spreadsheet workbook charts have no range editor.

items.where: Add attachment (+ button in the chat box) > Run code
steps: Open a chat with a model that supports code execution.
Click the + button labelled Add attachment next to the chat box.
Turn on the Run code item (it is greyed out when the model or plan does not allow it).
Send a request that analyses data, then look for the Code execution block under the reply, expand it, and compare its stdout, stderr and images with Expected.
items.needs: a model and plan that allow code execution; a data file to upload is useful
items.note: There is no separate Python analysis panel. Output appears as an expandable Code execution block (stdout, stderr, images); the code itself is not shown there as far as the code reveals. The Python Sandbox text in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json is a card label, not a panel.

items.where: Artifact panel for a spreadsheet > click a column heading
steps: Ask the assistant for a table or spreadsheet of results, and wait for it to open in the artifact panel.
Click a column heading once to sort ascending, again to sort descending, and a third time to clear the sort.
Watch the rows reorder and the heading's sort state change.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a request to the assistant that returns a spreadsheet artifact
items.note: The sortable table is the spreadsheet artifact (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx, aria-sort on column headers). The markdown table has no sorting. The headings have no visible sort words.

items.where: Artifact panel for a spreadsheet > Download (button) > Download generated file
steps: Ask the assistant for a spreadsheet (.xlsx) and wait for it to appear in the artifact panel.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download generated file in the menu, if it is listed.
Open the downloaded file in a spreadsheet app and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a request to the assistant that produces an .xlsx file
items.note: The menu item appears only when the artifact has a generated file manifest; the original evidence line moved in the code. No button builds an .xlsx from a sheet on demand.

items.where: Artifact panel for a spreadsheet > Download (button) > Download as CSV
steps: Open a spreadsheet, table or CSV artifact in the artifact panel.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download as CSV.
Open the file that downloads, and compare its rows and columns with the artifact.
items.needs: a request to the assistant for a table or spreadsheet

items.where: Chart artifact in the chat > PNG (button in the chart header)
steps: Ask the assistant for a chart, and wait for it to draw in the chat.
Click the button with the Download icon and the text PNG in the chart's header.
Open the downloaded PNG file.
Compare the picture with the chart on screen.
items.needs: a request to the assistant for a chart
items.note: Chart export is PNG only, with an accessible name Download <chart name> as PNG; no SVG or CSV export for charts was found.

items.where: Artifact panel for a document > Download (button) > Download as Word (.docx)
steps: Ask the assistant for a written report based on an analysis, and wait for the document artifact to open.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download as Word (.docx), then open the file; repeat with Download as PDF.
Compare the formatted file with the artifact text and with Expected.
items.needs: a request to the assistant for a report
items.note: No control turns an analysis into a report. Word and PDF are offered as downloads of a document artifact only. The line 'Writing report' is a progress label for research, not an export.

items.where: Artifact panel for a slide deck > Download (button) > Download as PDF
steps: Ask the assistant for a slide deck based on an analysis, and wait for the deck to open in the artifact panel.
Click the Download button (title Download) in the artifact header.
Click Download as PDF and open the file.
Compare with Expected, which asks for a .pptx slide deck.
items.needs: a request to the assistant for a slide deck
items.note: No pptx download item was found in the menus. Decks export only as PDF; a .pptx arrives only as a generated file through Download generated file, if the assistant made one. PptxFilePreview.tsx shows pptx files but does not download them.

items.where: New chat > ask the assistant for a PowerPoint deck (for example "Make a 3-slide PowerPoint deck about our release plan") > on the generated file card under the reply, click Download
steps: Click New chat (or press the command palette and choose New chat) to open an empty conversation.
Type a request that asks for a PowerPoint presentation with a few slide titles and bullets, then send it.
Wait for the reply to show a generated file card with a .pptx name.
Click the Download button on that card (its tooltip-style label is Download generated file).
Open the downloaded file in PowerPoint, Keynote or Preview and check it is a .pptx deck with the slide text you asked for. Compare with Expected: the user can download the deck as a .pptx file.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account (plan gating for office file creation not confirmed in code)
items.note: The plan's Code line is stale: the cited quoted code is not in apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts. The PPTX is created by the create_office_file chat tool (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts, pptxgenjs) and downloaded from the chat file card, not from an Export menu; no Export control was found in apps/desktop or apps/web. The exact prompt wording that triggers the tool and the Free-plan limit were not confirmed.

items.where: Library > open a text document artifact > its download menu > Download as PDF
steps: From the first screen after sign-in, click Library in the sidebar and open a saved text document (a document-type artifact).
Open the artifact's download menu in its preview (the menu that holds Download as HTML, Download as Markdown).
Click Download as PDF. The option appears only for document artifacts that are not Word or PDF files.
Compare with Expected: a PDF file should download. Also check Export as PDF in the library export menu, which lists PDF when the artifact allows it.
items.needs: a text document artifact (create one in chat first, or use an existing one)
items.note: Expected names Word, text and markdown inputs; the code offers PDF only for document artifacts, and the download menu trigger label was not confirmed. The quoted managed-office-file-service code moved and was not found.

items.needs: none
items.note: No spreadsheet-to-PDF option was found. The PDF options are only for document artifacts and presentations (ArtifactPreview.tsx), and the support page apps/web/content/support/artifacts.md says there is no spreadsheet export on web. Spreadsheet export offers Excel only (ArtifactRenderer.tsx). Searched for the PDF labels and for container-files.ts usage.

items.where: Library > open a presentation artifact > its download menu > Download as PDF
steps: From the first screen after sign-in, click Library in the sidebar and open a saved presentation (slide deck) artifact.
Open the artifact's download menu in its preview.
Click Download as PDF. The export runs through the local deck PDF code (presentation/deck-pdf) and shows the toast Preparing the PDF.
Compare with Expected: the PDF should download with one page per slide. Toast text: PDF downloaded.
items.needs: a presentation artifact (create a slide deck in chat first)
items.note: The audit's partial status refers to the E2B office template build script (apps/web/scripts/build-e2b-office-template.mjs), which is not needed for the deck export path found here. Page-per-slide layout was not checked.

items.where: New chat > attach a PDF with the attachment control in the message box > type a request for a summary > send
steps: From the first screen after sign-in, start a new chat.
Attach a PDF using the attachment control in the message box. The hidden file input is labelled File upload; its visible button label was not found.
Type a request such as Summarize this PDF, then send the message.
Compare with Expected: the answer should be a summary of the PDF content. A PDF attachment also opens a preview in the message.

Look at the activity bar: it changes to "Research stopped" with "(stopped by you)".
To cancel before searching, click "Cancel" on the "Research plan" card instead.
Check the run no longer updates and the bar says it was stopped or cancelled.
items.needs: a research run in progress
items.note: The composer stop button is the run stop path I found; I did not confirm it routes to the research cancel call.

items.where: Stop a running research, then open the "Report" tab in the research side panel and read the banner at the top of the report
steps: Start a run and press the stop button while it is searching.
Open the "Sources" button under the answer, then the "Report" tab.
Read the banner at the top of the report: "This report is" followed by the status and reason.
Check the report summarises what was gathered and says it is incomplete.
items.needs: a research run you can stop mid-way
items.note: The code never writes the word "partial"; the banner shows the status (interrupted or failed). A cancelled run stores gathered material with empty report text, so a readable partial report is confirmed only for runs cut short during synthesis.

items.where: "Sources" button under the answer > side panel "Report" tab (or "Library" tab > click a report)
steps: Finish a research run and click the "Sources" button under the answer.
Click the "Report" tab.
Check the title, the summary, the body and the sources at the end.
Click "Read report full screen" to open the reader view.
items.needs: a finished research run

items.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Contents" box above the report body
steps: Open a finished report with at least three headings in the "Report" tab.
Find the box labelled "Contents" above the body.
Click one heading in the list.
Check the page scrolls to that section.
items.needs: a finished report with three or more headings
items.note: The outline only appears when the report has at least three headings.

items.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > numbered citation markers in the report body, then the "Sources" list at the bottom
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Find a numbered citation marker in the text.
Click it and check the page jumps to the matching entry under "Sources" at the bottom.
Check that entry links to the web page.
items.needs: a finished report with citations
items.note: Whether the source entry opens the external page in a new tab was not verified from the code read.

items.where: "Research plan" card > "Format" > "Prose with comparison tables" (tables); charts appear in the report body when sources give comparable figures
steps: In the plan card, set "Format" to "Prose with comparison tables".
Press "Start research" and wait for the report.
Open the "Report" tab and look for a comparison table in the body.
Look for a drawn chart in the body; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid plan with Deep Research on; a question whose sources include comparable figures for charts
items.note: Charts depend on the model writing a mermaid chart block from the sources; the chart is rendered by the code block renderer, so it is not guaranteed for every report.

items.where: Research sources button (title "Research sources") or a "Sources" button under an answer > side panel "Library" tab
steps: Open the research side panel with the "Research sources" button or a "Sources" button.
Click the "Library" tab.
Read the list of past reports: title, date, source count.
Click a report to reopen it.
items.needs: at least one saved research report; if none, the tab shows "No reports yet"

items.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Run again" in the report header
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Click "Run again" in the report header.
Watch a new run start in the chat with the same question.
Check the new run uses current sources and produces a new report.
items.needs: a finished report that has its question saved

labels.text: Run this research again for current sources

items.note: The control says "Run again", not "Refresh"; the button only appears when the report has a question and the host supplies the action.

items.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Markdown", "PDF" or "Word" buttons in the report header
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Click "PDF", "Word" or "Markdown" in the header.
Check a file downloads and opens with the title and body.
If it fails, read the error text under the header.
items.needs: a finished report

items.where: Research panel > "Report" tab > "Artifact" button in the report header; or type a request in "Ask a follow-up about this report"
steps: Open a finished report in the "Report" tab.
Click "Artifact" in the report header (it hands the report to the artifacts panel).
Or type "interactive web page" wording in "Ask a follow-up about this report" and click "Ask".
Check the result is an interactive page as in Expected.
items.needs: a finished report

labels.text: Ask a follow-up about this report

items.note: The header "Artifact" button creates a Markdown artifact from the report, not an interactive page; an interactive page depends on the wording of the request. The follow-up box appears only when the host supplies it.

items.where: Bell icon at the top of the sidebar (label "Notifications") for results; the footer under the running research for the browser prompt
steps: Start a research run and switch to another tab or window.
If the footer shows, read "Get a notification when this research finishes" and click "Enable", then allow the browser prompt.
When the run ends, open the bell and look for "Research report ready" (or "Research did not finish").
Check the entry matches the run that finished.
items.needs: a browser that allows notifications; a finished or failed research run

labels.text: Get a notification when this research finishes

items.note: The browser footer is shown only when the "Reply ready" browser preference is on and permission is still undecided; the setting lives at Settings > Notifications > Reply ready.

items.where: "Research plan" card, above "Start research": the "Estimated cost" line and the "available right now" line
steps: Turn on Deep Research and send a question.
In the plan card read the line starting "Estimated cost:".
Read the line that says how much you have "available right now".
Compare with Expected; if it says the run may stop early, the warning appears in the same place.
items.needs: a paid account with credits
items.note: If no estimate can be made for the model, the line reads "A cost estimate is not available for this model." The running bar also shows "up to ~" a credit amount.

items.where: Chat > attachment menu > Research > send a research question > read the line that starts "Estimated cost" on the research plan card, just above "Start research"
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Open the attachment menu in the message box and click "Research" to turn research on.
Type a research question and send it.
When the plan card appears, read the line starting "Estimated cost: up to about" and the line under it starting "You have" and "available right now".
Compare with Expected: the remaining amount is shown before you click "Start research".
items.needs: a signed-in account; the "You have ... available right now" line appears only when usage data loads, and a line saying the estimate is not available appears for models with no estimate
items.note: The plan item asks for runs or credits, but the code shows only credits ("available right now"), not a run count; the line is shown only on the editable plan card before the run starts. I did not confirm the visible label of the attachment menu trigger button, so step 2 names the menu without a label.

items.where: Chat screen > ask a question that needs current web sources > read the answer; a small chip with a site name or domain sits right after the claim
steps: Sign in and open a new chat from the chat screen.
Type a question that needs current facts, such as a recent news topic, and send it.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Look for a small rounded chip with a site name after a sentence in the answer.
Compare with Expected: the claim should carry a marker that names its source.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources (web search must be on for the chat)
items.note: The chip is built from the citation link in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx; the chip text is the site name from the source, so no fixed visible label exists for it.

items.where: Answer with web sources > hover a source chip > tooltip shows the source title; or Sources > Research sources panel > Sources tab
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Hover the mouse over a small source chip after a sentence.
Read the bold line at the top of the tooltip that appears.
Alternatively, click the globe button titled Research sources in the top bar, then keep the Sources tab selected.
Compare with Expected: each source should show its title.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources; a mouse for hover
items.note: Titles come from the source data; a title may be missing for some sources and the chip then falls back to the site name.

items.where: Answer with web sources > hover a source chip > tooltip line under the title; or Research sources panel > Sources tab > line under each title
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Hover a source chip and read the grey line under the title in the tooltip.
Or click the globe button titled Research sources and open the Sources tab.
Read the grey line under each source title in the list.
Compare with Expected: each source should name its publisher or domain.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources
items.note: For search results the domain shown is the publisher's domain, not the routing host, per packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/citationPublisher.ts.

items.where: Research sources panel > Sources tab > click a source row, which opens in a new tab; or click a source chip in an answer
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Click the globe button titled Research sources at the top of the chat.
On the Sources tab, click one source row.
Look for a new browser tab that opens the web address.
Compare with Expected: the source should open at its own URL (the domain is shown under the title).
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources; a browser that allows new tabs
items.note: A source chip in an answer is also a link that opens the URL in a new tab (CitationChip.tsx), and a source row with no URL cannot be clicked.

items.where: Research sources panel > Sources tab > grey line under a source title; or hover a source chip and read the tooltip
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Click the globe button titled Research sources, then open the Sources tab.
Read the grey line under a source title for a date next to the domain.
Compare with Expected: the publication date should show when the source gives one.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources, with sources that have a date
items.note: Not all sources carry a date; the tester may see none. The panel shows the raw publishedDate string and the chip tooltip formats it via citationPublisher.ts, so the two formats can differ.

items.where: Research sources panel > Sources tab > grey line starting with Retrieved; or hover a source chip and read the tooltip
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Click the globe button titled Research sources, then open the Sources tab.
Read the line that starts with Retrieved under a source.
Compare with Expected: each cited source should show when it was retrieved.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources
items.note: Retrieved date appears only when the source has a retrieval time; the Retrieved label is also written in apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx.

items.where: Answer that used a project file > look at the icon before the file name in the chip; a web source chip shows a globe icon
steps: Open a chat in a project that has knowledge files, and ask a question the files can answer.
Wait for the answer and look at the chip after the claim.
A project-file chip shows a document icon before the file name.
Hover a web source chip and compare: it shows a favicon or a globe icon instead.
Compare with Expected: each source shows an icon for its type.
items.needs: a project with at least one indexed knowledge file; a question the file can answer
items.note: The only icons are FileText for project files (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/ProjectFileCitationChip.tsx), Globe for web sources (CitationChip.tsx) and MessagesSquare for past chats (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/CitationPastChats.tsx). No connector or chat icon was found in the citation chips; icons are not labelled in text.

items.where: Answer with web sources > hover a source chip > grey excerpt text at the bottom of the tooltip; or Research sources panel > Sources tab > two-line grey text under a source
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Hover a source chip and read the grey excerpt in the tooltip.
Or click the globe button titled Research sources and read the short excerpt under each source.
Compare with Expected: the excerpt should be the passage that supports the claim.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources where the source gives a snippet
items.note: The code shows the source's own snippet, capped at 180 characters (citationPublisher.ts); it is not verified that this snippet is the exact passage behind each claim.

items.where: Answer that used a project file > click a project-file chip that shows p. and a page number; the project Sources preview opens at that page
steps: Open a chat in a project with a knowledge file that has pages, such as a PDF.
Ask a question the file can answer and wait for the answer.
Look for a chip with the file name and text like p. 3 after it.
Click the chip.
Compare with Expected: the file preview should open at that page number.
items.needs: a project with a paginated knowledge file (PDF); a question the file can answer
items.note: The page text p. comes from formatProjectFileAnchor in packages/contracts/types/src/project-file-citations.ts; the preview reads the page from the link in apps/web/features/projects/components/SourcesPanel.tsx. The chip is an anchor only when a link exists, otherwise it is a non-clickable note.

items.where: Answer that used earlier chats > look for a row of chips above or below the answer with a past chat title and date > click one to open that chat at its message
steps: Use a chat that has earlier conversations saved, with the past-chat memory feature on.
Ask a question that refers to something from an earlier chat.
Look for the chip with a past chat title and a date after the answer.
Click the chip.
Compare with Expected: the source chat should open and land on the exact message.
items.needs: an account with an earlier saved chat that the answer can recall
items.note: The nav label Previous chats this answer used is an aria label only and is not visible text. The link carries a highlight parameter for the message; whether the page highlights it on arrival was not checked.
