items.where: Answer with web sources > read a sentence > the source chip sits right after the sentence it supports
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Read the answer one sentence at a time.
Look at where each source chip sits relative to the sentence.
Hover a chip to see which source it names.
Compare with Expected: each chip should sit at the claim it supports.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources
items.note: Placement is done by the markdown renderer in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx; it depends on the model's output, so the tester may see chips grouped at the end of a paragraph.

items.where: Answer with web sources > a source chip that shows +N after the site name > hover it to see every source in the tooltip
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Look for a chip with a site name followed by a plus count such as +1 or +2.
Hover the chip.
Read the tooltip, which lists one row per source.
Compare with Expected: all sources that back this claim should be listed.
items.needs: a question that needs current web sources where one claim cites several sources
items.note: The +N text is built in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx, so it has no fixed visible words. Multiple sources depend on the model citing more than one per claim.

items.where: Research sources panel > Report tab > open a saved report whose text has numbers like [1] but no captured links; the Sources heading shows the notice
steps: Click the globe button titled Research sources at the top of the chat.
Click the Report tab.
Open a saved research report.
Scroll to the bottom under the Sources heading.
Compare with Expected: where a link is missing, a notice should say the report refers to numbered sources without links, instead of a dead link.
items.needs: a saved research report whose sources were not captured (rare; may need a seeded report)
items.note: The notice text is in ResearchReportView.tsx and shows only when the report has no citations but its text has numbered references. Reaching such a report by a normal run is unverified.

items.where: Research sources panel > Report tab > open a saved report > click Markdown, PDF or Word in the top bar
steps: Click the globe button titled Research sources at the top of the chat.
Click the Report tab and open a saved research report.
Click Markdown, PDF or Word in the top bar of the report.
Open the downloaded file.
Compare with Expected: the file should keep the numbered citations and the Sources list at the end.
items.needs: a saved research report with sources
items.note: The Markdown export adds a ## Sources list built in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/research-report.ts; the PDF and Word output was not checked against this.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects (the Projects page lists every project as cards, with the search box "Search projects...")
steps: Sign in and click "Projects" in the left sidebar.
Look for the page heading "Projects" and the search box "Search projects...".
Each card is one project. Click a card's name ("Open project <name>") to open it.
Compare: you should see your list of projects and open one. If there are none, the text "Create one to group conversations, attach files, and share instructions." shows.
items.needs: a signed-in account (a project already created helps, to see a list)
items.note: The app calls notebooks "Projects"; the word "Notebook" does not appear in the UI. The sidebar entry can be hidden by the user (hideable: true).

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > New project > Create project
steps: Click "Projects" in the sidebar.
Click "New project" at the top of the page.
In the dialog titled "Create project", type a name in the field "Project name" (optional: pick a template under "Start from").
Click the "Create project" button at the bottom right. Compare: the dialog closes and the new project appears in the Projects list and stays there after you reload.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Projects page also has its own inline create form ("New project" in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ProjectGallery.tsx) with the placeholder "Project name"; the path above is the one the page opens.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings
steps: Create a project (see S37.02) and open it from Projects.
Fill the "Description" box in the "Create project" dialog, or later click "Project options" at the top right of the project and then "Project settings".
In "Project settings", change the "Project name" or "Description" text.
Click "Save". Compare: the new title and description show on the project page and stay after reload.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Project cards in Projects also have a menu with "Edit details" that opens the same settings.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > New chat in <project name> (send a message) > Panels > Project sources
steps: Open a project from Projects and send a first message in its composer (placeholder "New chat in <project name>").
In the chat, click the "Panels" button in the top bar.
Click the folder icon labelled "Project sources" (its tooltip; it toggles to "Close project sources").
Compare: a list of the project's sources opens beside the conversation.
items.needs: a project with at least one source file added (see S37.06)
items.note: On a narrow window the same toggle may appear only inside the Panels menu.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Add sources > Upload
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources" (or "+ Add sources" when files already exist).
Click "Upload" ("Files from your device") and choose a PDF or text file from the Mac file picker.
Compare: an "Uploading" banner shows the progress, then the file appears in the source list.
items.needs: a PDF or text file on the Mac
items.note: Accepted types are images, PDF, Office files and text (packages/contracts/types/src/chat.ts). Indexing for chats is server work and is not visible as its own screen.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Add sources > Google Drive (shows Coming soon)
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources", then look at the "Google Drive" card.
Compare: the card is disabled and shows "Coming soon", so a Drive file cannot be picked in this build.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Connectors are set to coming_soon (CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE in packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts). The picker needs GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY and GOOGLE_PICKER_APP_ID, which the owner has not set, so the Expected cannot be met yet.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Add sources > Text input
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources", then "Text input" ("Paste or type text").
Optionally type a title in "Title (optional)", then paste or type text in the large box.
Click "Add text". Compare: a new source with that title appears in the Sources list.
items.needs: none beyond a signed-in account
items.note: If no title is typed, the source is named "Text note" (AddSourcesModal.tsx). Notes in the Notes section are a separate feature.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > composer "New chat in <project name>"
steps: Open a project that has at least one source file added (see S37.06).
Click the composer box with the placeholder "New chat in <project name>" and type a question about the file's content.
Send it and wait for the answer.
Compare: the answer uses the project's sources and points to them (citation chips such as "p. 2" appear in the answer).
items.needs: a project with a source file added
items.note: Grounding happens on the server; the answer quality is not checked by this step.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Instructions
steps: Open a project and click "Project options" at the top right.
Click "Project settings", then type in the "Instructions" box (for example: answer in one sentence).
Click "Save".
Open a new chat in the project and ask a question. Compare: the reply follows the instruction.
items.needs: a project
items.note: A checkbox in the same dialog, labelled "Use your profile and instructions for AGI", controls whether account instructions also apply.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > ask a question in a project chat > click the citation chip under the answer
steps: In a project chat that has sources, ask a question whose answer comes from a file.
Look for the citation chip under the answer, showing the file name and a place such as "p. 2".
Click the chip.
Compare: the project's Sources tab opens with a preview of that file at the cited page.
items.needs: a project with a PDF source and a question that uses it
items.note: The chip is a link built from the citation (packages/contracts/types/src/project-file-citations.ts); a page location appears only when the citation has one.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Briefing doc
steps: Open a project with a source file and click the "Sources" tab.
Under "Create from your sources", click "Briefing doc".
Compare: a new chat in this project opens and starts writing a briefing from the sources.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: The button opens a chat with a prompt; the briefing is a chat reply, not a saved file. The label is "Briefing doc", not "Briefing document".

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Study guide
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Study guide" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and writes a study guide (quiz, essay questions, glossary) from the sources.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: Opens a new chat; the guide appears as the chat reply.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > FAQ
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "FAQ" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and writes a list of questions and answers from the sources.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: The button is labelled "FAQ", not "Frequently asked questions".

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Timeline
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Timeline" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and writes a dated timeline (as a Mermaid diagram plus a list) from the sources.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: Opens a new chat; the diagram is shown as the chat reply.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Mind map
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Mind map" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and draws a mind map of the sources' topics.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: Opens a new chat; the map is a Mermaid mindmap in the reply.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Data table
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Data table" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and returns a markdown table of facts from the sources.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: Opens a new chat; the table is a chat reply.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Slide deck
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Slide deck" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens with a request for a PowerPoint file built from the sources.
items.needs: a project with source files
items.note: The request sets officeCreationEnabled, so the result is meant to be a .pptx file; whether it is produced is not checked here.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > project card menu > Share > Share <project name>
steps: Click "Projects" in the sidebar, then open the menu on a project card ("Project options").
Click "Share". The dialog titled "Share <project name>" opens.
Choose "Everyone in the workspace can view" or "Only people you invite", then click "Share".
Compare: the access list shows "Can view" or "Can edit" for members. On a personal account the dialog only says "Only you can open this project. Switch to a team workspace to share it."
items.needs: a team workspace with a second member account in it

labels.text: Everyone in the workspace can view

items.note: The plan marks this as unfinished in the UI. Sharing is also on the project page under Project options > Share.

items.where: New chat (main chat) > the "Project" button in the composer > pick a project in "Search projects..."
steps: On the main chat screen, click the "Project" button in the composer's bottom bar.
Type part of a project name in "Search projects..." and click the project.
Type a question about that project's content and send it.
Compare: the reply uses that project's sources and instructions, and the chat is shown as part of that project.
items.needs: a project with a source file
items.note: The plan marks this as unfinished in the UI. On plans with AGI Work the same button is labelled "Project or folder" (ChatComposerNew.tsx).

items.where: No control of its own; visible by signing in to a second app with the same account and comparing the Projects list
steps: On the Desktop app, open "Projects" and note a project name, its sources and its notes.
Sign in to the web app with the same account and click "Projects".
Compare: the same project, with the same sources, appears there.
items.needs: a second app or browser signed in to the same account
items.note: Sync is server-side (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts); the Desktop app shows the hosted web app, so this is the same screen on both.

items.where: Sidebar > Study (also Composer + menu > Study)
steps: Sign in and click "Study" in the sidebar (or click the + button under the chat box and choose "Study").
On the page titled "Study", type a subject in "What are you studying?", keep the "How" choice, and click "Start studying".
Wait for the chat to open. Look for the "Studying: <your subject>" indicator above the chat, and check that the tutor teaches one idea at a time and asks a question before moving on.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account
items.note: The sidebar item is marked hideable, so a user who hid it will not see it; the teaching behaviour comes from the study instruction in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts (studyInstruction), not the plan's cited line 2892.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > "What are you studying?" and "How"
steps: Click "Study" in the sidebar.
Under "Start a session", click in the field "What are you studying?" and type a goal such as eigenvalues. The field stops at 200 characters.
Choose one option under "How": "Learn it", "Practise it" or "Revise it". Each shows a one-line description.
Optionally tick "Start with a personal study plan", then click "Start studying". Check that the chat opens and the first reply is about your goal.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Start with a personal study plan

items.note: The page has no separate goal screen; the typed subject and the How choice together stand in for stating a learning goal before the session starts.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > "What are you studying?" (and "Course material" when projects exist)
steps: Click "Study" in the sidebar.
Type the subject into "What are you studying?". There is no list of subjects to pick from; the subject is typed.
If you have projects, open the "Course material" menu and pick "From project: <name>" (or "None").
Click "Start studying" and check that the chat title starts with the mode label and the subject, and the indicator shows "Studying: <subject>".
items.needs: none (a project is needed to see the Course material menu)
items.note: The plan says the user picks a subject, but the code only has a free text field with a placeholder of examples; the Course material menu appears only when the account has at least one project.

items.where: Sidebar > Study > "Where you are with it"
steps: Click "Study" in the sidebar.
Open the "Where you are with it" menu. The options are "New to it" (default), "Some background" and "Know it well".
Pick "Know it well", type a subject, click "Start studying".
In the new chat, check that the tutor skips the basics and uses precise vocabulary, compared with a session started at "New to it", which defines every term first.
items.needs: none
items.note: The level is applied through LEVEL_INSTRUCTIONS in apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts, which the server sends to the model, so the tutor's behaviour change is only seen in the chat reply.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Persistent memory (switch)
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
Find the row Persistent memory with its switch.
Turn the switch off, then open a new chat and ask about a fact you saved before.
Compare: with the switch off the assistant should not use saved memories, and the switch should stay off after a reload.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The support text says Settings, Memory, but the real path is Settings, Personalization, Memory.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Search past chats (switch)
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
Find the row Search past chats and its switch.
Turn it off, then in a new chat ask about something said in an older chat.
Compare: the assistant should not pull excerpts from other chats while the switch is off.
items.needs: a signed-in account with older chats
items.note: The switch is separate from Persistent memory and is not disabled by it.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
Scroll to the Memory block and click Manage memories.
Look at the list that opens below the Memory block.
Compare: every saved memory should appear in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: The Manage memories button is disabled when no memories are saved.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Search memory box
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Click the box that says Search memory.
Type a word that appears in one saved memory.
Compare: only the memories that contain that text should stay in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with several saved memories
items.note: The search box only appears when at least one memory exists.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories (group headings)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Look for group headings above the memory lists.
Compare: memories should sit under headings such as Preferences, About you, Decisions, Context, Summaries, Skills, or Other.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories of different kinds
items.note: The headings come from each memory's category, so a tester may see only one group if all memories share a category.

items.where: Settings > Reflect > Work in progress
steps: Open Settings and choose Reflect.
Wait for the recap to load, then scroll down.
Look for a section titled Work in progress that lists chat titles with short descriptions.
Compare: it should list the projects or ongoing work the assistant knows about.
items.needs: a signed-in account with memory on and ongoing chats
items.note: The Work in progress section only appears when the recap has ongoing work; when memory is off Reflect shows Memory is off.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Add a new fact
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Click the box under the label Add a new fact and type a fact, for example I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work.
Click Add.
Compare: the new fact should appear in the list, and a new chat should be able to use it.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Adding works only when the Cloud memory is ready; otherwise the page shows Cloud memory is unavailable.

items.where: Any chat > composer > type Remember that ... and send
steps: Open a new chat.
Type Remember that I prefer short answers and send.
Look at the reply for a note that the fact was saved.
Open Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories and check the new fact is listed.
items.needs: a signed-in account with Persistent memory on
items.note: The phrase is taken from the support document. No confirmation text for the saved fact was found in the code, so the tester should record what the reply shows.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Save memories from chats (switch)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and make sure Persistent memory is on.
Turn on Save memories from chats.
Chat for a few turns and state a lasting detail, for example I work as a nurse in Denver.
Open Manage memories and compare: the new durable fact should appear without you asking.
items.needs: a signed-in account, Persistent memory on
items.note: The switch is disabled while Persistent memory is off.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > click a memory's text
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Click the text of a saved memory to edit it.
Change the text, then click Save.
Compare: the new text should show in the list, and later chats should use the corrected text.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a saved memory
items.note: The text itself is the edit control; its screen reader label is Edit memory.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Delete memory fact (icon)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
On one memory, click the trash icon labelled Delete memory fact.
In the dialog titled Delete this memory?, click Delete memory.
Compare: that one memory should leave the list and the others should stay.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least two saved memories
items.note: The trash icon has no visible text; find it by its position at the end of each memory row.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Clear all memories
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
In the Memory block click Clear all memories.
In the dialog titled Delete all memory facts?, read the warning, then click Forget everything.
Compare: the count line should show no saved memories and the Manage memories list should be empty.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: The button is disabled when no memories are saved.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Pin memory (icon)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
On one memory, click the pin icon labelled Pin memory.
Compare: the icon should change to Unpin memory and the memory should be shown as pinned.
Check that a pinned memory is kept when another memory is replaced (see Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree).
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: Some memory sources cannot be pinned and show Pinning is not available for this memory source.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories (line under each memory)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Read the small grey line under each memory.
Compare: it should say Added by you, Imported, or Learned from a chat with the chat title as a link.
items.needs: a signed-in account with memories from different sources (typed, imported, learned)

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories (grey line under each memory)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Read the grey line under a memory.
Edit that memory, then read the line again.
Compare: the Updated date should show the date of the change.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a saved memory

items.where: No control. The effect shows in Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree (Replaced: list).
steps: Save a memory by typing I live in Austin in Manage memories > Add a new fact.
In a new chat say I moved to Denver and send.
Open Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree and look for a line Replaced: I live in Austin.
Compare: in a later chat asking where you live, the reply should use Denver and not Austin.
items.needs: a signed-in account with Persistent memory on
items.note: The rule is applied by the server, so there is no button for it. The Replaced line may take a page reload to appear.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree (below the memory list)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and scroll down to the Memory block.
Find the section titled When memories disagree.
Read the rule line: Pinned wins, then ones you added, then the newest.
If a Replaced line is listed, click Use the replaced one instead and compare which memory the assistant uses next.
items.needs: a signed-in account with two memories that disagree
items.note: The section shows No memory has replaced another. until a conflict exists, so the tester needs to create one first.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Import memory from other AI providers > Start import
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and scroll to the row Import memory from other AI providers.
Click Start import.
In the dialog, choose Paste memories or Upload file, add the text or a file, then click Preview.
Tick the memories you want, click Import N selected, and compare: the memories should appear in Manage memories and later chats should use them.
items.needs: a text or export file of memories from another assistant

labels.text: Import memory from other AI providers

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Export memories
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and find the Memory block.
Click Export memories.
Open the downloaded file in a text editor or Preview.
Compare: it should list the saved memories in readable form.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
items.note: The button is disabled when no memories are saved. The file format was not checked in the code.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Project settings > Memory
steps: Open a project you own from Projects in the sidebar.
Open Project settings from the project's menu.
In the Memory section, read Use memories from outside this project and untick it to make project memory project-only.
Add a memory with Add a memory only this project uses, then open a chat in that project and a chat outside it and compare.
items.needs: a project you own

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project

items.note: The exact menu item that opens Project settings from a project page was not fully traced; the sidebar label was found.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Where a memory applies (Account, Workspace, Project); workspace on/off is in Workspace > Policy > Memory
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and find the block titled Where a memory applies.
Read the three rows: Account, Workspace, Project.
Open a workspace chat and a personal chat, ask what you know about the user, and compare that work memories do not appear in personal chats.
items.needs: a workspace the account belongs to, with a second personal chat
items.note: The workspace memory switch is in the Workspace console and needs an owner or admin; that part was not tested by reading only.

items.where: Chat > a reply that used saved memory: the note under the reply, or the Memory section in the Research panel
steps: Save a memory, such as I work as a nurse, then open a new chat.
Ask a question that depends on it, such as what do you know about my job.
Read the note under the reply for This answer came from your saved memories, not the web.
Compare: the note should appear only when memory shaped the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories

labels.text: This answer came from your saved memories, not the web.

items.note: The note is shown for one search-notice state; when it appears in an ordinary reply was not confirmed. The Research panel memory list only shows in research runs.

items.where: File > New Temporary Chat (desktop), or the composer's plus menu > Temporary chat
steps: Start a temporary chat with File > New Temporary Chat, or from the composer choose Temporary chat.
Read the composer note: Temporary chats never read or save memory.
Ask what you know about me, and compare: no saved memories should be used.
Afterward open Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories and check that nothing from the temporary chat was added.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories

labels.text: Temporary chats never read or save memory.

items.note: The exclusion itself is applied by the server; the composer plus menu row label was taken from the shared constant.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Never remember (and the switch Include sensitive topics in memory)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and find the block titled Never remember.
Type a term such as my home address in the box labelled Term to never remember and click Add.
Ask the assistant in a new chat to remember a term that matches, then check Manage memories.
Compare: the term should not be saved. Also check the switch Include sensitive topics in memory is off by default.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Credentials and other sensitive facts are refused by the server automatically and have no control.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Clear all memories (memory only). Chat deletion is in Settings > Privacy > Delete all chats in this workspace.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and click Clear all memories, then Forget everything. Check that the chats list is unchanged.
Open Settings > Privacy and find Delete all chats in this workspace, but do not confirm it unless you mean to.
Compare: deleting chats should not clear the memory list, and clearing memory should not delete chats.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories and chats

labels.text: Delete all chats in this workspace

items.note: The chat deletion control found is workspace-only; no personal delete-all-chats label was found in the files searched.

steps: Open a chat, pick one model from the model picker, and ask "What do you know about me?" or ask for a reply that uses a saved memory.
Switch to a different model in the same chat or a new chat and repeat the same question.
Compare the two replies: the saved memory and personalization should be used the same way with either model.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, with at least one saved memory, and two models available in the picker

labels.text: Synced to your account, available on every device you sign into.
Read in every personal chat on every device, unless a project claims it.

items.note: No control exists for this; the effect is applied in the server and client context code (apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts, apps/web/features/chat/lib/local-personal-context.ts, apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts), which attaches the same personal context block to every model request. The visible label for the answer-level indicator is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx: 'Answered without your instructions and memory: they could not be loaded onto this device.' This appears only when the context could not be loaded in local mode. I did not verify the rendered result per model.

steps: On a computer, sign in to the same account and add a memory in Settings > Personalization > Memory (the Memory section under Personalization).
On a phone or a second browser, sign in to the same account and open Settings > Personalization > Memory.
Check that the memory added on the first client is listed on the second client, and that a new chat on the second client uses it.
Look for the line 'Synced to your account, available on every device you sign into.' under the memory list on the first client.
items.needs: a second client signed in to the same account (for example a second browser or the phone app); a single account is enough

labels.text: Synced to your account, available on every device you sign into.

items.note: Cross-client sync is in the memory store (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/memoryStore.ts), which saves to the server through apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts; the visible sync status text is shown only when the store is in the 'synced' state, and the 'Settings' item is in the account menu (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx). I could not find a separate control for this, so the path to Memory is through Settings > Personalization. I did not verify the cross-device behaviour at runtime.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What should AGI call you?
steps: Sign in, open the account menu and choose Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to About you and click the field under What should AGI call you?.
Type a nickname or first name you choose (the field holds up to 60 characters).
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a short greeting, and check whether the reply uses the name.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The server prompt says to use the preferred name sparingly and never to open a reply (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:184), so the name may not appear in every reply. The Settings menu item text is confirmed in AccountFooter.tsx; the trigger that opens that menu was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > More about you
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
In About you, click the box under More about you and type a background detail, such as a hobby or a field you work in.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat and ask a question where that background would matter.
Compare the reply with Expected. The box holds up to 1,500 characters.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What best describes your work?
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
In About you, open the list under What best describes your work? and pick a role.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat and ask for help with a task that fits the role you picked.
Compare the reply with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The role list comes from apps/web/features/settings/constants/work-descriptions.ts, which was not opened in detail.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Response style
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response style and pick Explanatory.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer to confirm it shows the same choice.
Send a question and compare the reply with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The composer Style button has the same five presets and works per conversation (see S40.19).

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Response length
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response length and pick Shorter.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, ask a question that has a long answer, and compare its length with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The composer Style menu also has a Response Length row with Brief, Default and Thorough (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/StyleSelector.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Response style > Formal
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response style and pick Formal.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a casual question, and compare the register of the reply with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No separate formality control was found. The closest is the Formal preset (described as Formal register in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/StyleSelector.tsx:35), so there is no less-formal setting other than Default.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Response style
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response style and pick Learning.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and compare the reply with Expected.
Change to Concise and send the same question, then compare again.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The named presets are Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning and Formal. Warmth, Enthusiasm, Headers and lists and Emoji are separate settings (S40.09 to S40.12).

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Warmth
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open the list under Warmth.
Pick More, then wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and compare the warmth of the reply with Expected.
Pick Less, send the same question, and compare again.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The trait options are Less, Default and More.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Enthusiasm
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open the list under Enthusiasm.
Pick Less, then wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and compare the enthusiasm of the reply with Expected.
Pick More, send the same question, and compare again.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Preferred formatting
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Preferred formatting and pick Prose.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, ask a question that could have a list, and check whether the reply is prose or uses lists.
Compare with Expected. Headers and lists can also be turned Less or More under Characteristics.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Two controls cover this: Preferred formatting (Not set, Prose, Bullet lists, Headings and bullets, Tables and code) and the Headers and lists trait.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Emoji
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open the list under Emoji.
Pick Less, then wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question that invites emoji, and check whether the reply uses any.
Pick More, send the same question, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Technical level
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Technical level and pick Beginner.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, ask a technical question, and compare the depth of the reply with Expected.
Pick Expert, ask the same question again, and compare.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Response language
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response language and pick a language other than Match my message, such as French.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, write a message in English, and check which language the reply uses.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: This is separate from Display Language under Settings > General (apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Instructions for AGI
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Click the box under Instructions for AGI and type a standing rule, such as always end with a one-line summary.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and check that the reply follows the rule.
Turn off the switch beside Instructions for AGI, open a new chat, send the same question, and check the rule is no longer followed while the text stays in the box.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The switch has no visible text; its accessible name is Apply instructions for AGI in the same file. When off, the hint reads Off. Your instructions are kept and not sent to the model.

items.where: Sidebar > your project's row menu > Project settings > Instructions
steps: In the left sidebar, open the menu on a project row and click Project settings.
In the Instructions box, type a rule for that project, such as answer in short bullets.
Click Save.
Open a chat inside that project, send a question, and check the reply follows the rule.
Open a chat in a different project and check it does not follow the same rule.
items.needs: a project you own
items.note: The row menu label comes from packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx; the trigger that opens it was not separately confirmed.

items.where: Style > Concise (composer, in an open chat)
steps: Open a chat that already has messages and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Concise and send a message.
Compare the reply with Expected.
Open a second chat and check its Style button still shows its own choice.
Open Settings > Personalization > Response style and check the default there did not change.
items.needs: a chat with messages
items.note: The composer choice is stored per conversation in apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts; the Personalization default is a separate setting.

items.where: Style > Create Custom Style > Writing sample
steps: Click the Style button in the composer, then click Create Custom Style.
Type a name, paste two or three sentences of your own writing into Writing sample, and check the Style instruction box fills in.
Click Save.
Send a message in that chat and compare the reply's tone with your sample.
Edit the style and check the sample is still there.
items.needs: a writing sample of your own
items.note: The sample box exists only in the composer custom style form, not in Settings. The instruction is auto-filled only when it is empty and the sample is over 20 characters.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Reset response style
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Change Response style to Concise and set one Characteristics trait to More.
Click Reset response style.
Check the toast text Response style is back to the defaults. and that Response style and the traits show Default.
Check that About you and Instructions for AGI kept their text.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The reset also clears the composer Style choice and per-conversation picks (apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts:225). It does not change custom styles or the instructions box.

items.where: Style > Explanatory (composer, in an open chat)
steps: Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Explanatory and send a question.
Compare the reply with Expected, looking for reasoning and context.
items.needs: a chat
items.note: The same preset is also at Settings > Personalization > Response style.

items.where: Style > Learning (composer, in an open chat)
steps: Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Learning, which is described as Step by step, with check-ins, and send a question.
Compare the reply with Expected: teaching, quizzing and step-by-step structure.
items.needs: a chat
items.note: The learning guidance is sent to the model from apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts; whether replies follow it was not judged.

items.where: Style > Concise (composer, in an open chat)
steps: Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Concise and send a question that normally gets a long answer.
Compare the reply with Expected: it should be short and direct.
items.needs: a chat

items.where: Style > Create Custom Style
steps: Click the Style button in the composer, then click Create Custom Style.
Type a Name, a Style instruction such as Answer in two sentences, and click Save.
Check the new style is listed and selected. Click the pencil icon to edit it, change the name, and click Save changes.
Click the trash icon, then Delete style in the confirmation to delete it.
Check it is gone from the list and that the dialog warned it cannot be recovered.
items.needs: a chat
items.note: Deleting asks first, per the confirmation text, and removes the style on every device.

items.where: Sidebar > your project's row menu > Project settings > Personalization
steps: In the left sidebar, open the menu on a project row and click Project settings.
Under Personalization, untick Use your profile and instructions for AGI and read the line beneath it.
Click Save.
Open a chat in that project and send a question, then compare with Expected.
Open a chat in another project that still has the box ticked and compare.
items.needs: a project you own and a saved Instructions for AGI

labels.text: Use your profile and instructions for AGI

items.note: The box is ticked by default. The server choice is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts.

items.where: Composer > + menu > Use incognito (desktop: File > New Temporary Chat)
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the + button in the message box (its own label was not checked in the code).
Click Use incognito. The row changes to Exit incognito.
Send one message, then look at the top header for Temporary chat with an eye icon. Compare with Expected: the user can start a temporary chat from the chat surface.
items.needs: none
items.note: The composer row reads Use incognito, not Temporary chat. The Settings toggle Start new chats as temporary (S41.18) also makes new chats temporary by default. The desktop menu item sends the same flag to the hosted web app.

items.where: Top header of a temporary chat: Temporary chat
steps: Start a temporary chat (Use incognito in the + menu).
With no messages yet, look at the header: Temporary chat with an eye icon, then the note Won't be saved to your history and skips memory for this turn.
Send a message and open a second chat; the header shows Temporary chat only, with no note.
Return to the temporary chat and check the banner is still there. Compare with Expected: it stays visible while the chat is open.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Won't be saved to your history and skips memory for this turn.

items.note: On narrow screens the note after the label is hidden; the full note is also the hover text of the label.

items.where: Hover over the Use incognito row in the + menu, or Settings > Privacy > Start new chats as temporary
steps: Open the + menu in a new chat and hover over Use incognito.
Read the line under the row: Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.
Open Settings > Privacy and read the description under Start new chats as temporary: Not saved to history or search, and deleted after 30 days.
Compare with Expected: the explanation should match what happens to the chat.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.

items.note: The retention wording differs slightly between the header note, the row hover text and the Privacy page; the code was not checked for whether each clause matches behaviour.

items.where: The memory control in the composer is greyed out in a temporary chat; hover it to read why
steps: Start a temporary chat and open the + menu.
Look at the memory item: it is greyed out, not switchable.
Hover over it to see Temporary chats never read or save memory.
Compare with Expected: no choice is offered in the code, so memory is never read in a temporary chat.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Temporary chats never read or save memory.

items.note: The code offers no per-chat choice to let a temporary chat read memory. Expected says where offered, so this may not apply.

items.where: Effect is seen in Settings memory after a temporary chat; there is no control
steps: Start a temporary chat and tell the assistant a personal fact to remember.
Open Settings and look at the memory section for new saved items.
Compare with Expected: nothing from the temporary chat should be saved to memory.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with Memory turned on

labels.text: Temporary chats never read or save memory.

items.note: The code path that skips memory writes was found, but the exact Settings memory screen was not traced.

items.where: Top header of a temporary chat: the Personalized switch
steps: Start a temporary chat.
Find the switch in the header labelled Personalized (it is the switch beside Temporary chat).
Hover it to read Personalized uses your profile, instructions and response style.
Click it: the word changes to Unpersonalized. Compare with Expected: custom instructions should apply or not as the switch says.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Personalized uses your profile, instructions and response style.

items.note: The switch is shown only while a temporary chat is active, and hidden in voice mode. The effect on custom instructions was located in the request code but not traced to the screen.

items.where: Hover over the Use incognito row in the + menu (the retention note)
steps: Open the + menu in a new chat.
Hover over Use incognito and read the hover text.
Look for the clause: a connector asks before every call even where you saved Always allow, and a connector call still reaches that service.
Compare with Expected: the user should be able to tell which connectors work in a temporary chat and how.
items.needs: a connector set up in the account

labels.text: a connector asks before every call even where you saved Always allow

items.note: The text is a hover title only, not on-screen copy. The plan's Code line cited a line that moved; the policy file was used instead.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > How we protect your data (retention paragraph); also the attach note in the + menu
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Expand How we protect your data.
Read the paragraph: A temporary chat and its attachments are removed after 30 days.
Open the + menu in a temporary chat and hover over an attach row; compare with Expected: the note should say what happens to files.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Kept out of your Library and deleted with this temporary chat.

items.note: Where the attach-row note is shown on screen was not traced.

items.needs: a temporary chat that makes an image or video
items.note: The code keeps generated media for a temporary chat in media-assets.ts, video-generation-jobs.ts and the video route, but no control for a user to choose to keep the output was found in the chat UI. Searched the chat and library folders for save and keep wording without a match.

items.where: Composer > + menu > Exit incognito, then the Save this chat? dialog > Save chat (only when the chat has messages)
steps: Start a temporary chat and send a message.
Open the + menu and click Exit incognito.
In the dialog Save this chat?, read the list of what will be kept, then click Save chat.
Look for the toast Chat saved to your history. and open the chat in the sidebar. Compare with Expected: everything in it is kept.
items.needs: a temporary chat with at least one message
items.note: The dialog and save path are in WebChatPage.tsx; the Save chat button is the confirm label.

items.where: Composer > + menu > Exit incognito, then the Save this chat? dialog (before confirming)
steps: Start a temporary chat with a few messages and attach a file if you can.
Open the + menu and click Exit incognito.
Read the dialog Save this chat?: it says how many messages and any files will be kept in your history.
Click Cancel or the close control to check nothing changed, then repeat and click Save chat. Compare with Expected: the user sees what is kept and confirms first.
items.needs: a temporary chat with messages
items.note: Cancel is the dialog's cancel action in the confirm flow; its exact label was not read.

items.where: Settings > Privacy: Start new chats as temporary, Only use models that do not train on your chats, How we protect your data
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Read Start new chats as temporary with its switch and its description.
Read the switch Only use models that do not train on your chats under the heading Model improvement.
Expand How we protect your data and read the retention paragraph. Compare with Expected: history, training and retention each have their own control or statement.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Only use models that do not train on your chats

items.note: The Settings label Privacy comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json; how the user reaches Settings was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Privacy: the one-line description under each switch
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Read the description under Start new chats as temporary.
Read the description under each model improvement switch, including Only use models that do not train on your chats.
Compare with Expected: each setting should say in context what it does.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Only use models that do not train on your chats

items.note: The descriptions for the model improvement switches were not read in full.

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Where each feature processes your data
steps: Open Settings > Privacy.
Expand Where each feature processes your data.
Read the rows: Chat, Files you attach, Memory and past-chat search, Web search and Deep Research, Image and video generation, Dictation, Voice mode, Read aloud, Connectors.
Compare with Expected: each row names the place the data is processed, such as Cloud or a named provider.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Where each feature processes your data

items.note: Rows are built from a PROCESSING_LOCATIONS list in the same file; the full list was not read.

items.where: Scheduled > New task (choose Frequency: Daily)
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar.
Click "New task" (or "Create Your First Schedule" if the list is empty).
Type a prompt, set "Frequency" to "Daily", set "Local Time" and "Time Zone", then click "Create Schedule".
Look for the new task card in the list showing "Every day at" and the time you set. Compare with Expected: a recurring daily task that is generated and delivered.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan (scheduled tasks are hidden on Free)
items.note: The UI has no briefing-specific control; a daily briefing is a Daily scheduled task with a prompt. Delivery to the user was not verified.

items.where: Scheduled > New task > Local Time and Time Zone
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar.
Click "New task", then set "Frequency" to "Daily".
Change "Local Time" and open "Time Zone" and pick a different zone.
Click "Create Schedule" and check the card shows "Every day at" with the time you chose. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Basic or higher paid plan
items.note: The card's time text is built in ScheduleCard.tsx; the ScheduleForm line the Code audit cited was not re-checked.

items.where: Scheduled > task card > Pause (or Resume)
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar.
On a task card, click the "Pause" button, or flip its switch labelled "Pause" with the task name.
Look for the card to show "Paused" and the button to change to "Resume".
Click "Resume" and check the card returns to its active state. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a task that already exists (create one first)

items.where: Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours
steps: Open "Settings" from the account menu, then click "Time and focus".
Turn on the "Quiet hours" switch, pick days, set the start and end times.
Click "Save changes".
Check the saved times stay after reload. Whether proactive notifications are held during those hours needs a phone or push check and was not verified in the code.
items.needs: a notification channel turned on (for example mobile push) to see the effect
items.note: The holding of notifications is inner behaviour; only the settings are visible. The quoted code in push-notification-service and job-handlers was not found, so the hold logic was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Scheduled task finished
steps: Open "Settings" from the account menu, then click "Notifications".
Find the row "Scheduled task finished" ("When a scheduled task completes or fails.") and turn on its Email or mobile push channel.
Run a scheduled task (for example "Run now" from its card) and wait for it to finish.
Check that the chosen channel receives a notice saying the task finished. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an email or mobile push channel reachable from the account; a scheduled task to run
items.note: Agent-run updates are a separate block titled "Agent run updates" in the same section; the delivery itself was not verified.

items.where: Settings > Reflect
steps: Open "Settings" from the account menu, then click "Reflect".
Look at the heading "Reflect" and the activity chart below it.
Change the range in the "Reflect range" dropdown, for example "Past 30 days" to "Past 3 months".
Check the recap updates for that range. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: some conversation history; the page may ask for memory to be on
items.note: The error text the Code line quoted was not found, so the error and memory-required messages were only checked in use-reflect-recap.ts.

items.where: Settings > Reflect > range "Past year"
steps: Open "Settings" from the account menu, then click "Reflect".
Open the "Reflect range" dropdown and choose "Past year".
Look at the recap and activity chart, which should cover the last 365 days.
Compare with Expected: a recap of the past year.
items.needs: conversation history spanning the past year, ideally
items.note: There is no separate annual-recap screen; it is the "Past year" option on the Reflect page.

items.where: Settings > Time and focus > Break reminder
steps: Open "Settings" from the account menu, then click "Time and focus".
Open the "Break reminder" dropdown and choose an interval such as "30 minutes".
Click "Save changes", then keep using the app until the interval has passed.
Look for a break reminder to appear in the app. Compare with Expected. The exact reminder wording was not confirmed.
items.needs: a few minutes of active use
items.note: The reminder itself is shown by apps/web/features/time-focus/TimeFocusReminder.tsx; its visible text was not checked.

items.where: Settings > Time and focus
steps: Open "Settings" from the account menu, then click "Time and focus".
Look for the "Break reminder" dropdown and the "Quiet hours" section with its switch.
Change a value, then click "Save changes".
Close and reopen Settings and check the values stayed. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The page title shown in the code is "Time and focus" (TimeFocusSection.tsx), not "Time & focus".

items.where: Scheduled > Recent results
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the left sidebar.
Scroll below the task list to the "Recent results" heading.
Open a result row to see the saved output of an earlier run.
Compare with Expected: past briefings and outputs are kept and can be browsed. Run History is also reachable from a task card.
items.needs: a task that has run at least once
items.note: The Recent results section appears only when at least one schedule exists; Run History is referenced in ScheduleCard.tsx.

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the round + button beside the message box (it has no visible words).
Click Add photos & files and choose one image.
Type "What is in this picture?" and send.
Compare: the answer describes what the image shows.
items.needs: an image file to upload; a Free account must use a model that accepts images
items.note: The + button's label was not found in the code. Production can refuse uploads through the external scanner (UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL), which is server configuration, not a control.

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and select two images at once.
Type "What is different between these two pictures?" and send.
Compare: the answer refers to both images.
items.needs: two image files to upload
items.note: The + button has no visible words in the code. An attachment count limit applies per message.

items.where: File > Screenshot to Chat (desktop app), then the message box
steps: Open the desktop app and go to a chat.
Choose File > Screenshot to Chat and capture the screen as the app asks.
If the image does not appear in the message box, click the box and press Command-V.
Type "What does this screenshot show?" and send.
Compare: the answer explains the screenshot.
items.needs: the desktop app; macOS may ask for screen recording permission (unknown)
items.note: If the composer is not ready, the app copies the screenshot to the clipboard and tells the person to paste it, as the code shows.

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose a photo of a paper document or a scanned PDF.
Type "Read this document and explain it." and send.
Compare: the answer reads the text and explains it.
items.needs: a photo or scan of a document, or a PDF
items.note: The composer has a conflict check for images and PDFs in one message (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx); the exact warning text was not confirmed.

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose a chart image.
Type "What trend does this chart show?" and send.
Compare: the answer reads the values and trends from the chart.
items.needs: a chart image file

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose a diagram image.
Type "Explain the structure of this diagram." and send.
Compare: the answer names the parts and how they connect.
items.needs: a diagram image file

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose a photo of handwritten notes.
Type "Transcribe these notes." and send.
Compare: the answer gives the handwritten words.
items.needs: a photo of handwritten notes

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files, then the reply
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose an image that contains text.
Type "Extract all the text in this image." and send.
Click Copy message under the reply and paste it somewhere to check.
Compare: the copied text matches the text in the image.
items.needs: an image with readable text
items.note: The Copy message control's visibility on assistant replies was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose an image with several of one object.
Type "How many apples are in this picture?" (use the object in the image) and send.
Compare: the answer gives a count that matches the image.
items.needs: an image with countable objects

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and select two scene images.
Type "Describe the differences between these two scenes." and send.
Compare: the answer names differences that appear in the two images.
items.needs: two scene images

items.where: New chat > round + button beside the message box > Add photos & files
steps: Open a new chat and click the round + button beside the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose a photo or screenshot of the problem (device, error or setup).
Type "What is wrong and how do I fix it?" and send.
Compare: the answer gives troubleshooting steps that match the picture.
items.needs: a photo or screenshot of a problem

items.where: Library > image item > Remix (a new chat opens with the image attached and Image mode on)
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Open the menu of an image item in the Library.
Click Remix.
Check the new chat: the image is attached and the menu "What to do with the attached image" shows.
Type an edit prompt, send, and compare: the new image is made from the chosen reference.
items.needs: an image in the Library; an account that can create images (plan limits unknown)
items.note: Remix shows only for image items. The menu trigger label for an item was not found. An earlier chat image can also be used through the Variation button in apps/web/features/chat/components/ImageGenerationCard.tsx.

items.where: Composer plus menu > Create image, then type a prompt and send
steps: Open the composer's plus menu and click Create image. The composer shows an Image chip with the button Exit image generation mode.
Type a prompt in the message box.
Press the send button.
Look for the Generating image card in the conversation, then check that a generated image appears in the same conversation, matching Expected.
items.needs: a paid account (plan not verified in code)
items.note: The plus button's own label was not found; only the menu row text was verified.

items.where: Create image (image mode) > Select image model button
steps: Turn on image mode with Create image from the composer plus menu.
Click the button labelled with the current model name (its aria-label is Select image model). The menu is titled Image model.
Pick a different model from the list.
Generate an image and check that the picked model is the one shown in the card caption (Generated with ...).
items.needs: a paid account with more than one image model enabled
items.note: The list only shows models the account's media admission marks enabled, plus promotional image models.

items.where: Create image (image mode) > Style button > pick a preset
steps: Turn on image mode with Create image.
Click the Style button (aria-label Add a style to the prompt).
Click a preset: Photorealistic, Illustration, Watercolor, Oil painting or 3D render.
Check that the preset's wording is added to the message box, then generate and compare the look with Expected.
items.needs: none beyond image mode access
items.note: A preset does not set a separate field; it appends style words to the prompt text, so the look change depends on the model.

items.where: Create image (image mode) > attach a picture with the attach control, then What to do with the attached image
steps: Turn on image mode with Create image.
Attach one or more pictures using the composer's attach control (File upload).
Open the menu named by the button What to do with the attached image to choose the operation.
Check that the first picture is edited and the others guide the result, as the send-time message says: Attach up to N images.
items.needs: one to several image files to upload

labels.text: What to do with the attached image

items.note: No separately labelled reference slots were found; the code treats extra attachments as references by order. Confirm on screen.

items.where: Create image (image mode) > Select aspect ratio button
steps: Turn on image mode with Create image.
Click the button for the aspect ratio (aria-label Select aspect ratio; shows Auto by default).
Pick a ratio from the menu titled Image aspect ratio.
Generate an image and check the picture's shape against the ratio chosen.
items.needs: none beyond image mode access
items.note: The button is hidden for promotional image models; the options come from the chosen model.

items.where: Create image (image mode) > the button titled Return the image on a transparent background
steps: Turn on image mode with Create image and choose a model that can edit images.
Hover the button titled Return the image on a transparent background to read its title.
Turn it on (it shows as pressed), then generate an image.
Check that the returned image has a transparent background, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account and a model that supports editing

labels.text: Return the image on a transparent background

items.note: The button only appears when the chosen model supports edit; its visible text was not read in code, so the tester should find it by its title.

items.where: Composer send button (turns into stop) while an image generation runs
steps: Start an image generation with a prompt.
While the Generating image card shows, click the composer's send button, which becomes the stop control during a turn.
Check that the Generating image card ends with Image generation stopped and that no image is added.
Check the card offers Try again.
items.needs: a paid account, and time to click before the image finishes
items.note: No stop button labelled for images was found on the card; cancel is wired through the composer stop action. Whether billing stops is not verified in this read.

items.where: A stopped or failed image card > Try again
steps: Make an image generation fail or stop it (see S44.18).
Find the card labelled Image generation stopped or the error card.
Click Try again (it may show a countdown such as Try again in 30s first).
Check that a new generation starts with the same prompt in the same place.
items.needs: a way to cause a failure or stop
items.note: The retry label can change to retryLabel or a countdown text, so match on Try again.

items.where: A generated image card > Variation button under the image
steps: Generate an image so its card shows under the chat.
Click the Variation button below the image card.
Wait for the new generation to appear.
Check that a new image is made from the same picture, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account and a generated image
items.note: The button is disabled while generating or while a retry is blocked.

items.where: Library (/chat/library) > Images tab
steps: Open the Library page from the app's navigation.
Click the Images tab.
Check that generated images show together as a grid of thumbnails.
Use the Library layout control to switch view if you want to compare.
items.needs: a few generated images in the account
items.note: The sidebar label that leads to the Library was not confirmed in code; the page is /chat/library.

items.where: Library > Images > click a picture to open the file viewer
steps: Open Library > Images.
Click a generated image.
Check that the viewer opens over the page with Zoom in, Zoom out and Download, and a Close file viewer button.
Use Zoom in to confirm it enlarges the picture.
items.needs: a generated image in the Library
items.note: No control named Full screen was found; the viewer is a zoomable panel, so compare with Expected.

items.where: A generated image card in chat > the caption under the image Generated with
steps: Generate or open an image card in a conversation.
Read the caption under the image.
Check that it shows the model and the aspect ratio (for example Generated with ... · 16:9).
Look for the prompt and any size or quality setting, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a generated image
items.note: The caption shows model and ratio; a prompt, size or quality display was not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Library > Images > item menu > Remix
steps: Open Library > Images.
Open the menu of a generated image.
Click Remix.
Check that the composer opens in image mode with the image's prompt filled in.
items.needs: a saved generated image in the Library
items.note: The item menu's own trigger label was not confirmed; the Remix row is shown only for image items.

items.where: Library > Images > item menu > Remix (settings carry over)
steps: Open Library > Images and pick an image made with a specific model and aspect ratio.
Click Remix in its menu.
Check that the composer's model and aspect ratio match that image before generating.
Generate again and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a saved image made with a non-default model or ratio
items.note: The handoff code shown stages the asset, prompt and image mode; the model and ratio carry-over is set through pending image settings in the composer and was not walked through on screen.

items.where: A generated image card > More actions > Save to Library
steps: Generate an image so its card shows.
Click the More actions button on the card.
Click Save to Library.
Open Library from the app and check that the image is listed, and still there after a reload.
items.needs: a generated image
items.note: Save to Library only appears on cards where the app passes a keep action.

items.where: Library > Images > item menu > Add to project
steps: Open Library > Images.
Open the menu of a generated image.
Click Add to project.
In the dialog titled Add to project, pick a project folder and check that the image shows up in that project.
items.needs: a Project and a generated image in the Library
items.note: The menu row shows only when the file type is an accepted attachment type; not confirmed for image types on screen. The card itself has no Add to Project control.

items.where: A generated image card > More actions > Download
steps: Click the More actions button on the image card.
Click Download.
Open the downloaded file in Preview and check its size and sharpness against Expected.
Compare with the Download button on the image's hover bar.
items.needs: a generated image
items.note: Full quality was not verified; the code fetches the image blob and saves it.

items.where: A generated image card > Copy image
steps: Generate an image so its card shows.
Click the Copy button under the image (its title is Copy image).
Paste into another app such as Notes or a chat box.
Check that the picture itself pastes, not only a link.
items.needs: a generated image
items.note: The copy button in the preview modal copies a link, not the image; only the card's Copy image is the image copy.

items.where: A generated image card > New version
steps: Click the New version button on the generated image.
In the Revise this image panel, type a change to describe.
Click send and wait for the new version.
Check that the new image keeps the source picture and applies the change, as Expected says.
items.needs: a generated image, or a picture you upload in image mode
items.note: The button's title is Revise this image; for an uploaded picture, use image mode and the operation menu in S44.04.

items.where: A generated image reply > message menu > Report this response
steps: Find the image reply in the conversation.
Open the message's menu.
Click Report this response.
Check that the menu shows Reported and a toast says Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it.
items.needs: a generated image reply in a conversation
items.note: The message menu's trigger label was not confirmed; the report item is shown for non-user messages.

items.where: A generated image card > caption Generated with
steps: Look at the caption under any generated image card.
Check whether it says the image is AI-generated.
Download the image and check whether AI-generation metadata exists in the file (provenance is set by the server in the file route).
items.needs: a generated image; a file inspection tool for the metadata check
items.note: The visible caption says Generated with <model>, not AI-generated; machine-readable provenance is set in apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts and is not visible in the UI.

items.where: Chat composer > + menu > Add photos & files (attach your picture), then + menu > Create image, then type a change and send
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the + button in the composer and choose Add photos & files, then pick a PNG or JPG from your computer.
Click the + button again and choose Create image; the Image pill appears.
Type an instruction such as 'make the sky red' and press send.
Compare: the result is an edit of your uploaded picture, not a brand-new unrelated image.
items.needs: a file to upload and a model that supports edit
items.note: The attached picture is used as the source image only when the selected image model supports edit; the composer shows a conflict notice otherwise.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > open an image item's menu > Remix (opens the image in image mode); or open the chat that made it and use New version on the image
steps: Click Library in the left sidebar.
Find an earlier image and open its menu.
Click Remix.
Look at the composer: the image is attached and the Image pill is on.
Compare: the image is ready to be changed by the next message.
items.needs: an image generated in an earlier chat or in the Library
items.note: The Remix row appears only for image items and only in hosts with an image composer; the New version route works from any chat that shows the image.

items.where: Chat with a generated image > hover the image > New version > type in the box 'Describe a change to generate a new version...' > click the send button labelled Apply this change to the image
steps: Open a chat that contains a generated image.
Hover over the image and click New version.
Type a change, for example 'add a hat'.
Click the send button (Apply this change to the image).
Compare: the image above is edited to match the change.
items.needs: a generated image and a model that supports edit

labels.text: Apply this change to the image

items.note: When the model does not support edit, the same box generates a new image and the original is not changed.

items.where: Chat with a generated image > hover the image > New version > Select area
steps: Open a chat with a generated image and click New version.
Click Select area.
Paint over the part of the image to change.
Type a change and send it (Apply this change to the image).
Compare: only the painted area is meant to change, though the guide notes nearby content may change too.
items.needs: a generated image and a model that supports edit
items.note: The area painter is shown only when the model supports edit; the app's own helper text warns that the rest of the image may change too.

items.where: Chat with a generated image > New version > Select area > paint an area > Clear selection
steps: Open New version on a generated image.
Click Select area and paint a part of the image.
Click Clear selection.
Compare: the painted area disappears and the selection is empty; the Clear selection button goes away.
items.needs: a generated image and a model that supports edit
items.note: Clear selection is shown only while a selection exists.

items.needs: a picture file
items.note: No Remove background control was found. Searched for 'Remove background', 'background removal' and 'transparent background' in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx and apps/web/features/chat/components/ImageGenerationCard.tsx.
