The only related control is the Transparent pill, which asks for a transparent background on a newly generated image, not removal from a chosen picture.

items.where: Chat with a generated image > New version > change the aspect ratio of the image > apply the change
steps: Open New version on a generated image.
Choose a different aspect ratio (the aspect control is inside the New version panel).
Apply the change with the send button (Apply this change to the image).
Compare: the image is extended to the new frame and the new area is generated to match.
items.needs: a generated image and a model that supports edit
items.note: The composer does not offer outpainting (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx comment); the card's aspect change calls buildReframeEdit with operation outpaint. The aspect control's visible words were not located.

items.where: Chat with a generated image > New version > change the aspect ratio > apply the change
steps: Open New version on a generated image.
Choose a different aspect ratio.
Apply the change with the send button.
Compare: the same scene now fills the new frame, with no change to the content beyond the reframe.
items.needs: a generated image and a model that supports edit
items.note: Reframe uses the same aspect-change path as S45.16 (apps/web/features/chat/lib/imageGenerationOptions.ts); the aspect control's visible words were not located, and a tiny ratio change is skipped.

items.needs: a reference picture file and a model that supports edit
items.note: Searched for 'Reference' in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx. Visible reference labels found ('Reference images', 'Reference image') belong to video mode only; the image-mode reference path (readReferenceImageAsBase64) has no visible label located.

items.where: Chat with a generated image > New version > send a change > use the Previous version arrow to see the earlier image
steps: Open New version on a generated image and send a change.
When the new version appears, look for the group of version arrows under the image.
Click Previous version to see the earlier image.
Compare: the original image is still there next to the new result.
items.needs: a generated image and a model that supports edit
items.note: Earlier versions are stored in message metadata (imageVersions in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx).

items.where: The result of a Transparent image (inner behaviour of the image pipeline); seen in the downloaded file
steps: Click + > Create image, then turn on the Transparent pill and type a prompt.
Send it and wait for the image.
Download the image from the card.
Compare: the background is see-through, not white or filled.
items.needs: a model that supports edit
items.note: The Transparent pill appears only when the image model supports edit; the alpha path through storage and download was not traced end to end.

items.where: Composer > + menu > Create video, then type a prompt and send
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the + button in the composer and click Create video.
Type a text prompt in the composer and press send.
Look for a video placeholder in the chat that becomes a playable clip, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account (Create video is offered only to an entitled tier)
items.note: The + button's exact visible label was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Composer (video mode on) > Select video model button
steps: Turn on video mode with Composer > + menu > Create video.
Click the model button in the composer that shows a model name (aria-label Select video model).
Look at the list of video models that opens and pick one.
Check that the button now shows the chosen model name.
items.needs: a paid account

items.where: Composer (video mode on) > Select video length button
steps: Turn on video mode with Composer > + menu > Create video.
Click the pill button that shows a length such as 5s (aria-label Select video length).
Look at the menu of options, each shown as N seconds, and pick one.
Check that the pill now shows the chosen length before sending.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The length pill is inside the video-mode controls; the options depend on the chosen model and quality.

items.where: Composer (video mode on) > Select video aspect ratio button
steps: Turn on video mode with Composer > + menu > Create video.
Click the pill that shows a ratio such as 16:9 (aria-label Select video aspect ratio).
Pick another ratio from the menu labelled Video aspect ratio.
Check that the pill shows the new ratio and the menu closes.
items.needs: a paid account

items.where: Composer (video mode on) > Select video quality button
steps: Turn on video mode with Composer > + menu > Create video.
Click the pill that shows a quality label (aria-label Select video quality).
Pick another quality from the menu labelled Video quality.
Send a prompt and compare the clip's resolution with the chosen quality.
items.needs: a paid account, a finished clip to check the resolution
items.note: The UI offers quality labels, not raw pixel sizes; checking the output resolution needs a file tool outside the app.

items.where: Chat, after sending a video prompt > progress placeholder in the reply
steps: Send a video prompt in video mode.
Look at the placeholder that appears in the reply, with a progress bar named Video progress and a percentage.
Watch the percentage and the elapsed time change while the clip is generated.
Compare with Expected: the user sees progress until the clip is ready.
items.needs: a paid account, a video generation in progress

items.where: Composer (video mode on, a video model selected) > estimate note near the video pills
steps: Turn on video mode with Composer > + menu > Create video and pick a video model.
Choose a length, ratio and quality.
Look for the note that starts with This video is estimated at near the video pills; hover it to see the full text in the tooltip.
Compare the amount with your available credits, and after sending check the cost once the clip is done.
items.needs: a paid account with credits
items.note: The estimate text is built as a template in the code; whether it is shown as visible text or only as a tooltip was not fully confirmed.

items.where: Chat, during a video generation > Stop generating button on the progress placeholder
steps: Start a video generation in video mode.
While the progress placeholder is shown, click Stop generating at its top-right.
Look for the button to change to Stopping… and then for the note Cancellation requested.
Check that the placeholder stops progressing and the job ends, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account, a video generation still in progress
items.note: Server-side cancellation has special cases for providers; whether the job ends for every provider was not checked.

items.where: Chat, a failed video reply > Try video again button
steps: Find a failed video reply titled Video generation ended.
Read the text under it; the button shows only when the job is marked as retryable.
Click Try video again.
Check that a new video starts with the same model, ratio, quality and length as before.
items.needs: a failed video job marked retryable (hard to produce on demand)
items.note: A second Retry button also appears on a video player that fails to load; it is not the failed-job retry.

items.where: Sidebar > Library > Videos tab
steps: Click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Videos tab.
Look for all finished clips listed together in the gallery.
items.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one finished clip
items.note: The Library entry in the sidebar can be hidden by a setting; the tab labels are All, Images, Videos, Documents, Artifacts, Uploads and Generated files.

items.where: Library > Videos tab > click a clip; or the clip in the chat reply
steps: Open Library > Videos.
Click a clip to open it in the viewer.
Use the player controls to play, pause and drag the timeline.
Compare with Expected: the clip plays, pauses and scrubs.
items.needs: a finished clip in the account
items.note: The chat clip has native controls labelled Generated video; the opening step in the Library viewer was not traced in detail.

items.where: Chat, finished video reply > Download video button (top-right of the clip)
steps: Open a finished clip in a chat reply.
Hover over the clip, or Tab to it, so the round Download video button shows at its top-right.
Click Download video.
Check that the file saves to the Downloads folder as a playable video.
items.needs: a finished clip in a chat
items.note: The Library viewer also has a Download button named Download plus the file name.

items.where: Open an existing chat > bottom composer, with the text field empty > "Start voice mode" button at the right end of the composer
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat from the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty and look at the right end of the composer.
Click the button labelled "Start voice mode".
Check that the voice view opens in this chat and that the chat's earlier messages are still there.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The button only appears when the field is empty and voice is allowed (canUseVoice); the binding to this chat was not traced beyond the code lines in the plan.

items.where: New chat > bottom composer, with the text field empty > "Start voice mode" button
steps: Sign in and click New chat in the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty and find the "Start voice mode" button at the right end of the composer.
Click it and check that voice starts in a new chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The same button is shown on the new-chat composer (ChatComposerNew), but the code I opened did not show a separate new-chat-creation step for voice.

items.where: Open a chat > "Start voice mode" button in the composer > voice view
steps: Open a chat and click "Start voice mode" with the text field empty.
Speak one turn, then type one message in the "Type a message to send as a normal turn" field.
Look at the chat's message list and check that spoken and typed turns appear in the same list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: I did not confirm from the code whether the voice view sits over the chat or replaces it; the transcript placement is only cited as line references.

items.where: Open a chat > "Start voice mode" button in the composer > voice view fills the window
steps: Click "Start voice mode" from the composer of any chat.
Check whether the voice view fills the window, with the orb in the centre.
Check whether the transcript is hidden or shown in a smaller area.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The full-screen layout is in VoiceModeSurface.tsx, but I did not confirm the exact size from the code.

items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The listening state is drawn by VoiceOrb (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/VoiceOrb.tsx) and the state machine (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice/voice-session-machine.ts), but I did not find a visible word for the listening state, so I could not give the exact path to it.

items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The speaking state is drawn by VoiceOrb and live-voice-session.ts, but I did not find its visible words; the "Tap to hear the assistant" text is a different state (audio blocked).

items.where: Start voice mode > ask a question that needs a tool or a long answer > the status line while the reply is working
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Ask for something that needs a tool, such as a search.
While the reply is still working, look for the status text "Working on your request".
Compare it with the orb's thinking or working look.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The visible text is from the LABEL constant; the exact moment it shows was not traced.

items.where: Inside the voice view, the orb in the middle of the screen
steps: Start voice mode and speak.
Watch the orb while you talk and while the reply plays.
Check that the orb's shape changes with the loudness of the sound.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The visual follows audio level in VoiceOrb.tsx; it has no control of its own.

items.where: Start voice mode > bottom bar of the voice view > microphone button labelled "Turn off microphone"
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the microphone button in the bottom bar; its label is "Turn off microphone".
Check that the button changes to "Turn on microphone" and the call stays open.
Click again and check the microphone is back on without the call ending.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone

items.where: Start voice mode > bottom bar of the voice view > "End voice session" button
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the button labelled "End voice session" in the bottom bar.
Check that the voice view closes and the call stops.
Check the chat still shows the conversation.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The settling of usage is not visible on screen; I did not check it.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Open this chat panel" button > "Pause call" item
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the "Open this chat panel" button in the voice bottom bar.
In the menu labelled "In this chat", click "Pause call".
Check the screen shows "Paused." text with a "Resume" button, then click "Resume" and check the call continues.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The pause text says the call is closed, which may differ from the Expected line that says mic and assistant pause without ending.

items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: I searched apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice, the voice hook and packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice for hands-free and found no visible control or label for it.

items.where: Inside a voice reply, while the assistant is speaking
steps: Start voice mode and ask a question with a long answer.
While the assistant is speaking, speak loudly for a moment.
Check that the spoken reply stops and the app starts listening to you.
items.needs: a microphone and an external voice service
items.note: Barge-in is a threshold rule (BARGE_IN_LEVEL_THRESHOLD) in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/voice/voice-session-machine.ts and has no control; I did not confirm it runs in the browser.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" button at the top of the voice view > "Voice" carousel
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click the "Voice settings" link at the top of the voice view.
In the dialog titled "Voice settings", use the arrows in the "Voice" section to change the voice.
Start a reply and check that the chosen voice is the one speaking.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone

items.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" > voice carousel > "Play sample" button
steps: Open "Voice settings" from the top of the voice view.
Look at the voice carousel for a "Play sample" button.
Click "Play sample" and check that a short sample plays in that voice.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access
items.note: Partly unfinished: the ledger says the sample manifest is empty so the button stays hidden until the owner generates the samples; the code does show the "Play sample" text when a sample is present.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" > "Language" picker
steps: Open "Voice settings" from the top of the voice view.
Find the "Language" section and pick a different language.
Start a new turn in voice and check the spoken language matches the choice.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: Whether the choice reaches speech recognition was not confirmed from the code.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Voice settings" > "Audio output" menu
steps: Open "Voice settings" from the top of the voice view.
Find the "Audio output" control and open it.
Check the menu titled "Audio output device" lists "System default" and the other speakers.
Pick a speaker and check the next reply plays through it.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access, a microphone, and a second speaker or headphones
items.note: The picker only appears where the browser supports changing the output device (setSinkId); not checked in the Electron window.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Open this chat panel" button > "Captions" item
steps: Start voice mode from a chat.
Click "Open this chat panel" and then "Captions".
Check a region labelled "Voice captions" appears.
Speak and let the assistant reply, then check both speakers' lines appear.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone

items.where: Start voice mode > speak a few turns > end the call > open the same chat and read the message list
steps: Start voice mode from a chat and have a short spoken exchange.
End the call with "End voice session".
Read the same chat's message list.
Check the spoken turns appear as a transcript kept with the chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The transcript code is cited at WebChatPage.tsx lines only; I did not find a visible label for the transcript itself.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Activity" panel during a voice turn that uses a tool
steps: Start voice mode and ask for something that uses a tool.
Open the activity view during the turn (the "Activity" panel).
Check the tool steps and results are listed, and that the panel closes with "Close the activity panel".
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The control that opens the Activity panel was not traced; I only read the panel's labels.

items.where: Start voice mode > ask for an action that needs approval > approval card in the voice view > "Approve" button
steps: Start voice mode and ask for an action that needs approval.
When the approval card appears in the voice view, read its summary.
Click the approve button labelled "Approve" with the action name.
Check the reply continues without leaving the voice view.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone
items.note: The deny button's visible words were not found in the card file I searched.

items.where: Start voice mode > ask for a document > the file card in the voice view > "Open" button
steps: Start voice mode and ask the assistant to create a document.
When the file appears in the voice view, click its "Open" button (its label includes the file name).
Check the document opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access, a microphone, and a voice turn that creates a file
items.note: The desktop window routing that decides where the file opens is in apps/desktop/electron/windowPolicy.ts; not traced in detail.

items.where: Start voice mode > the connection drops (for example, turn off Wi-Fi for a moment) > "Reconnecting, attempt" notice
steps: Start voice mode and speak once.
Turn Wi-Fi off for a few seconds, then back on.
Look for the "Reconnecting, attempt" notice with the count of attempts.
Check that the call reconnects or shows that it could not.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access, a microphone, and the ability to drop the network
items.note: The message shown when reconnecting fails was not found in the label list.

items.where: Start voice mode > when voice usage runs out > usage notice with "Upgrade" button
steps: Start voice mode on an account whose voice usage is used up.
Look for the usage-limit notice in the voice view.
Click "Upgrade" and check the upgrade page opens.
items.needs: an account whose voice usage is used up (a Free account)
items.note: The notice text itself was not found in the label list; only the Upgrade label and the data-testid voice-usage-limit were found.

items.where: Start voice mode > "Continue in text" button in the voice view
steps: Start voice mode and have a spoken turn.
Click "Continue in text" in the voice view.
Type a message in the "Type a message to send as a normal turn" field and send it.
Check the reply continues in the same chat's text conversation.
items.needs: a signed-in account with voice access and a microphone

labels.text: Type a message to send as a normal turn

items.where: Open an existing chat from the sidebar > leave the message box empty > Start voice mode
steps: Sign in and open an existing chat that already has earlier messages, from the sidebar.
Leave the message box empty. The round button at the right end of the message box shows Start voice mode (it is replaced by Send once you type).
Click Start voice mode and speak. The voice view opens in the same chat.
Ask about something said earlier in the chat by text. Compare: the reply should use the earlier turns, and the spoken turns should be added to the same chat, not a new one.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, a microphone, an existing chat with earlier messages
items.note: The code loads earlier turns on the server (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts, loadLiveVoiceContext) and passes the current chat id, but there is no separate Resume button or history list for voice; the tester can only see the effect by asking about earlier content. Whether the voice view is bound to the same chat was confirmed from ChatComposerNew, not from a running session.

items.where: Code > Your computer > Connected to ... > Task box > Start voice input
steps: Sign in on the web app and pair a Desktop computer first (Desktop: Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control, Pair a phone, Copy link for a browser; then paste it under Your computer).
Open Code in the sidebar, then click Your computer in the rail.
Under the heading Connected to ..., click inside the Task box, then click the microphone button with the label Start voice input.
Speak the task, then use the controls on the dictation strip to stop or send. Compare: the spoken words should appear as the task you send to the computer, and no reply is spoken back.
items.needs: a paid or Free account that can use Remote Control, a paired Desktop computer that accepts tasks, a microphone
items.note: Steering here is speech-to-text dictation into the task box (useDictation), not a live voice conversation, and the strip's send button label was not checked. The same dictation strip also appears in the Code composer (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeComposer.tsx). Whether the sidebar item is visible depends on the Remote Control feature flag (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts).

items.needs: a microphone, a voice task that starts a running action
items.note: Found only half of the item. During a voice call, a Stop the task button appears in the status line while an action runs (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx, line 596 cancelBackendWork, hint Stops the running action and keeps the call open.). No separate control to stop only the spoken reply was found in VoiceModeSurface.tsx, VoiceComposer, use-voice-session.ts or live-voice-session.ts. Searched for Stop, interrupt, cancel and response.cancel in those files.

items.where: Chat message box (composer) > Start voice input (microphone button beside the send button)
steps: Sign in and open a new chat so the message box is visible.
Click the microphone button labelled Start voice input.
Speak one sentence; the strip shows a moving waveform and the Voice dictation group is visible.
Click the square button labelled Stop recording and edit the transcript.
Look: the spoken words appear as text in the message box, ready to edit.
items.needs: a microphone; a browser that supports voice input (Chrome or Edge per the button hint)

labels.text: Stop recording and edit the transcript

items.note: The keyboard shortcut Toggle dictation (Ctrl+Cmd+Shift+S) also starts it, per packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/shortcutRegistry.ts; the button label is a translation key with this text as default, and I did not check the translation files.

items.where: Chat message box (composer) > Start voice input > Stop recording and edit the transcript
steps: Click Start voice input and speak a sentence.
Click Stop recording and edit the transcript (not Enter, which sends at once).
Wait for the transcript to appear in the message box.
Click into the text, change a word, and check the edit is kept.
Look: the message is not sent until you press the send button; the edited text is what gets sent.
items.needs: a microphone

labels.text: Stop recording and edit the transcript

items.note: Pressing Enter while recording sends the dictated text immediately (DictationStrip.tsx handleKeyDown), so the edit-first path is the Stop button.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Dictation language (dropdown; the Settings path to the Voice section was not traced)
steps: Open Settings and go to the Voice section.
Turn on the Dictation switch, which enables the language dropdown.
Open the Dictation language dropdown and choose a different language.
Go back to the chat, click Start voice input, speak in that language, then stop.
Look: the transcript is written in the chosen language, as Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a second language you can speak
items.note: The Settings navigation label for the Voice section was not confirmed; the dropdown options come from SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES as native names.

items.where: Chat message box (composer) > Start voice input > Stop recording and edit the transcript
steps: Dictate a sentence with Start voice input.
Click Stop recording and edit the transcript.
Watch the strip show Transcribing with a spinner.
Wait until the spinner stops.
Look: the complete final transcript is in the message box, after any text that was already there.
items.needs: a microphone

items.where: Chat message box (composer) > Start voice input > Stop recording and edit the transcript > Try again (shown after an error)
steps: Click Start voice input and speak a sentence.
Turn off the internet connection before stopping, so transcription fails.
Click Stop recording and edit the transcript; wait for the red error text in the strip.
Turn the connection back on and click Try again.
Look: the transcript appears without recording again.
items.needs: a microphone; a way to switch off the internet (for example Wi-Fi off)
items.note: When a usage limit is reached the button reads Upgrade instead of Try again; the error close button is labelled Dismiss voice input error.

items.where: Chat message box (composer) > Start voice input > Discard recording (round X button at the left of the strip)
steps: Click Start voice input and speak a sentence.
Click the X button labelled Discard recording.
Look: the strip closes and the message box is unchanged, with no text added and nothing sent.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: Pressing Escape while the strip is open also discards the recording (DictationStrip.tsx handleKeyDown).

items.where: Effect seen after Chat message box > Start voice input > Stop recording and edit the transcript: the text arrives all at once
steps: Click Start voice input and speak a longer sentence.
Click Stop recording and edit the transcript.
Watch the Transcribing spinner; no text appears while speaking.
Look: the whole transcript appears in one piece when transcription finishes.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The batch request is transcribeViaServer in apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts, posting to apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts; I did not read the route body.

items.where: Chat message box (composer) with empty text > Start voice mode (voice entry button on the right)
steps: Leave the message box empty and click the button labelled Start voice mode.
Speak a sentence slowly while the voice screen is open.
Look: whether words appear as text while you are still speaking, as Expected.
items.needs: a microphone; a plan that allows voice mode (not checked)
items.note: Dictation itself is batch, not streaming; the streaming code is in the voice mode path (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts), and I did not confirm that the text is shown on screen while speaking.

items.needs: a microphone; a fresh start of voice capture
items.note: Searched apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice, apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer and VoiceSection.tsx for consent, recorded and notice; no pre-capture consent screen found. The only related text is the microphone purpose Dictation and voice conversations in packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/desktop-privacy.ts, which is a system permission review line, not a shown notice.

items.where: Open a conversation > conversation title menu > Export…
steps: Open a conversation that contains dictated text.
Open the conversation's title menu (the menu that holds Export…).
Click Export….
Choose a format in the Export Chat History dialog and click its export button.
Look: a file downloads and contains the dictated text.
items.needs: a conversation with dictated text
items.note: The export covers the whole chat history, not a separate recording transcript; the title menu trigger control itself was not labelled in the code I read.

items.where: Open a conversation > conversation title menu > Delete (retention window is in the workspace policy settings and needs a workspace admin)
steps: Open a conversation that contains dictated text.
Open the conversation's title menu and click Delete.
Read and confirm any prompt that appears.
Look: the conversation disappears from the sidebar and cannot be reopened.
For the retention setting, go to the workspace policy section with the Retention window and Enforce retention fields and check they are shown.
items.needs: a conversation; a workspace admin account to see retention settings
items.note: The Settings path to WorkspacePolicySection was not traced, and whether Delete asks for confirmation was not verified.

items.needs: a microphone; a chat message box
items.note: Dictated text is added through appendComposerMessage in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx; I searched ChatComposerNew.tsx and use-dictation.ts for undo and found no dictation-specific undo handling, so Cmd+Z behaviour is unverified.

items.where: Open a chat with an assistant reply > hover the reply and click the "More message actions" button > "Read message aloud"
steps: Sign in and open a chat that has at least one assistant reply.
Hover over an assistant reply and click the "More message actions" button (three-dot button).
Click "Read message aloud" in the menu.
Check that the reply is spoken aloud, and that the menu item changes to "Stop reading message" while it plays. Click it again to stop.
items.needs: a browser or desktop app with speech support (a system voice); an account with a chat that has an assistant reply
items.note: A second button with the same action exists in the reply action bar (aria-label "Read message aloud" in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ActionBar.tsx), which I did not confirm is shown in the web app. The menu item is hidden when the browser cannot speak, and is shown disabled with a reason when a reason exists. The button is not visible text, so the tester must hover or look for the icon.

items.where: Settings > General > Preferences > "Backup read-aloud voice"
steps: Open Settings and choose the "General" section.
Scroll to the "Preferences" heading and find the "Backup read-aloud voice" row.
Open the drop-down. It starts at "Browser default"; pick another voice from the list, which shows each voice name and its language in brackets.
Click "Preview" and listen. The voice is used for read-aloud when it falls back to this voice. Compare with Expected: the chosen voice and language are used for spoken playback.
items.needs: a browser or desktop app that lists system voices (if it lists none, the row says "This browser has no voices, so read-aloud has no backup.")
items.note: There is no separate spoken-language picker. The language comes from the chosen voice (shown in brackets), and "Display Language" in the same section changes the app's UI language, not spoken playback. The row is called a backup voice, and the text says the AGI voice is separate.

items.where: Settings > General > Preferences > "Read-aloud speed"
steps: Open Settings and choose the "General" section.
Scroll to the "Preferences" heading and find the "Read-aloud speed" row, just below "Backup read-aloud voice".
Click "Slow", "Normal" or "Fast" (the selected one is pressed).
Click "Read message aloud" on an assistant reply (see S50.01) and listen. Compare with Expected: the speech speed changes with the setting.
items.needs: a browser or desktop app with speech support; a chat with an assistant reply
items.note: The row is hidden when the browser cannot speak (the code returns nothing when speech is not supported). The rate is applied to the browser speech voice only, and the code gives three steps, not a numeric slider. A separate "Voice conversation pace" row (Slower, Normal, Faster, Fastest) controls the live voice conversation, not read-aloud.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Browse
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and click Skills under Customize.
Click Browse at the top right of the Skills list.
Scroll the catalogue and look for skills that are not installed yet.
Click a skill name and check that its detail page opens, with an Install button if it is not installed.
Compare with Expected: you can browse uninstalled skills and open any of them.
items.needs: none
items.note: How Settings opens from the sidebar was not confirmed in the code; the Settings > Skills path is taken from the settings navigation.

items.where: Settings > Skills
steps: Open Settings and click Skills under Customize.
Look at the list: each row shows the skill name, its Author (You, AGI or Managed), Last updated, and a status.
Compare with Expected: the list shows the skills installed or active for this account.
items.needs: none
items.note: The manage list is built from the directory adapter; the exact row layout was not rendered in the code read.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Add > Create a skill
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, then click Add.
Click Create a skill.
Type a Name, a Description and Instructions, then click Create skill.
Look in the Skills list for the new skill with Author shown as You.
Compare with Expected: the skill belongs only to this account and appears as personal.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can create skills
items.note: The Create action only appears when the account can author skills (onCreateSkill is capability-gated); the empty state says No skills of your own yet.

items.where: Settings > Skills > click a skill name
steps: Open Settings, click Skills.
Click any skill name in the list.
Check that the detail page shows the description, the Source and access section, and a Skill files list.
Click a file in Skill files and check that its contents show below.
Compare with Expected: description, instructions and files are visible.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Skills
steps: Open Settings, click Skills.
Read the name and any description shown on each row.
Click a skill and check the Description field in the detail page.
Compare with Expected: each skill shows its name and what it does.
items.needs: none
items.note: The row description is set by the directory adapter; the exact row text was not checked against a rendered screen.

items.where: Settings > Skills > open an installed skill > Try in chat; or type / in the chat box
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open an installed skill.
Click Try in chat; the chat opens with that skill selected.
Or in the chat box, type / and look for the Skills group listing skill names.
Compare with Expected: the product shows how a skill is started (slash name, button or automatic matching).
items.needs: an installed skill
items.note: The line Use one in chat with / or @ is in the fallback SkillsPanel in SettingsModal.tsx; the code read did not confirm the web app shows it.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Add > Create a skill (or open an existing skill and click its edit control)
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, click Add, then Create a skill.
Find the Instructions field and type some text.
Click Create skill and check the new skill appears in the list.
Reopen an editable skill and change Instructions, then click Save changes.
Compare with Expected: the instructions can be written and edited in the product.
items.needs: a personal skill you can edit
items.note: The edit control's exact label on the row was not confirmed in the code read.

items.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Skill files
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill that has more than one file.
Look at the Skill files list on the left.
Click a non-SKILL.md file and check that its contents appear.
Compare with Expected: the skill's bundled reference files are visible. Whether the model reads them during a run is server-side and not checked here.
items.needs: a skill with reference files
items.note: Only the viewing of bundled files is reachable from UI; reading them during a run is not visible from the UI.

items.where: Skill files list in a skill's detail page (script files appear there); runs happen server-side
steps: Open a skill that bundles a script file in Settings > Skills.
Check that the script file appears in Skill files.
Use the skill in chat and see whether the reply reflects the script's output.
items.needs: a skill with a script bundle
items.note: Script execution is in apps/web/lib/e2b/skill-staging.ts and the tool loop; the UI only shows the files.

items.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Source and access > Needs tools
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill.
Look under Source and access for the Needs tools row.
Compare with Expected: the tools the skill needs are listed as names.
items.needs: a skill that declares required tools
items.note: The row only shows the requirement; enforcement is in the server skill route, which the code read did not run.

items.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Source and access > Needs connectors
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill that needs a connector.
Look under Source and access at Needs connectors.
Check each connector shows Connected, Not connected, or a Connect button.
Click Connect if shown and check the state changes.
Compare with Expected: the required connections are shown.
items.needs: a skill that declares required connectors; an outside account if the connector needs sign-in

items.where: Chat box > Add attachments and tools (+) > Skills > pick a skill; or type / in the chat box
steps: Open a chat and click the + button labelled Add attachments and tools.
Click Skills and pick a skill from the list.
Type a message and send it.
Compare with Expected: the reply follows that skill's instructions.
items.needs: an installed skill; a model that supports tools
items.note: The + label is a translation default value; the reply's use of the skill is checked by the server.

items.where: No control; the chat reply uses a matching skill without a pick
steps: Install a skill with a clear description, then in a new chat send a message that matches that description without choosing a skill.
Check whether the reply follows that skill's instructions.
items.needs: an installed skill; a model that supports tools
items.note: The offer is applied server-side in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts (applyImplicitManagedSkillOffer) and skips some surfaces and any request with a tool choice.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Browse > open an installed skill > Enable skill
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, then click the skill (or Browse for a catalogue skill).
Turn off the Enable skill switch.
Check the skill stays in the list but no longer appears in the / menu in chat.
Turn the switch on again and check it comes back.
Compare with Expected: the skill is turned off and on without being deleted.
items.needs: an installed catalogue skill
items.note: The switch is not shown for skills you created (editable skills get Delete instead), so personal skills can only be deleted, not switched off.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Add > Upload a skill; or Settings > Skills > Add > Create a skill > Import a SKILL.md
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, click Add, then Upload a skill.
Choose a .zip, .skill or SKILL.md file from your computer and click Upload.
Check the skill appears in the Skills list.
Use it in chat with / and check the reply follows it.
Compare with Expected: the uploaded skill can be used.
items.needs: a file to upload (a .zip with SKILL.md inside, a .skill file, or a SKILL.md)

items.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > click a file in Skill files > Download file
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill.
Click a file in Skill files.
Click Download file.
Check that the file saves to your computer with its contents.
Compare with Expected: the skill's files can be downloaded.
items.needs: a skill with files
items.note: Download is per file; no whole-skill export was found in the code read.

items.where: Settings > Skills > open a skill > Source and access
steps: Open Settings, click Skills, and open a skill.
Read the Source and access section.
Check the Source, Added, Version, Needs tools, Needs connectors and Access rows.
Compare with Expected: the skill's permissions and where it came from are summarised.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Customize (group) > Skills, Connectors, Plugins
steps: Open Settings from the account menu.
Look for the group named Customize in the left list.
Open Skills, then Connectors, then Plugins: all three sit under that one group.
Compare: one Customize group gathers skills, connectors and plugins.
items.needs: none
items.note: The entry point that opens Settings was not confirmed; the Settings title is SettingsModal.tsx. The old /chat/customize route only redirects to /settings/<section>.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins
steps: Open Settings, then click Plugins under Customize.
Look for the headings Installed and All plugins.
Check that the list shows installed and available plugins.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Customize > Skills
steps: Open Settings, then click Skills under Customize, right beside Plugins.
Look for the headings Installed and All skills.
Check that the Skills page opens next to the Plugins entry.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Customize > Connectors
steps: Open Settings, then click Connectors under Customize.
Look for the headings Connected and All connectors.
Check that the Connectors section sits in the same Customize group.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Add marketplace > Browse AGI sources
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Plugins.
Click Add marketplace.
Click Browse AGI sources (text: Curated marketplaces of plugins from AGI and partners).
Look for a list of marketplaces and install a plugin from one of them, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Owner decision is still open on this item; the Add marketplace button only appears when the account can add sources.

items.where: Workspace console > Plugins
steps: Sign in as an organization admin and open the workspace console.
Click Plugins in the console menu (hint: Plugins this workspace publishes, and who gets them).
Look at the assignment choices Required, Installed by default, Available to install and Not available.
items.needs: an organization admin account in a workspace
items.note: How the workspace console is opened from the first screen was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Add marketplace > Add from a repository
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Plugins and click Add marketplace.
Click Add from a repository.
Type a git repository url in Repository url, optionally a branch or tag, then click Sync marketplace.
Look for the plugins listed under Plugins in this marketplace, then install one, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a git repository url that holds a plugin marketplace

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Plugins.
Click the search box (placeholder Search plugins) and type a plugin name.
Click Filter by, then Sort by, and try a choice.
Look for the list to narrow to matching plugins, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The exact filter options were not read; they come from the directory adapter.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Filter by > Category
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Plugins.
Click Filter by and look for the group Category.
Pick a category and check that the list shows only plugins in it.
items.needs: none
items.note: The category values come from the server, not from a fixed list in the UI.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Publisher
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Plugins and click a plugin.
Scroll to the Publisher section.
Check the publisher name, the link More from and the Website link.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin
steps: Open Settings > Customize > Plugins.
Click a plugin card, or its More info link.
Check the detail page: name, Install or Uninstall button, Plugin contents tabs.
items.needs: none
items.note: The detail view is packages/ui/ui/src/directory/PluginDetailView.tsx; the exact card click target was not read.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Includes > Skills
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Look at the Includes section and its Skills tab under Plugin contents.
Click Install, then type / in chat and look for the plugin's skills in the list.
items.needs: a plugin that includes skills

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Plugin contents > Connectors
steps: Open a plugin's detail page that lists connectors.
Click the Connectors tab under Plugin contents.
Look at each connector's status: Connected, Not connected or Not added.
items.needs: a plugin that includes connectors

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Includes > Agents
steps: Open a plugin's detail page that includes agents.
Look at the Includes section for the Agents line.
Read the note: Agents run in the agi CLI, not in chat.
items.needs: a plugin that includes agents; the agi CLI if you want to use them

labels.text: Agents run in the agi CLI, not in chat.

items.note: Expected says the agents are usable when installed; the page says they run only in the CLI.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Includes > Commands
steps: Open a plugin's detail page that includes commands.
Look at the Includes section for the Commands line and its tab.
Install the plugin and check that its commands appear for use.
items.needs: a plugin that includes commands
items.note: The use of commands in chat was not read.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Permissions
steps: Open a plugin's detail page before installing it.
Read the Permissions section and its copy: What this plugin says it needs.
Install, then open the same page again and check that the permissions are still shown.
items.needs: a plugin that lists permissions

labels.text: What this plugin says it needs. Installing it agrees to these; you can remove it at any time.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Works with
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Look at the Works with line and the Desktop and CLI note.
Compare with the surface you are on.
items.needs: none
items.note: Owner decision is still open on this item.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin > Install
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Click Install.
Confirm in the Install dialog (Cancel is the other button).
Look for the primary button to change to the installed state, and the plugin to appear under Installed.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Look at the Enabled switch and the per-skill Use switches.
Change a setting, then reopen the page and check it was kept.
items.needs: an installed plugin
items.note: The plugin settings block was not read in full; the Use prefix is a constant.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin > Plugin contents > Connectors > Connect
steps: Open an installed plugin that bundles connectors.
Click the Connectors tab under Plugin contents.
Click Connect (or Add API key) on a connector.
Look for the status to change from Not connected to Connected.
items.needs: an installed plugin with connectors; an outside account for connectors that sign in with a service

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin > Enabled
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Turn the Enabled switch off.
Read the hint: Turn this off to keep the plugin installed without using it.
Check that the plugin is still listed as installed, then turn Enabled back on.
items.needs: an installed plugin

labels.text: Turn this off to keep the plugin installed without using it.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin > Update to
steps: Open an installed plugin that has a newer version.
Look for the Update available label and the Update to line in the version section.
Click Update to and confirm.
Check that the Installed version changes to the new version.
items.needs: an installed plugin with a newer version published

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin > Choose a version
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Click Choose a version (or Switch version).
Pick an older version and confirm in Switch to version.
Check that the plugin stays on that version.
items.needs: an installed plugin with more than one version
items.note: No control is labelled Pin; the pin behaviour is the version switch with the copy: stays on it until you choose another.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin > Customize
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Click Customize (hint: Make your own copy of this plugin and edit its skills).
Confirm with Make my copy.
Look for your own copy to be editable and the original to be turned off.
items.needs: an installed plugin
items.note: Editing is done through Customize, which makes a copy; Edit plugin is for plugins the account created.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click an installed plugin > Customize > Make my copy
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Click Customize, then Make my copy.
Look for the copy in your own plugins list with the same skills and files.
items.needs: an installed plugin
items.note: No control is labelled Fork; Customize with Make my copy is the fork action.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Remove (beside an installed plugin) > Remove in the "Remove plugin?" box. A second route: open the plugin's detail and click Uninstall.
steps: Sign in and open Settings.
Under Customize, click Plugins.
On a plugin that shows as installed, click Remove.
In the "Remove plugin?" box, click Remove.
Compare with Expected: the plugin leaves the installed list and its skills and commands stop working. Then open the plugin's detail and check that Uninstall is gone or changed.
items.needs: an account with at least one installed plugin
items.note: The Remove control in the list has a confirmation box; in the detail view's Uninstall path I did not find a confirmation step, only the adapter call. A dependents prompt exists in apps/web/features/directory/hooks/useDirectoryAdapter.ts.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Plugins (workspace console at /workspace/plugins)
steps: Sign in as an admin of a workspace and open Settings, then Workspace, then Workspace administration.
Click Plugins in the console's left list.
On a plugin row, open the install setting and choose one of Required, Installed by default, Available to install or Not available.
Under the group settings, pick a group in "Choose a group", choose a setting for it and save.
Sign in as a member of that workspace and compare with Expected: a Required plugin is on and cannot be turned off, a Not available plugin is hidden.
items.needs: an admin account in a workspace, plus a member account in the same workspace
items.note: The exact save button label and the member-side result were not confirmed in the code I read.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > click a plugin row > Security scan
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Click a plugin row to open its detail.
Scroll to the section headed Security scan.
Read the verdict line under the heading.

Compare with Expected: the verdict is one of "Passed. No unsafe patterns were found.", "Needs your review. It may carry risk depending on where it came from." or "Blocked. It cannot be installed.", with any findings listed below it.
items.needs: a plugin that has a scan result (for example one you uploaded as an archive)

labels.text: Passed. No unsafe patterns were found.

items.note: The Security scan section only appears when a scan exists; the way into a plugin's detail is by clicking the row, which I did not confirm as a specific control.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin's detail > Not available on this surface
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Open an installed plugin that the server no longer runs on this surface.
Look for the row headed "Not available on this surface" with the hint "Still installed, but the server no longer runs it here."
Compare with Expected: the warning replaces the Enabled switch for that plugin.
items.needs: a plugin the server has stopped running on this surface; ask the owner for one
items.note: I found only this unavailable row as the visible warning. The version and surface check in apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts (around line 680) only sets install-state labels, so a version-specific warning was not found.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin's detail > Reload skills or Connect
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Open an installed plugin whose skill failed to load or whose connector is not connected.
Look for the line "These skills did not load:" with the skill names and a Reload skills button, or the line "Its skills need the connector" with a Connect button.
Click the button shown and compare with Expected: skills reload, or the connector's connect flow opens.
items.needs: an installed plugin with a missing skill or an unconnected connector
items.note: The repair list shows only when the plugin is installed and the server reports repairs; I did not confirm when that happens.

items.needs: none
items.note: No assistant was found. The only plugin-making flow is the "Create a plugin" form (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts, opened from DirectoryPanel.tsx when the plugins section has createPlugin). apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts only holds an on/off switch (AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING) and no assistant UI. I did not confirm the form is shown in Settings > Customize > Plugins.

items.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open a plugin you created > Submit to the directory > Submit for review
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Open a plugin you created (through Create a plugin).
Click Submit to the directory.
Click Submit for review in the confirmation.
Compare with Expected: the plugin shows Submitted for review and a Withdraw button. A second admin account can then open Admin > Plugin moderation to review it.
items.needs: a plugin you created, and a platform staff account to review it
items.note: The Submit button shows only for plugins the owner can submit and that are not already pending (apps/web/features/directory/services/plugins-directory.ts around line 1036).

items.where: Admin console > Plugin moderation (page at /admin/plugins)
steps: Sign in as platform staff and open the admin console.
Click Plugin moderation.
Click Review next to a plugin, then open a version.
Click Deprecate or Suspend. In the confirmation, click Suspend.
Compare with Expected: the version shows the Deprecated or Suspended badge.
items.needs: a platform staff account
items.note: The queue of submissions also has Review, Suspend and a note field (apps/web/features/admin/pages/PluginModerationPage.tsx).

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors
steps: Open Settings (Mac menu bar Settings… or Command+,).
Click Connectors in the Settings list.
Click Add, then click Browse connectors.
Look for a catalogue of connector cards, each with its name and a state (Connected or Connect).
Click one connector and check its Made by row for the publisher.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Settings table shows Connector, Type and status columns with no publisher column; the publisher is on the detail page under Made by.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Search connectors…
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Click the search box at the top right of the connector list.
Type part of a name, for example Gmail.
Look for the list narrowing to matching rows, then clear the box to see all connectors again.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Settings table search matches name and description only; the Browse connectors search also matches publisher and category; neither matches tool names as Expected says.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > Filter by > Category
steps: Open Settings, click Connectors, then Add and Browse connectors.
Click Filter by.
Under Category, pick one (for example Productivity).
Look for the list showing only connectors in that category, then click Clear filters to reset.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Category group only appears when the catalogue has at least two categories.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > click a connector name
steps: Open Settings, Connectors, then Add and Browse connectors.
Click any connector name or card.
Read the description and the Categories, Made by, Author and Sign-in rows (Sign-in shows Required or None).
Check the Connector URL and More info links, the Tools list, and the note Only use connectors you trust.
Compare with Expected: description, publisher, sign-in requirement, tools and links should all be present.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > click a connector > Tools
steps: Open a connector that is not connected yet.
Find the Tools heading and read the list of tools.
Connect the connector, reopen it, and find the Live MCP capabilities section.
Check that the tools, resources and prompts it lists match the list you saw before connecting.
items.needs: a connector that exposes tools; a connected one to see the live list
items.note: The live capabilities panel only appears once the connector is connected.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connector that is not connected yet
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Click a connector that is not connected.
Read the Before you connect box and the Permissions requested list, which shows a Read or Write badge for each permission.
Click Connect and read the dialog titled Connect <name>? that lists the permissions.
Compare with Expected: the text should say in plain language what the connector can read and change.
items.needs: a connector not yet connected
items.note: For connectors without a provider scope list, the text says the exact permissions are named on the provider's own consent screen.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Connect
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Click Connect on a connector row, or open the connector and click Connect.
In the dialog titled Connect <name>? click Allow.
Look for the connector to move to its connected state, or for the provider sign-in page to open.
items.needs: none for the dialog; an outside account for OAuth connectors
items.note: The consent dialog is opened from apps/web/features/connectors/lib/open-connector-authorization.ts before the authorization starts.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Connect (an OAuth connector such as Google Drive)
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Click Connect on an OAuth connector such as Google Drive.
In the dialog click Allow.
Look for the provider's own consent page to open; approve there.
Return to the app and look for the connector shown as connected.
items.needs: an outside account (Google) that can approve the provider consent
items.note: Only the code path was traced; the stored grant after the callback was not checked in the UI.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connector that uses an API key > Add API key
steps: Open Settings, Connectors, then click the API key connector.
Click Add API key.
Type a key into the API key field and click Test and save.
Look for the message Connected. with the tool count, and for the key to be stored (the form says it is stored encrypted).
items.needs: an API-key connector and a valid key for it

items.where: Workspace console > Sharing > Shared connectors > Share connector with organization
steps: As an organization admin, open the Workspace console and click Sharing.
Under Shared connectors, pick one of your connectors and click Share connector with organization.
Sign in as a member of the same organization and open that connector's tools.
Look for the member to use the connector without seeing the credential.
items.needs: an organization admin account and a second member account in the same workspace
items.note: Code search did not confirm the menu item that opens the Workspace console from the app; the route is /workspace/sharing.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > click a connected connector > Connected account
steps: Open Settings, Connectors, then Add and Browse connectors.
Click a connector that is connected.
Find the Connected account heading and the row under it.
Look for the account name (email or login). If the provider sent no name, the text says The provider did not share the account name.
items.needs: a connected account

labels.text: The provider did not share the account name.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > click a connected connector > Connected account
steps: Open a connected connector as in S55.13.
Look at the Connected account row for the sign-in identity (email or login).
Look for any domain or workspace name next to it.
items.needs: a connected account signed in with an email or login
items.note: Only the identity label is shown; no domain or workspace field was found in the UI or in apps/web/lib/connectors/accounts.ts.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > click a connected connector > Permissions granted
steps: Open a connected connector as in S55.13.
Find the Permissions granted list.
Read each row and its Read or Write badge.
Compare with the Permissions requested list shown before connecting (S55.06).
items.needs: a connected account
items.note: The list appears only when the stored grant has scopes.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > Browse connectors > click a connector > Connector health
steps: Open Settings, Connectors, then Add and Browse connectors.
Click a connector and scroll to the Connector health section.
Read the state for the connector: Responding, Degraded, Not responding or Not called yet.
Click Refresh and check the call counts. A connector that needs reconnecting shows a Reconnect button on its row instead.
items.needs: a connector that has been called recently for a useful state
items.note: The health section reads call statistics from the last hour; it does not itself say needs reauthorization.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connector whose grant has expired or was revoked (for example Google Drive) > Reconnect
steps: Open the connector whose connection needs reconnecting.
Look for a Reconnect button beside Disconnect and the text that says it needs reconnecting; its settings are kept.
Click Reconnect and check that the provider's consent page opens again.
Look for the connector to return to connected, with its tool permissions still set.
items.needs: an expired or revoked connection, for example a Google Drive grant revoked at Google
items.note: The plan marks this item as unfinished; the code path exists but was not run.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched the connector feature, settings and directory for Test, Check, Refresh and Retry. Only Test and save exists, and it tests a new API key while saving it; no standalone test-connection action was found. Refresh re-reads call stats and Retry discovery appears only when live capabilities fail to load.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connected connector > Disconnect
steps: Open Settings, click Connectors, then click a connected connector.
Click Disconnect.
In the dialog titled Disconnect <name>? read the warning and click Disconnect.
Look for the connector to show Connect again and for the assistant to stop using it in a new chat.
items.needs: a connected connector
items.note: The dialog says you can connect it again later; the trust copy says Disconnect deletes its saved per-tool permissions.

items.where: After Disconnect (S55.22), on the provider's own connected-apps page
steps: Disconnect a connected connector as in S55.22.
Open the provider's own account page for connected or authorised apps.
Look for the app to be gone from the list.
items.needs: an outside account for the provider
items.note: No Revoke button or word exists in the UI; the token revocation runs on the server when Disconnect is used (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts and apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts). Not checked live.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched the connector feature, the connectors API routes, the directory and the desktop folder picker. No folder or repository limit control was found for connectors. GitHub repositories are picked in the GitHub install flow on GitHub's side, and Choose a folder belongs to local folder attach, not connectors.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connected connector > Tool permissions > Write and delete tools
steps: Open a connected connector and click Tool permissions.
Find the Write and delete tools group.
Use the bulk control for that group to set Deny, or set Deny on each write tool.
Look in a chat for the assistant to be unable to run those write tools.
items.needs: a connected connector with write tools and a chat to test in
items.note: No single read-only switch was found; read-only behaviour is set per tool group in Tool permissions. The bulk button wording was read from aria labels, not confirmed visually.

items.where: Settings > Connectors > click a connected connector > Tool permissions
steps: Open a connected connector and click Tool permissions.
Find a tool under Write and delete tools.
Click Allow (Always run without asking), Ask (Needs approval each time) or Deny (Never run this tool).
Look for the chosen option to be highlighted and saved, and for a chat to follow it.
items.needs: a connected connector with write tools

items.where: No control found; the replacement notice is written for the model in the conversation context, and the model reads the full stored result with the read_tool_result tool

items.where: Settings > Connectors > [a connected connector] > "Tool permissions" > "Recent calls"

items.where: Chat > a tool step that shows "This tool requires approval before execution." > Allow or Deny on that one card
steps: Sign in, open Chat and ask the agent for an action that needs approval (for example a write or a send). Set Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals > Ask before every action first if nothing asks.
When the card shows "This tool requires approval before execution.", click Deny on that one card.
Look: the run continues, the card records Denied and the agent answers without running that tool.
Repeat with a new request and click Allow: the tool runs and the run continues.

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

items.where: Tasks page > a run under "Waiting for your approval" > Approve or Deny (one button decides every request in that run)

Find the run that shows "Waiting for your approval".
Click Approve once.
Look: all pending requests of that run are approved together, as Expected. The Tasks page path was taken from code and not confirmed on screen.

items.note: The chat Approvals inbox has no bulk button; each request there is answered on its own.

items.where: Chat > a tool step that shows "This tool requires approval before execution." > Allow for this chat

Click Allow for this chat on its card.
Trigger the same tool again in the same chat and watch whether it asks.

Select Ask before every action, then start a chat and ask for a read such as a search: it waits for approval.

Look: reads run and writes stop and ask, as Expected.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals > Run read-only actions without asking
steps: Select Run read-only actions without asking under Tool approvals.
Trigger a low-risk read in chat and confirm it runs without asking.

steps: Trigger a tool that needs approval in chat.

Look: the card shows the tool name and the reason in the line "This tool requires approval before execution."

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

steps: Ask the agent to edit or create a file in a granted folder.

steps: Ask the agent to change text in a file.

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

steps: Trigger a tool that needs approval and leave the card unanswered until the run ends or times out.

steps: Open Settings > Capabilities and scroll below Tool approvals.

steps: Set a tool to Always run without asking under Settings > Connectors > Tool permissions.

Trigger that tool again and look: it asks again.

items.where: Second signed-in device > open the same chat > Approvals in the chat header (or Tasks > run "Waiting for your approval")
steps: Start an approval on the first device and leave it pending.
On a second device signed into the same account, open the same chat.
Open Approvals in the header, approve the request.

items.where: Desktop app > ask AGI to run a shell command or control another app > the native window titled "Permission required" (its buttons are "Deny", "Allow this session", and "Never allow" for app control only). In the web chat, a high-risk tool card shows the notice and has no "Allow for this chat" button.
steps: Open the Desktop app and sign in.
In a chat, ask AGI to run a shell command, or to control another app.
When the native window "Permission required" appears, read its warning text and buttons.
Check that the text says it is a high-impact permission that lasts until you quit the app, and that there is no "Always allow" button.
For a web tool card with the high-risk notice, check that "Allow for this chat" is missing and the card is red.
Compare with Expected: a stronger warning, no permanent allow, and the permission is asked again later.

labels.text: Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI. Check where it goes before you allow it.

items.where: Desktop app > File > Take Over Screen Control (also the bar "AGI is using your computer" with the "Take over" button; hand back with File > Hand Back Screen Control or "Hand back"). Computer use must be on in Settings > Computer use.
steps: Open the Desktop app, sign in, and turn on computer use in Settings > Computer use.
Start a chat task that makes AGI use the screen, for example a click on a visible app.
While AGI is using your computer, click the "Take over" button in the bar at the bottom of the window, or choose File > Take Over Screen Control.
Check that the bar now says "Paused. You have the screen." and that AGI stops moving the pointer.
Click "Hand back" in the bar, or choose File > Hand Back Screen Control, and check that AGI can act again.
Compare with Expected: the user can take control while AGI works and give it back.
items.needs: a Desktop app, computer use turned on, and a task that uses the screen (a Mac with screen permission for the app)
items.note: A second bar with the text "Screen control is yours. Agents cannot click or type." also exists in apps/desktop/src/features/voice/ComputerUseControlStatus.tsx; whether that bar is mounted in the app was not confirmed. The Take Over menu item is in the File menu (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts), while the plan's Code line cited the protocol and session files.

items.where: Chat > send a request that needs approval > click "Allow" on the tool card (the card text is "This tool requires approval before execution."). For computer use: "Hand back" in the Desktop bar sends a message that makes the run carry on.
steps: In a chat, send a request that makes AGI call a tool needing approval.
When the tool card shows "This tool requires approval before execution.", click "Allow".
Watch the same chat and the same tool entry: check that the run continues in this chat and does not start over.
Optional on the Desktop app: while AGI is paused, click "Hand back" in the bar; check that a new message saying the control was handed back appears and that AGI takes a new screenshot and continues.
Compare with Expected: after the user acts, the same run carries on where it stopped.
items.needs: none for the approval card (a signed-in account where a tool needs approval); the computer-use hand-back needs the Desktop app and a paused computer-use run

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

items.note: The resume after approval is handled by apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve/route.ts, which is server-side, so the tester only sees the same run continue. Whether a particular tool needs approval depends on the account's tool approval policy.

items.where: Chat > send a request that needs approval > click "Allow" or "Deny" on the tool card > read the tool summary line in the chat (the timeline).
steps: In a chat, send a request that makes AGI call a tool needing approval.
Click "Deny" on the tool card and read the tool entry: it should say "You denied this tool." as the error and "The user denied permission to run this tool." as the result.
Look at the tool timeline summary line: it should read "You denied 1 tool call" (or "You denied N tool calls").
Send another request, click "Allow", and read the summary line when the tool finishes: it should read "Tool run complete" and the tool entry should show the result.
Compare with Expected: each decision shows what was decided and what happened (denied, or ran with a result).
items.needs: none beyond a signed-in account where a tool needs approval

items.where: Composer > "Work" (the Chat | Work switch above the composer) > type the task > Send

Click "Work" in the Chat | Work switch.
Type a task in the composer and click Send.
Look for the "Review the plan" panel (a Work run starts, not a plain chat reply). Compare with Expected.

Click "Add scope (optional)".

The composer has a "Work tools" palette with "Connected apps", "Folders" and "Skills" headings (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json), but I did not find the control that opens it.

items.where: Composer > "Work" > "Add scope (optional)" > "Tools this task may use"
steps: Click "Work" in the Chat | Work switch.
Click "Add scope (optional)".
Look at "Tools this task may use" and tick or untick "Web search and browsing" or "Code execution".
Send the task and compare which tools it uses with the ticks you set.
items.needs: a paid account with Work access

items.note: Searched ComposerPlusMenu.tsx and ChatComposerNew.tsx: the only location-like control is the desktop-only "Device steps" toggle, not a cloud-versus-computer choice with visible words.

items.where: Composer footer > model selector (at the bottom of the composer, next to the Work switch)
steps: Click "Work" in the Chat | Work switch.
Open the model selector in the composer footer and choose a model.
Send the task.
Open the task in Work history and compare the model shown with the one you chose.
items.needs: a paid account with Work access
items.note: ComposerFooter shows the model selector (showModelSelector in ChatComposerNew.tsx); I did not confirm its exact visible label.

items.where: Composer footer > "Reasoning effort" button (brain icon)
steps: Click "Work" in the Chat | Work switch.
Click the button with the brain icon titled "Reasoning effort" in the composer footer.
Pick an effort level with the slider.
Send the task and compare the effort shown with your choice.
items.needs: a paid account, and a model that supports effort control
items.note: The effort button appears only when the selected model has an effort control.

items.where: Composer > "Work" > send a task > "Review the plan" panel
steps: Click "Work" in the Chat | Work switch and send a task.
Wait for the "Review the plan" panel before the agent acts.
Edit a step, click "Add a step" or "Remove this step" as needed.
Click "Start work" to approve or "Cancel" to reject, then check that the agent did not act before Start work.
items.needs: a paid account with Work access

items.where: Work history > click a task > step list
steps: Open "Work history" and click a task that has steps.
Read the numbered step list in the task detail.
Compare each step's status word with what happened.
items.needs: a paid account with a Work task that has steps
items.note: Step status words come from STATUS_LABEL in AgiWorkPlanReview.tsx; I did not confirm the exact step list screen in TaskDetailPanel.

items.where: Work history > click a running task > step marked "In progress"
steps: Start a Work task and let it run.
Open "Work history" and click the running task.
Look for the step marked "In progress" and check it matches the step being worked on.
items.needs: a paid account

items.note: Parallel tool calls are grouped by parallelGroup in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ToolTimeline.tsx, but I found no visible words for a parallel-work indicator.
Server code exists in apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts; I found no visible UI text for a clarifying question in the Work history or task components.

items.where: Work history > "Needs you" filter > task card showing "Wants to run ..." > Approve or Deny
steps: Open "Work history".
Click the "Needs you" filter.
On a card that says "Wants to run" followed by a tool name, click the approve or deny button.
Check the task continues after Approve, or stops after Deny.
items.needs: a paid account and a Work task that asks for a tool permission
items.note: The Approve and Deny button words come from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS, which I did not read.

items.where: Work history > click a running task > "Message the agent" box > Send
steps: Open "Work history" and click a running task.
Click the box with the placeholder "Message the agent to add instructions or change course".
Type the new guidance and click "Send".
Check the message shows as queued and the task continues without restarting.
items.needs: a paid account and a running Work task

items.where: Work history > running task card > "Pause"
steps: Open "Work history" and find a running task card.
Click "Pause" on the card.
Wait for the card to show "Pausing" and then the paused state.
Check the task keeps its finished steps.
items.needs: a paid account and a running Work task
items.note: The Pause button appears only on pausable tasks.

items.where: Work history > paused task card > "Resume"
