Compare the listed items (Browser, Computer use, Local models, Local MCP, Remote Control) with the Expected line.
items.needs: a linked device with capabilities
items.note: Code sessions are not in the capability list shown; the dispatcher line cited has moved.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone
steps: Click Settings, then Capabilities, and scroll to Remote Control.
Click Pair a phone.
Look for the pairing QR code and the Pairing code.
Pair the phone or a second browser, then check Settings > Account > Linked devices shows it.
Compare with the Expected line.
items.needs: a paid plan, and a phone or second browser
items.note: The claim route needs signaling settings (apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts); the plan says it was not live-checked, and I did not confirm it.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Disconnect phone
steps: With a paired phone shown, click Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control.
Click Disconnect phone and read the confirmation dialog.
Click Disconnect phone in the dialog.
Check the phone stops working, and see Settings > Account > Linked devices, where the device row has an Unlink device button.
items.needs: a paired phone, and a paid plan
a second client signed in to the account and a folder approved on the computer
items.note: Approved folders are under Settings > Capabilities > Local access > Folders > Add a folder (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/LocalAccessSection.tsx), but I found no screen on another client that starts a session; the plan says that screen is unverified and Remote Control is hidden in mobile v1.

items.where: Sidebar > Your computer
steps: In a web browser, click Your computer in the Code sidebar.
Open a computer that is offline or asleep, and read its status after its name.
Read the message: Your computer went offline. This page reconnects when it is back.
Compare with the Expected line.
items.needs: a linked computer that is offline or asleep
items.note: Settings > Account > Linked devices shows only the word Offline; the explanation appears on the Your computer page.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control
steps: With a phone paired, click Settings, Capabilities, Remote Control.
Turn off the phone's network for a moment.
Look for the message Connection lost. Reconnecting so your phone can pick up where it left off.
Turn the network back on and look for Connected to followed by the phone name.
items.needs: a paired phone and a paid plan

labels.text: Connection lost. Reconnecting so your phone can pick up where it left off.

items.note: The reconnect message only shows while the status is reconnecting.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Agent run updates
steps: Click Settings, then Notifications.
Find Agent run updates and read its line: Completions, failures and approval requests. This browser only.
Start an approval or a failing run in a session on another client.
Check whether this client shows a notification.
items.needs: two clients on the same account, and a session that needs approval
items.note: The line says This browser only, which conflicts with the cross-client Expected; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/codeSessionActivity.ts is gone, so only the reporting in apps/desktop/electron/main.ts remains.

items.where: Effect seen by opening and re-opening the app window
steps: Open AGI Desktop from the Applications folder.
Open AGI Desktop a second time and check that the one open window comes forward instead of a second copy appearing.
Close the window with the red button, then click the app icon in the Dock and check the same window returns.
items.needs: none
items.note: Single-instance and crash-recovery screen code was not located by visible words; the earlier recovery check was not re-verified.

items.where: Menu bar > File > New Chat (menu titles File, Edit, View, History, Window, Help)
steps: Click File in the menu bar and check the items listed: New Chat, New Temporary Chat, New Project, Open Folder.
Click Edit and check Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Find.
Click View and History, then Window and Help, and check each lists its items.
Click File > New Chat and check a new chat opens. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Help menu uses the system role, so its title comes from macOS, not a literal string.

items.where: Menu bar icon (AGI Desktop) > Open Desktop; > New Chat; > Quick Ask; > Screenshot to Chat; > Dictation; > Shortcuts
steps: Click the AGI Desktop icon in the menu bar.
Check the items: Open Desktop, New Chat, Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Dictation, Shortcuts, Check for Updates, Quit.
Click Shortcuts and check the shortcut choices list.
Open Settings > Desktop app > General, find the Menu bar switch, turn it off, and check the icon disappears from the menu bar.
items.needs: none
items.note: Open Desktop and Quit labels are built from a template, so their literal text was not found; the Menu bar hint is Show Desktop in the menu bar.

items.where: Red close button on the window, then the AGI Desktop icon in the Dock
steps: Open a chat window and click the red close button at the top left.
Look at the Dock: the AGI Desktop icon should still be there with its running dot.
Click the AGI Desktop icon in the Dock.
Check the chat window comes back. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Behaviour is in the app code (activate and window-all-closed handlers); no visible label on the control itself.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Quick Ask shortcut (dropdown)
steps: Open Settings, choose the Desktop app group, then General.
Find the row Quick Ask shortcut and open its dropdown.
Pick another choice, or No shortcut.

Click into another app and press the chosen key combination; check Quick Ask opens. For a conflict, check the note under the row: Already used by another Desktop shortcut or Already used by another app.
items.needs: a Desktop app build
items.note: Conflict notes come from STATUS_NOTE in the same file.

items.where: File > Quick Ask (or the Quick Ask shortcut from any app)
steps: From any other app, press the Quick Ask shortcut, or click File > Quick Ask in AGI Desktop.
Check a small window opens above the other windows.
Type a short prompt in the box and send it.
Check the answer appears in the small window.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The send control was not confirmed by visible words; the Quick Ask page is apps/web/app/quick-ask/page.tsx.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/desktop/electron and apps/web/features/desktop-host for companion; only a code comment in apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts mentions companion windows. The nearest control is Quick Ask (floating window) and Window > Always on Top.

items.where: Window > Always on Top
steps: Open a chat window and click Window in the menu bar.
Click Always on Top so it shows a tick.
Click into another app such as Notes or Finder.
Check the AGI window stays above the other windows. Click Always on Top again to turn it off.
items.needs: none
items.note: The item is greyed out when the front window cannot take the setting.

items.where: Window > New Window; Window > Move Conversation to New Window
steps: Click Window > New Window and check a second AGI window opens.
Open a conversation in one window.
Click Window > Move Conversation to New Window.
Check the conversation opens in its own window and the old window no longer shows it. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a conversation to move
items.note: Move Conversation is greyed out unless a conversation is in the front window.

items.where: File > Open Folder (folder dialog); composer + > Add photos & files (file picker)
steps: Click File > Open Folder in the menu bar.
Check the operating system's own folder dialog opens.
Choose a folder and click Open.
Check a notice says which folder was approved.
items.needs: a folder on the Mac
items.note: Only the folder path was confirmed as the OS dialog (the shell owns the directory dialog); the file picker path was not checked.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Local access > Folders
steps: Approve a folder with File > Open Folder.
Open Settings, click Capabilities, and scroll to Local access.
Quit AGI Desktop with Cmd+Q, reopen it, and return to Settings > Capabilities.
Check the folder is still listed under Folders. Click Remove access in the confirmation to revoke it, then check it disappears.
items.needs: an approved folder
items.note: Local access is rendered by Settings > Capabilities (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx).

items.where: Composer + > Attach from local folder
steps: In a new chat click the + button in the composer and click Attach from local folder.
In the dialog Attach from a local folder, open an approved folder.
Type a file name or some text in the box Search names and text and click Search.
Check the results under Matching names and Matching text.
items.needs: an approved folder and a file inside it
items.note: The assistant-side search (device-steps) was not tested from chat; only the person's dialog path was traced.

items.where: Composer + > Add working folder, then ask the assistant in chat
steps: In a new chat click + and choose Add working folder, then pick an approved folder.
Type: Create a file named test.txt in this folder with the word hello.
Check a permission prompt appears before anything is written.
Approve it and check the file exists in the folder in Finder.
items.needs: an approved folder and a Desktop build
items.note: The approval prompt wording was not located by visible words.

items.where: Composer + > Run a local command
steps: In a chat with an approved folder, click + and choose Run a local command.
Type a harmless command such as ls and send it.
Check an approval request appears before the command runs.
Approve it and check the output streams into the chat. Settings > Capabilities > Local access shows the Commands section.
items.needs: an approved folder and a Desktop build
items.note: No sandboxing text was found in LocalAccessSection, so sandboxing could not be checked from the labels.

items.where: File > Screenshot to Chat
steps: Click File > Screenshot to Chat in the menu bar.
Choose the screen to capture if asked.
Check the screenshot is attached in the chat composer.
Send it and check the image appears in the conversation.
items.needs: Screen Recording permission on macOS
items.note: The window-capture variant is Window to Chat, set in the Desktop app settings.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > Computer use (turn on Any app); then the control bar shows Take over, Hand back, Stop
steps: Open Settings, click the Desktop app group, then Computer use, and turn on Any app.
Ask the assistant in chat to click something on screen, and approve when asked.
Check the control bar labelled Computer use appears with Take over or Hand back and Stop.
Click Take over, then Stop, and check the assistant stops moving the pointer.
items.needs: Accessibility and Screen Recording permission on macOS, and a Desktop build
items.note: The Any app label is in ComputerUseSettings.tsx, which is one of the Desktop app settings pages.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities.
Scroll to Remote Control.
Click Pair a phone and check a pairing code and QR code appear.
Scan the code with the phone and check Connected to appears.
items.needs: a phone and a Desktop build
items.note: The section returns nothing unless the desktop host is present and supported; a hidden-in-v1 setting was not checked in code.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Run on startup
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General.
Turn on the switch Run on startup.
Quit AGI Desktop and log out and back in, or restart the Mac.
Check AGI Desktop opens by itself. Turn the switch off to stop it.
items.needs: a Desktop build and a restart
items.note: The macOS app menu also has Launch at Login (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts).

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Running on this Mac
steps: Start an agent task in a chat so something runs in the background.
Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General.
Find the section Running on this Mac and check it lists the running item.
Click Stop next to it and check Nothing is running in the background appears.
items.needs: a running agent or background task

labels.text: Nothing is running in the background.

items.note: The Keep computer awake switch is also in General and is a separate control.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > App version > Check for updates
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General.
Find the row App version and click Check for updates.
If a newer version exists, check the button changes to Download installer, then Relaunch to update.
If none exists, check This is the latest version appears.
items.needs: a Desktop build; a newer published version to see the update path
items.note: The UI asks for one click to download and then relaunch; it does not show a silent install, unlike Expected's by itself wording. Help menu also has Check for Updates (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts).

items.where: Help > Troubleshooting > Copy Diagnostics (or Open Logs)
steps: Click Help in the menu bar and hover Troubleshooting.
Click Copy Diagnostics.
Paste into a text field (Cmd+V) and check diagnostic text appears.
Go back to Help > Troubleshooting and click Open Logs, and check the log folder opens.
items.needs: none
items.note: Clear Cache and Restart is also under Troubleshooting; do not click it unless intended.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > Storage
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then Storage.
Check the heading Storage and the row Data folder show what is kept on the computer.
Under Clean up, click Clear for the web cache or Delete for old logs, then confirm.
Check the size goes down and the confirmation text Chats stay on this computer appears where chats are kept.
items.needs: a Desktop build
items.note: The Storage page is shown only in the Electron host.

items.where: Open an agiworkforce-cloud:// link from another app, such as Notes or Safari
steps: In Notes or Safari, open a link that starts with agiworkforce-cloud://.
Check AGI Desktop opens or comes forward.
Check it lands on the same screen the link names, such as a chat.
Click a notification the app raised and check it opens that conversation.
items.needs: a Desktop build and a link to open
items.note: Accepted link paths are in apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/deep-links.ts; the exact paths were not tested.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Permissions
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General, and scroll to Permissions.
Read Your answers and the system hint about computer use, screenshots and dictation.
Click Open System Settings to check the macOS privacy pane opens.
Click Remove on an answer and check it is gone, so Desktop asks again next time. Click Refresh to reload.
items.needs: a Desktop build and at least one saved answer
items.note: Remove button label was not found by visible words; the control is rendered by the card at DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:175-180.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Chrome. The Chrome section is shown only inside the Desktop app (it is hidden in a normal browser). Pairing starts in Chrome: open the extension side panel and choose Connect to Desktop; Desktop then opens a dialog on this Mac that shows the code.
steps: Open the Desktop app on the Mac and sign in. Open the app menu, choose Settings…, then open the Capabilities tab.
Scroll to the Chrome section. If it says Nothing has asked to pair yet, the Install extension button is shown; that is the path to the extension setup page.
In Chrome, open the AGI extension side panel and choose Connect to Desktop. A dialog opens on the Mac showing a code.
Type the code from the Desktop dialog into the Chrome side panel.
Go back to Settings > Capabilities > Chrome and look for the line Paired and answering (with a fingerprint after a dot). Compare with Expected: the extension is paired with the Desktop app.
items.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app, Chrome with the AGI extension installed, and a signed-in account
items.note: The code is shown in a dialog opened by the Desktop app (its source is apps/desktop/electron/browser/bridgeServer.ts), not on the Settings page; the dialog's own wording was not found in the web files. The Install extension button is shown only while no pairing exists yet.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Chrome. The status line shows Paired and answering or Paired, not answering right now. The reconnect action is the button Register the browser host again.
steps: Open the Desktop app, open the app menu, choose Settings…, then the Capabilities tab.
Scroll to the Chrome section and read the status line. It shows Paired and answering when the native host is connected, or Paired, not answering right now when it is not.

If the line says Paired, not answering right now, or the text The browser host is not registered, so Chrome cannot reach this app. Register it again below. appears, click Register the browser host again.
Wait for the spinner to finish. Compare with Expected: the status line changes to Paired and answering, and an error appears in red text only if registration fails.
items.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app and a paired Chrome extension (to see a connected state); a way to stop the connection, such as quitting Chrome, to see the not-answering state
items.note: The connection status comes from the native host and bridge (apps/desktop/electron/browser/bridgeServer.ts, which sets bridgeListening from the server state). The button re-registers the host; it does not have a separate Reconnect label, so the tester should treat it as the reconnect control. The status text Paired, not answering right now was not checked against a live connection.

items.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities (text-only models show Text only)
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer (its label ends in Change model).
In the Models dialog, click the About button on any model row.
Read the Capabilities line on the card.
Compare: every model accepts text, so text input has no chip of its own; a model with no other chip shows Text only.
items.needs: none
items.note: Text input is not listed as its own item; the only visible sign is the absence of a chip and the Text only label, and routing to text-only handling was not confirmed in the UI.

items.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities (text output is implied for every model)
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Read the Capabilities line and check that a chat reply comes back as text.
items.needs: none
items.note: No separate text-output control or chip exists; text output is shown only by replies appearing in the chat.

items.where: Composer > More composer options > Add photos & files, then pick a picture; Models > About <model name> > Capabilities > Vision
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer and click About on a model without a Vision chip.
Close the picker, click More composer options and choose Add photos & files, then pick a JPG or PNG file.
Click Send or look at the composer alert.

Compare: the alert should read The selected model can't read the attached image. Switch to Auto, choose an image-capable model, or remove the image. Switch to a model with the Vision chip and the alert should not appear.
items.needs: a picture file to upload, a model without Vision and one with Vision
items.note: The refusal alert text was found in ChatComposerNew.tsx; the exact send-blocking behaviour was not confirmed.

items.where: Composer > Add photos & files with several pictures; the check runs when the request is sent
steps: Click More composer options and choose Add photos & files.
Select several pictures in one go and click Send.
Compare: the request should go through or fail with a message about the image limit.
items.needs: several picture files to upload
items.note: Per-request image count limits are enforced in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/media-input.ts; no visible image-count message was found in the web composer.

items.where: Composer > More composer options > Add photos & files, then pick a PDF file
steps: Click the model name button and pick a model that cannot read documents.
Click More composer options and choose Add photos & files, then pick a PDF.
Click Send or look at the composer alert.

Compare: the alert should read The selected model can't read the attached document. Switch to Auto, choose a document-capable model, or remove the file. Switching to a document-capable model should remove the alert.
items.needs: a PDF file to upload

labels.text: The selected model can't read the attached document. Switch to Auto, choose a document-capable model, or remove the file.

items.note: The alert is shown for models without document support; whether a PDF is sent natively to a document-capable model was not checked in the UI.

items.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities > Audio in
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Look at the Capabilities chips on the card.
Compare: a model that accepts audio input shows an Audio in chip; other models do not.
items.needs: none
items.note: Only the chip was found; no audio file attach control was located in the composer.

items.where: Settings > Voice > Dictation; then the composer microphone button Start voice input
steps: Open Settings and click Voice.
Turn on the Dictation switch and check Dictation language.
Close Settings, click the microphone button labelled Start voice input in the composer, and speak.
Compare: the spoken words should be added to the message text after transcription.
items.needs: a microphone; a Free account may have dictation limits
items.note: Privacy copy says recordings go to OpenAI for transcription; the choice of transcription model is not shown on screen.

items.where: Composer > Start voice mode (icon button with a waveform)
steps: Click the button labelled Start voice mode in the composer.
Allow microphone access when asked.
Speak a short sentence and wait for a reply.
Compare: a live voice session should start and show the transcript turns of your speech.
items.needs: a microphone and a signed-in account
items.note: The realtime model name is not shown on screen; the session route is in apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts.

items.where: Assistant reply > More message actions > Read message aloud
steps: Get a text reply from the assistant.
Click the More message actions button under the reply.
Click Read message aloud.
Compare: the reply should be read aloud, and the menu item should change to Stop reading message while speaking.
items.needs: a speaker and a browser with built-in voices
items.note: Privacy copy says Read aloud uses the browser's built-in voices, not a registry-chosen model; this may differ from Expected.

items.where: Composer > Start voice mode, then speak and listen for the spoken reply
steps: Click Start voice mode in the composer.
Allow the microphone and ask a question out loud.
Listen for the spoken answer.
Compare: the reply should be spoken back during the live session, not only written in the chat.
items.needs: a microphone, speakers and a signed-in account
items.note: The speech-to-speech model is not named on screen; confirm the spoken reply in the live session.

items.where: Composer > More composer options > Create image
steps: Click More composer options in the composer.
Click Create image.
Type a short picture prompt and send it.
Compare: an image should be generated; if the chosen model cannot make images, the image mode should not start.
items.needs: none; a plan may limit image creation
items.note: Image output is also listed as an Image out chip on each model card in the Models picker.

items.where: Composer > More composer options > Create image, then Add photos & files to attach a picture
steps: Click More composer options and choose Create image.
Click More composer options again and choose Add photos & files, then pick a picture.
Type an edit instruction and send.
Compare: the edited picture should come back; the composer should warn if the file is not a picture.
items.needs: a picture file to upload
items.note: The warning Image mode takes images only was found in ChatComposerNew.tsx; which image models accept edits is not shown in the picker.

items.where: Composer > More composer options > Create video
steps: Click More composer options and choose Create video.
Type a short video prompt and check the duration or size controls.
Send the request.
Compare: the video should match the duration and size offered for the chosen model.
items.needs: none; a plan may limit video creation
items.note: No duration or size control was located in the composer code reviewed; check the screen after choosing Create video.

items.where: Generated video file after Composer > More composer options > Create video
steps: Create a short video with Create video.
Download or open the finished video.
Compare: the video should have a sound track only if the model that made it supports audio.
items.needs: a finished generated video
items.note: No audio on/off control was found; the effect is only visible in the finished video file.

items.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities > Tools
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Look for the Tools chip in Capabilities.
Compare: a model with function calling shows Tools; a model without it does not.
items.needs: none
items.note: The refusal or rerouting of tool turns to models without Tools was not confirmed in the UI.

items.where: Chat reply that uses several tools in one step (effect seen in the reply)
steps: Ask a question that needs two tools at once, such as a search plus a file lookup.
Watch the tool steps shown under the reply.
Compare: the tool steps should run together when the model supports parallel tool calls.
items.needs: a Connector or tool that the model can use
items.note: No visible setting for parallel tool calls was found.

items.where: Chat reply that calls tools over several rounds (effect seen in the reply)
steps: Ask a question that needs a search, then a follow-up tool use, such as a file lookup.
Watch the reply for several tool rounds before the final answer.
Compare: the model should use more than one tool round when needed.
items.needs: a Connector or tool that the model can use
items.note: The only visible label is the Tools chip on the model card, which is function calling rather than agentic rounds.

items.where: Composer footer > Reasoning effort control; Settings > General > Reasoning effort
steps: Open the model picker from the composer footer and pick a model that supports reasoning effort.
Click the Reasoning effort control in the composer footer and look at the levels offered.
Open Settings > General and find Reasoning effort.
Compare: only the levels that the chosen model supports should appear; Off should show a note if the model cannot turn reasoning off.
items.needs: a Free or paid account; a model with reasoning effort levels
items.note: The Off note text is Off is not supported by this model in ComposerFooter.tsx.

items.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Context ceiling
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Read the Context ceiling value in the grid of facts.
Compare: the value should match the model's context window; a very long chat should be trimmed or refused.
items.needs: none
items.note: Trimming or refusing over-long requests was not confirmed in the UI.

items.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Output ceiling
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Read the Output ceiling value.
Compare: the value should match the model's output limit, and a very long reply should stop at that size.
items.needs: none
items.note: The effect on long replies was not confirmed in the UI.

items.where: Chat reply as it is written (effect seen while the answer arrives)
steps: Send a long question to a model.
Watch the reply text while it is still arriving.
Compare: the text should appear piece by piece rather than all at once.
items.needs: none
items.note: No streaming on/off control was found; the transport choice is inside the request path.

items.where: Composer, after at least one reply in the chat: switch model with the model name button
steps: Send a message and wait for a reply in a chat.
Click the model name button in the composer footer and pick a different model.
Look at the line just above the composer footer.
Compare: the line Switching models here starts a new prompt cache should appear once there are earlier turns.
items.needs: a chat with at least one reply

labels.text: Switching models here starts a new prompt cache

items.note: The cache class per route is not shown; only the switch warning is visible.

items.needs: a workspace admin account
items.note: Searched for region, residency and countries; the only match was Allowed countries in apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceFeatureControls.tsx, which is not shown as model or provider residency in the picker.

items.where: Workspace policy page (Workspace policy link) > Zero data retention only
steps: Open the Workspace policy page (the link is labelled Workspace policy; address /workspace/policy).
Find the Zero data retention only switch.
Turn it on and save.
Compare: routes that keep data should be excluded for chats in this workspace; this routing effect is not shown on the page itself.
items.needs: a workspace admin account
items.note: The admin page path from the sidebar was not confirmed; the routing effect is inner behaviour and is not visible on screen.

items.where: Models picker: model row status text (Leaving <date> or Unavailable right now)
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer to open the Models dialog.
Look at the status text on each model row.
Compare: a model with a scheduled retirement shows Leaving <date>; a model that is down shows Unavailable right now, and it cannot be picked.
items.needs: none; the Leaving text appears only in the warning window before retirement
items.note: Retired models are excluded from the list in routing code, but the picker label for them was not located.

items.where: No screen shows route-specific capabilities, cache class, retention or price. The only related visible text is a line in the chat model picker: "Switching models here starts a new prompt cache", shown after a chat has at least one assistant reply.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has at least one reply.
Open the model picker in the composer footer and look at its bottom area.

Check that the line "Switching models here starts a new prompt cache" is shown, and that it is absent on a new empty chat. This line is about cache reset on model switch, not per-route differences; the route ranking itself has no visible effect in the UI.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account, and a chat with at least one reply

labels.text: Switching models here starts a new prompt cache

items.note: Expected asks for per-route cache class, retention, price and routing rank. The Code line cites ComposerFooter.tsx:1571 (the catalogue open branch, no route text) and auto.ts:1099 and 1169 (route rejection reasons and cache-affinity ranking, internal only). Searched for route, cacheClass and cache text in apps/web, apps/desktop, packages/ui and packages/ai; the route data lives in the generated model registry (packages/ai/model-registry), not in any visible control. The plan note says "not written yet".

items.where: No single resolver screen. Its effect shows in the composer controls and in Settings toggles, for example the Reasoning effort button.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Open the model button at the bottom of the composer and switch between two models.
Compare which controls appear (for example the Reasoning effort button) with what Expected says.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code cited at WebSettingsModal.tsx:243 is a per-feature capability-decision hook (useCapabilityDecision), not one resolver found by name.

items.where: Composer > model button > choose a model with reasoning > Reasoning effort button beside the composer
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Open the model picker from the model name button at the bottom of the composer and pick a reasoning-capable model.
Look for the Reasoning effort button in the composer footer.
Pick a model with no reasoning support and check that the Reasoning effort button is gone or changed, as Expected says.
items.needs: none
items.note: Which models have reasoning comes from live catalogue data; the exact model list was not verified.

items.where: Composer > plus menu > Add photos & files, then the model picker
steps: Open the plus menu in the composer and click Add photos & files.
Choose an image or a PDF from your computer.
Open the model picker and select a model that cannot read that file type.
Look for the warning that says the selected model can't read the attached file, and the Use Auto button, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a file to upload; a model on your plan that cannot read the file
items.note: The composer's accepted-file rules are in ChatComposerNew.tsx; the exact file-type list per model was not traced.

items.where: Composer > Reasoning effort button > slider popover
steps: Open a reasoning-capable model.
Click the Reasoning effort button in the composer footer.
Read the marks on the slider and the note under it.
Switch to another model, open the button again, and compare the marks with Expected.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Off is not supported by this model.

items.where: Composer > plus menu > Create video, then the video controls in the composer
steps: Open the plus menu and click Create video.
Open the Video model button.
Look at the Video aspect ratio, Video quality and Video length buttons in the composer.
Change the video model and check that the offered settings change, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account (video generation is gated by plan)
items.note: Whether a Free account sees these controls was not verified.

items.where: Sidebar > Code (the Code page)
steps: Sign in with a Free account and click Code in the sidebar.
Look for the notice Code is on paid plans and the Upgrade button.
Sign in with a paid account and check the Code page changes.
Compare with Expected; the server-side check cannot be seen from the screen.
items.needs: a Free account and a paid account
items.note: The server refusal on the session route is not visible to a person; only the UI state is.

items.where: Settings window > Usage
steps: Open the Settings window and click Usage.
Read the percent used bars and the note about the UTC calendar month.
Check the limit message, for example Limit reached, when a limit is used up.
Compare what is shown with the allowance shown elsewhere in Settings, as Expected says.
items.needs: a paid account with some usage (or a Free account)
items.note: How the Settings window is opened was not traced in code; Usage is the settings nav item.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy
steps: Sign in as a workspace owner or admin and open Settings, then Workspace.
Click Workspace administration, then Policy.
Change a setting such as Zero data retention only and save.
Sign in as a member of the same workspace and check the restricted choice is limited, as Expected says.
items.needs: an admin account in a workspace and a second account in the same workspace
items.note: The console page is also at /workspace/policy.

items.where: Settings > Workspace
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin and open Settings, then Workspace; note the Transfer ownership button.
Sign in as a plain member of the same workspace and open Settings, then Workspace.
Check that owner and admin controls (such as Transfer ownership) are not shown.
Compare with Expected; the server refusal cannot be seen from the screen.
items.needs: an admin account and a member account in the same workspace

items.where: Settings > Privacy > Only use AI providers based in the US
steps: Open Settings and click Privacy.
Turn on Only use AI providers based in the US.
Open the model picker and look for models that are marked unavailable.
Compare with Expected; the note says models without a US-based provider are unavailable.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Only use AI providers based in the US

items.note: The label string is in apps/web/features/settings/components/UsOnlyRoutingPanel.tsx (const LABEL); the Privacy nav item is in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts.

items.where: Sign-up > Confirm your age step
steps: Start a new account on the sign-up page and reach the Confirm your age step.
Read the notice that says this service is for adults.
Complete the step with an age under 18 if the step offers that choice.
Check the screen that tells you that you must be at least 18 to continue, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a new account to sign up
items.note: The ineligible wording is built from a template in packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts, and the age input itself was not traced; the cited RecordTermsAcceptance.tsx lines moved.

items.where: Plugins (composer plus menu) > a plugin page (/plugins/<id>) > Required connectors
steps: Open a plugin that needs connectors from the Plugins item in the composer plus menu.
Scroll to Required connectors.
Look at each connector row: Checking, then Connected or a Connect link.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account where some connectors are not connected yet
items.note: The route from the Plugins item to a plugin page was not traced; the plugin page URL is /plugins/<id>.

items.where: Code page > the Code more menu > Work with local code (Desktop app)
steps: Sign in on the web app and click Code in the sidebar.
Open the Code menu that holds Work with local code.
Hover or read the Desktop app row: the status says the paired desktop is online, asleep or offline.
Compare with Expected; with no paired desktop the row links to the download page.
items.needs: a Desktop app signed in to the same account (to see online or offline status)
items.note: The status text comes from apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-paired-desktop.ts; the exact trigger label of the Code more menu was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar > Code
steps: Sign in and click Code in the sidebar.
If the deployment has managed environments off, read Managed environments are not enabled on this deployment.
If the plan does not include them, read Your plan does not include managed environments.
Compare with Expected; when the environment is being prepared the page says it is still being prepared.
items.needs: a Free account (to see the plan notice)

labels.text: Your plan does not include managed environments.

items.note: Which of the two notices shows depends on the live deployment setting.

items.where: Composer > model button > Models picker
steps: Open the model picker from the model name button in the composer.
Look for rows with Coming soon or Beta labels and rows marked Not available in this app.
Look for a row marked Temporarily unavailable.
Compare the wording: Temporarily unavailable means a temporary provider problem; Not available in this app means not offered here.
items.needs: none (a provider outage must be present for the Temporarily unavailable row)
items.note: The Temporarily unavailable state depends on live provider status, so it may not appear in a normal test run.

items.where: Composer > plus menu > Use the browser (Desktop app only)
steps: In the web app, open the composer plus menu and note that Use the browser, Run a local command and Use this computer are not listed.
Open the same plus menu in the Desktop app.
Check that Use the browser appears there.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: the Desktop app on a Mac, and the web app in a browser
items.note: The rows appear only when the desktop host is present (ChatComposerNew.tsx sets showDesktopActionRows from desktopHost).

items.where: Composer > model button > Models picker > a locked row
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open the model picker.
Find a row with a lock label such as an upgrade-plan label, or Coming soon.
Hover or click the locked row and read the reason.
Check the row stays visible and shows why it is locked, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: Locked rows read as '<plan> and above' built from a template; the exact plan label depends on the catalogue.

items.where: Composer > model button > Models picker > locked row > Upgrade to use, and the link What each plan includes
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open the model picker.
Find a row marked Upgrade to use with a plan name.
Click the row or the link What each plan includes.
Check that the plan that unlocks it is named and the upgrade path is reachable, as Expected says.
items.needs: a Free account

items.where: Plugins page for a plugin (/plugins/<id>) > Required connectors > Connect
steps: Open a plugin that needs connectors.
Find a connector row that shows Connect.
Click Connect and confirm it opens the connectors page.
Compare with Expected: the connector to connect is named in the row and the link gives the way to connect.
items.needs: an outside account (such as Google or GitHub) to finish connecting
items.note: The Connect link goes to /connectors.

items.where: Composer > plus menu > Use the browser (Desktop app)
steps: In the Desktop app, open the composer plus menu and click Use the browser.
Read the dialog text that says every action asks you first.
Open Settings > Voice and look at the Microphone choice.
Compare with Expected; no microphone permission explanation was found before the system prompt.
items.needs: the Desktop app; a Chrome extension paired for the browser text; a microphone for the Voice settings
items.note: The dictation start error shows The microphone could not be started. Try again. (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-dictation.ts); no pre-permission explanation for the microphone was found.

items.where: Composer > plus menu > Add photos & files, then the model picker
steps: Attach an image from Add photos & files.
Open the model picker and choose a model that cannot read images.
Read the warning that says the selected model can't read the attached image.
Check the Use Auto button and the Choose a compatible model button, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: an image file; a model on your plan that cannot read images
items.note: The server-side refusal text for an unsupported feature is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts.

items.where: Code page > Work with local code (Desktop app)
steps: Sign in on the web app and open Code.
Open the Code menu that holds Work with local code, and choose the Desktop app row.
If the Desktop app is paired and online, check that the link opens the same work in Desktop.
Compare with Expected; there is no equivalent action in the chat composer.
items.needs: a Desktop app signed in to the same account
items.note: The session menu also has a Desktop app row (CodeSessionMenu.tsx); the trigger for the Code more menu was not confirmed.

items.where: Composer > model button > On this device (local models); workspace owners set Your own keys and Cloud in Workspace administration > Policy
steps: Open the model picker and look for the section On this device.
Choose a local model there and send a message.
As a workspace admin, open Workspace administration > Policy and read the Local, Your own keys and Cloud modes.

items.note: No video usage row was found on the Usage page. Searched UsageSection.tsx for Video; only a video_seconds key in a counts mapping and a VideoCostEstimate in the composer were found.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area > Deep Research
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and check the By product area table.
Find the row Deep Research.
Compare its credits and request count with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account that has run Deep Research
items.note: Usage is attributed to research when the work mode is research.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area > AGI Code and AGI Work
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and open the By product area table.
Find the rows AGI Code and AGI Work.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account that has used coding or work mode
items.note: none

items.needs: a paid account
items.note: No storage row was found on the Usage page. Searched UsageSection.tsx; only a knowledge-files route in apps/web/app/api/projects was found, which is not a settings screen.

items.where: Settings > Usage
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Look for the line labelled Responses running now.
Read the value shown as N of M at a time.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with a response running
items.note: The row only appears when the usage read returns a responses value; the card it sits in was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the rows Bonus credits and Purchased credits.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: none

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, read the Purchased credits row and the Bonus credits row.
Read the sentence starting Past a plan limit, bonus credits go first.
In Plan usage limits, check the included allowance bars, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account that has bought credits

labels.text: Past a plan limit, bonus credits go first

items.note: none

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances > Bonus credits
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, find the row Bonus credits.
Read the amount and the line Next expiry with its date, or the note about referrals and promotions if there are none.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free or paid account that has received a promotional or referral credit
items.note: The copy promises a referral or promotion credit; whether a credit can be given to the tester depends on the account.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, read the detail line under Bonus credits, which shows Next expiry with a date.
Read the detail line under Purchased credits.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with bonus or purchased credits
items.note: Plan-reset timing appears in Plan usage limits; this item covers the credit rows only.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Plan usage limits, read the detail under Current session or This week.
Look for the Resets at or reset-in text next to each bar.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The countdown text itself is built in formatUsageResetIn in packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts and was not read in full.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Where your usage went, find the segmented control with Days, Weeks and Months.
Click Weeks, then Months, and watch the history table change.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
items.note: none

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By project
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Find the table captioned By project.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with usage inside a project
items.note: Rows with no project in the workspace show the text Project not in this workspace.

items.where: Sidebar > Tasks > open a task > Cost and usage
steps: Click Tasks in the sidebar.
Open any task from the list.
Find the section titled Cost and usage in the task panel.
Read the cost and token line, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account that has run a task
items.note: The sidebar path to Tasks was not confirmed on screen; the label comes from project-icons.ts.

items.where: Chat composer > Deep Research > send a research request > Research activity
steps: Choose Deep Research in the composer, type a question and do not send yet, or send it.
Look in the research activity panel for the line that starts with up to ~ and shows credits.
Compare the estimate with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account
items.note: The composer entry point for Deep Research was not verified; the estimate line is built in ResearchActivity.tsx.

items.where: Sidebar > Tasks > open a finished task > Cost and usage
steps: Click Tasks in the sidebar.
Open a task that has finished.
Find Cost and usage and read the cost line and the tokens line.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with a finished task
items.note: The note Cost and token usage are recorded when this task settles appears while a task is still running.

items.where: Chat > composer area > usage warning banner
steps: Use an account that is close to a plan limit and open a chat.
Look above the composer for the usage warning banner.
Read the headline and compare with Expected.
Click Try later to dismiss, or Get more usage to upgrade.
items.needs: an account near a usage limit
items.note: It shows only when the account is near a limit; it cannot be forced on a fresh account.

items.where: Chat > send a message after a limit is reached > paywall card in the chat
steps: Use an account that has reached a limit and send a chat message.
Look for the card in the chat that says a limit was reached.
Read the headline and the buttons, such as Buy credits or Upgrade.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account at a usage limit
items.note: The headline text is one of several per refusal reason; the card is rendered inline in the message list.

items.where: Chat > send a message after a limit is reached > paywall card > Switch to [model name]
steps: Use an account that is blocked from the chosen model and send a message.
Look in the paywall card for a button starting Switch to followed by a model name.
Click it and check the chat now uses that model.
Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an account blocked from one model
items.note: The button text is a template with the model name; the label shown is the fixed prefix Switch to.

items.where: Chat > send a message while the plan's usage is used up, then read the blocked card
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan usage is used up (or wait for the limit to be hit in a chat).
Send a message in the chat composer.
Read the blocked card that appears in the chat message list.
Look for the sentence 'Upgrade or wait for the reset.' and any reset time shown under the headline; compare with Expected (wait option plus reset time, alongside paying).
items.needs: a Free account or an account at a usage limit

labels.text: Upgrade or wait for the reset.

items.note: Plan item ID S82.28 is absent from the plan file, so the range has six items (27, 29-33). The reset time text comes from paywallResetLabel in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx, whose exact wording I did not read. The wait button text for the free-capacity case is a constant (FREE_CAPACITY_RETRY_LABEL) I did not resolve, and it shows a countdown 'in ...'.

items.where: Chat > send a message at a limit > blocked card > 'Buy credits'
steps: Reach a usage limit in chat with an account that can buy credits.
Read the blocked card and find the button 'Buy credits'.
Click 'Buy credits' and note the page or dialog that opens.
Compare with Expected: the purchase starts from where the limit was hit.
items.needs: a paid account that can buy credits, at a usage limit
items.note: The button appears only when the server's recovery action is top_up (apps/web/features/chat/lib/quotaPaywallSlot.ts). Settings > Billing also has a top-up panel, but its visible title was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Billing > 'Auto-reload' panel
steps: Open Settings and go to the Billing section.
Scroll to the panel titled 'Auto-reload'.
Turn auto-reload on, set the threshold and save; a dialog titled 'Turn on auto-reload?' appears first.
Compare with Expected: the balance threshold and reload amount can be set and saved.
items.needs: a paid account with card billing (Stripe)
items.note: The panel is shown only when the account can buy top-ups and billing is through Stripe (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx). The Settings nav label for Billing was not confirmed.

items.where: Workspace console > usage analytics > 'Monthly spend limit' card
steps: Sign in as the owner of a workspace and open the workspace console (nav title 'Workspace').
Open the usage analytics view that holds the card.
Find the card titled 'Monthly spend limit'.
Set a monthly cap and pick the enforcement option 'Block' (other option 'Notify'), then save.
Compare with Expected: once the cap is reached, managed usage stops.
items.needs: an owner account in a workspace
items.note: The card is mounted inside WorkspaceUsageAnalytics (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceUsageAnalytics.tsx). The exact tab label that opens it was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Usage > 'Download CSV'
steps: Open Settings and go to the Usage section.
Scroll to the buttons under the history chart.
Click 'Download CSV' and wait for the file to save.
Open the CSV and compare with Expected: a usage report file is downloaded.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Settings nav label for Usage was not found in the code (searched apps/web/features/settings for the 'Usage' label without a match), so the path opens from the Usage section itself.

items.where: Settings > Usage > 'Report a billing problem'
steps: Open Settings and go to the Usage section.
Scroll to the buttons under the history chart and click 'Report a billing problem'.
Fill in the message and the period, then submit.
Compare with Expected: the report is sent and a confirmation or tracking result appears.
items.needs: none
items.note: The form posts to /api/usage/discrepancy (apps/web/app/api/usage/discrepancy/route.ts). The success message after submit was not read.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Compare plans (paid plan); Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan (Free plan)
steps: Sign in and open Settings, then Billing.
On a paid plan, click Compare plans. On the Free plan, click Upgrade plan, which opens the plan chooser instead.
On the pricing page, scroll to the Compare plans heading and the table under it.
Check that prices, Usage rows and feature rows can be compared across plans before choosing one.
items.needs: a paid account to see Compare plans; a Free account for Upgrade plan
items.note: The chat upgrade dialog (UpgradePlanDialog.tsx) also has See all plans and a Compare plans link to /pricing; those are a second route to the same comparison.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Compare plans > Team & Enterprise tab > Monthly / Annual
steps: Open Settings, then Billing, then click Compare plans.
On the pricing page, click the Team & Enterprise button in the audience toggle.
Find the group with the buttons Monthly and Annual.
Click Annual, then Monthly, and compare the displayed seat prices and the line that says billed yearly or billed monthly.
items.needs: none for viewing prices; a signed-in account to see the plan-state wording
items.note: The toggle is shown only on the Team & Enterprise tab and only when yearly checkout is ready; the Individual plans on the same page are monthly only in the code.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Subscribe to (plan name)
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open Settings, then Billing.
Click Upgrade plan, then click Continue with and the plan name.
Read the Order details box, then click Subscribe to and the plan name (or Start free trial if shown).
Expect a Stripe Checkout page to open; then look for the plan showing as active in Billing.
items.needs: a Free account that is not on the billing waitlist, and a Stripe test card
items.note: Owner decision is open on this item. Paid checkout is behind the billing waitlist and an access code, so a waitlisted account sees a waitlist or access-code message instead of checkout.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Switch to a smaller plan
steps: Sign in with a paid Stripe-billed account and open Settings, then Billing.
Click Switch to a smaller plan.
In the dialog, pick a plan under the Plan heading and read the panel titled What changes on that plan.
Look for the rows Plan price, plus tax, Usage, Limits and Not included, and the line that says when the change starts, then compare with the Switch on (date) or Switch to (plan) button.
items.needs: a paid Stripe-billed account with no scheduled change; Team and Enterprise plans change in Manage billing instead
items.note: The button is hidden when the account has no Stripe billing, is on a Team or Enterprise plan, or already has a scheduled change.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Adjust plan > Continue with (plan name) > Order details
steps: Sign in with a paid Stripe-billed account and open Settings, then Billing.
Click Adjust plan, then Continue with and a higher plan name.
Read the note that starts with Upgrading starts a new billing period today, and the Order details box with its credit row.
Look for the Total due today line and the renewal sentence below it, and compare them with the note.
items.needs: a paid Stripe-billed account that has a higher plan to move to, and a Stripe test card

labels.text: Upgrading starts a new billing period today, with credit for unused time on your plan.

items.note: The proration rows are Stripe lines shown from the preview, so the exact credit amount depends on the account.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Order details
steps: Open Settings, then Billing, then click Upgrade plan (Free) or Adjust plan (paid).
Click Continue with and a plan name to open the order page.
Read the Order details box: Subtotal, Tax, Total and Total due today.
Compare the Tax line with the note Tax is calculated at checkout.
items.needs: a Free or paid account; the order box needs a working price preview
items.note: Tax appears as a line only when the preview returns it; otherwise the order box says tax is calculated at checkout.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Add a promotion code
steps: Open the order page: Settings, then Billing, then Upgrade plan, then Continue with and a plan name.
Click Add a promotion code.
Type a code into the field with the placeholder Promotion code and click the apply button.
Check that the Order details box updates with a Discount line, or shows an error if the code is not valid.
items.needs: a Free or paid account and a valid promotion code
items.note: The same code box is inside the upgrade confirm dialog, which is opened from the chat upgrade flow.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Start free trial
steps: Open the order page: Settings, then Billing, then Upgrade plan, then Continue with and a plan name.
Read the trial line in Order details, which gives the end date and the charge after it.
Compare the trial line with the button Start free trial, and note that Checkout asks for a card.
After starting a trial, open Settings > Billing and read the notice that starts with Your and the trial length and says free trial.
items.needs: a Free account for a plan that offers a trial, and a Stripe test card
items.note: Trial terms are built in apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts (trialDisclosure) and in BillingPlanNotices; whether a trial is offered depends on the plan.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Payment > Add payment method
steps: Sign in with an account that has no card on file and open Settings, then Billing.
Find the Payment heading and read the line saying No card on file.
Click Add payment method, which opens the billing portal in a new page (Stripe).
Add a Stripe test card in the portal, return to Billing and check the card appears under Payment.
items.needs: an account with no saved card; a Stripe test card
items.note: On the order page, the Payment method box also has an Add button; the card form itself is Stripe-hosted.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Payment
steps: Open Settings, then Billing, and find the Payment heading.
Look for the saved card line with a Default tag on the default card.
Click Manage cards to open the billing portal.
In the portal, change or remove a card, then return to Billing and check the Payment list again.
items.needs: a paid account with at least one saved card
items.note: Setting a default card and removing a card are done in the Stripe portal, not in an AGI control.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Subscribe to (plan name), then the Stripe Checkout page
steps: Start a paid checkout as in S83.03 until the Stripe Checkout page opens.
On the Stripe page, find the billing address fields, which are required.
Enter an address, then go back to Settings > Billing to see if it was kept.
Compare with the address shown in the Stripe billing portal after Manage billing.
items.needs: a Free account with checkout open, and a Stripe test card
items.note: No AGI screen has an address field; the address is collected on Stripe's own page (apps/web/lib/billing/tax-policy.ts sets billing_address_collection required).

items.needs: a Free account with checkout open, and a business test customer
items.note: Searched for Tax ID and VAT in apps/web and packages/ui: the code turns on tax_id_collection in Stripe Checkout (apps/web/lib/billing/tax-policy.ts:103), but no AGI screen has a tax ID input; the Tax ID key in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/pricing.json is not used by any component. Whether Stripe's page shows the field is not verified in code.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Subscribe to (plan name), then return to the app
steps: Complete a paid checkout in Stripe (see S83.03).
Wait on the page after Stripe returns; the app polls the plan for a short time.
Look for the heading Payment received. or Checkout confirmed. and the plan name with its status.
Open Settings > Billing and check the plan name and status match the confirmation.
items.needs: a Free account and a Stripe test card
items.note: The confirmation page lives at /billing after success=true; it shows You're all set. with the plan name.

items.where: Settings > Billing (red notice at the top of the plan card)
steps: Sign in with an account whose renewal payment failed (needs a Stripe test card that declines).
Open Settings, then Billing.
Look at the red notice that says your payment did not go through and the plan is past due or unpaid.
Check that the notice names the buttons Update payment method and, when an invoice is open, Pay (amount) now.
items.needs: a paid Stripe account with a failed renewal

labels.text: why a payment fails and what to do

items.note: The notice shows only for past_due or unpaid status; it is not shown on the first payment attempt at checkout, which uses the payment-failure page instead.

items.where: Settings > Billing > red payment notice > Update payment method or Pay (amount) now
steps: Sign in with an account in a failed-payment state and open Settings, then Billing.
Click Update payment method; the billing portal opens in a new page.
Or click Pay (amount) now to open the open invoice in a new page.
Also open the link why a payment fails and what to do, which opens the Open billing help page; click Open billing and check the notice returns to a normal state after payment.
items.needs: a paid account with a failed or open invoice, and a Stripe test card
items.note: There is no separate retry button; retry happens by paying the open invoice or updating the card. Try again on the billing page only reloads the data.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Invoices, and Settings > Billing > Credit purchases
steps: Open Settings, then Billing.
Scroll to the Invoices heading and read the list of dates, totals and status.
Scroll further to the Credit purchases heading and the Refunds heading below it.
Compare the rows with the purchases you made.
items.needs: a paid account with at least one invoice; a credit purchase for the second list
items.note: The separate /billing/invoices page has no link from any app screen; it can be reached only by typing its address.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Invoices > View (or Pay for an open invoice)
steps: Open Settings, then Billing, then find the Invoices list.
Click the View link on a paid invoice; it opens the invoice in a new page.
Check the invoice opens with the right date, total and status.
Look for a PDF download on that page.
items.needs: a paid account with at least one issued invoice
items.note: A PDF link (invoice_pdf) exists only on /billing/invoices (InvoiceList.tsx), which no app screen links to; whether the Stripe-hosted page offers a PDF is not verified in code.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Credit purchases > View receipt
steps: Open Settings, then Billing, and scroll to the Credit purchases list.
Find a credit purchase row with a View receipt link.
Click View receipt; it opens the receipt in a new page.
Check the receipt amount matches the row. Rows with no receipt show Not issued yet.
items.needs: an account that has bought a credit pack
items.note: This list covers credit purchases; plan payments are listed under Invoices, not here.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Refunds
steps: Open Settings, then Billing, and scroll to the Refunds list (newest first).
Find a refund row and read its status: Processing, Action needed, Refunded, Failed or Canceled.
Compare the status with the refund's state in the payment provider.
Check the amount and date on the row.
items.needs: an account with at least one refund (created by the owner or a Stripe test refund)
items.note: The code has no status labelled requested; the first state shown is Processing.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Cancel plan
steps: Sign in with a paid Stripe-billed account and open Settings, then Billing.
Click Cancel plan; the billing portal opens on the cancel screen.
Confirm the cancellation in the portal.
Return to Billing and check that the plan shows an Ends on date and the button Resume (plan) appears.
items.needs: a paid Stripe-billed account (not Apple, Google or organization billing)
items.note: The confirmation happens in the Stripe portal, not in an AGI dialog.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Resume (plan name)
steps: After a cancellation (S83.21), open Settings, then Billing.
Find the notice that says Your (plan) plan ends on (date).
Click the button Resume (plan name).
Check that the notice disappears and the Cancel plan button comes back.
items.needs: a paid Stripe account with a scheduled cancellation
items.note: The same resume control is used for a trial that is set to end ('Continue (plan) after the trial').

items.where: Settings > Billing > plan card row Ends on
steps: Cancel a paid Stripe plan (S83.21).
Open Settings, then Billing, and look at the plan card rows.
Find the row labelled Ends on with a date.
Compare the date with the notice that says Your (plan) plan ends on (date).
items.needs: a paid Stripe account with a scheduled cancellation
items.note: The row label changes with the state: Trial ends on, Renews on or Current period ends are the other labels.

items.where: Settings > Billing > notice after Cancel plan
steps: Cancel a paid Stripe plan (S83.21).
Open Settings, then Billing, and read the notice below the plan card.
Read the sentence starting You keep (plan) features and credits until then.
Check that it ends with Free; your chats, projects and files stay.
items.needs: a paid Stripe account with a scheduled cancellation

labels.text: Free; your chats, projects and files stay.

items.note: The same explanation appears on the Upgrade page (apps/web/app/upgrade/UpgradeChooser.tsx) for an ending plan.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Manage in the App Store or Manage on Google Play
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan is billed by Apple or Google (bought in the mobile app).
Open Settings, then Billing, and find the Billed through row, which names the store.
Click Manage in the App Store (or Manage on Google Play); the store page opens in a new window.
Check that Cancel plan and Switch to a smaller plan are not shown for this account.
items.needs: an account billed through the Apple App Store or Google Play
items.note: The Billed through row text comes from BILLING_SOURCE_LABEL in BillingSection.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > Continue with (plan name) > Subscribe to (plan name)
steps: Use an account that already has an active subscription with the payment provider but does not show it as a paid plan.
Open the order page and click Subscribe to (plan name).
Read the red error line under the order box.
Check that the message says to open Billing to manage it, or contact support.
items.needs: an account with an active Stripe subscription that the app does not show as paid (hard to set up)

labels.text: This account already has an active subscription with our payment provider.

items.note: Paid accounts normally see Adjust plan instead of Upgrade plan, so the warning appears only on a conflict; the code returns it from the server, and no pre-purchase warning dialog was found.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Compare plans (opens /pricing) > Team card > Seats box > Get Team. A team owner whose plan already bills per seat sees Update seats instead. Adding seats later: Settings > Workspace > Seats & billing > Change seats (opens /pricing with the seat count).
steps: Sign in as the account that would own the Team workspace. Open Settings, then Billing, then click Compare plans.
On the Team card, change the number in the Seats box (minimum 2) and read the total line that shows Seats: N and the monthly total.
Click Get Team. If upgrades are on the waitlist, the button reads Join the Team waitlist, or Enter access code if you already joined.

Compare with Expected: the seat count is chosen before purchase, and checkout or the waitlist/access-code message appears. For adding seats later, use Settings > Workspace > Seats & billing > Change seats and check the Seats box is pre-filled with the current licensed count.
items.needs: a Free account (or a team owner account to test adding seats); a second account is not needed. Paid checkout is held behind the billing waitlist by the owner's decision, so a Free tester may see the waitlist or access-code message instead of checkout.
items.note: The Team button label switches to Join the {plan} waitlist, You're on the waitlist and Enter access code while upgrades are waitlisted (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:424-430 and around line 596). Plain Settings > Workspace > Choose Team seats (apps/web/features/settings/sections/TeamSection.tsx) is the entry for a non-Team user. Whether the Settings entry in the account menu is labelled Settings was not traced; the Settings nav labels are in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Seats & billing (figures Licensed, In use, Available, and Premium seats if the workspace bills seats). On each member row, the Seat type dropdown. Workspace console: Workspace > Billing shows Seats used as X of Y.
steps: Sign in as the workspace owner or an admin. Open Settings, then Workspace.
Find the card titled Seats & billing and read the Licensed, In use and Available figures.
On a member row, open the seat dropdown (it reads Standard seat or Premium seat) and pick the other seat type.
Confirm the dialog that appears, then compare the In use count and the Premium seats assigned count with Expected: admins can assign seats and see seats used against licensed.
items.needs: a workspace owner or admin account; a workspace with seat billing (Premium seats) for the dropdown to appear; a second member in the same workspace to change a seat on. Without seat billing the row shows static text instead of the dropdown.
items.note: The seat dropdown is only shown to admins on seat-billed workspaces (TeamSection.tsx, around line 1325). Invitations also reserve a seat (the note Active members and pending invitations each reserve one seat). How a person reaches the Workspace console from the first screen was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Seats & billing > Review contract (opens Workspace > Billing) > Enterprise contract > Contacts. Rows: Billing contact and Procurement contact.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin of a workspace that has an enterprise contract on record. Open Settings, then Workspace.
In the Seats & billing card, click Review contract.
On the billing page, scroll to the Enterprise contract card and find the Contacts section.
Read the Billing contact and Procurement contact rows and compare with Expected: each shows a name and email, or Not on record. The card is read only.
items.needs: an owner or admin account on a workspace with a contract on record (the contract is entered by billing staff, not in the app). Without a contract, a contract-priced workspace shows No contract is on record for this workspace.; other plans see no contract card at all.
items.note: Review contract shows only when the workspace is contract-priced; otherwise the button reads Change seats. The Billing contact and Procurement contact row labels are in WorkspaceEnterpriseContract.tsx.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Seats & billing > Review contract > Enterprise contract card (rows Payment terms and Purchase order) and the Invoices table in the same page.
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin of a contract-priced workspace. Open Settings, then Workspace, then click Review contract.
In the Enterprise contract card, read the Payment terms row (Net N, Due on receipt, or As stated on each invoice).
Read the Purchase order row (a PO number or Not on record).

Scroll to the Invoices section and read the Invoice, Period, Due, Status and Amount columns, then check the Links column; compare with Expected: PO numbers and invoice terms are shown. Buying by purchase order or reporting a bank transfer has no control on any screen.
items.needs: an owner or admin account on a contract-priced workspace with a contract on record and at least one invoice (created by billing staff, not in the app).
items.note: Offline payment reporting (bank transfer with a remittance reference) exists only as the POST API route apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/billing-contract/route.ts; no button or form for it was found in apps/web or packages/ui, so a person cannot reach it from the UI. Purchase-order buying has no screen either. Only the display of PO and terms is reachable.

items.where: Settings > Billing > Credit history (table with Date, Description, Amount), and the Credit purchases section below it.
steps: Sign in with an account that has bought credits (a top-up). Open Settings, then Billing.
Scroll to the Credit history card and read the rows; a credit purchase appears with the description Top-up purchase.
Scroll further to the Credit purchases section and read each purchase row, including its receipt link.
Compare with Expected: every credit purchase is listed, newest first. A Free account with no purchases sees No credit activity yet... or No credit purchases yet.

items.where: Settings > General > Display Language
steps: Open Settings and choose General in the settings list (the group is titled Settings).
Find the row labelled Display Language and open its drop-down (options show a flag and the language's own name).
Pick a different language.
Look at whether the interface text switches to that language, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The drop-down's accessible name is Display language (LanguageSelector.tsx); how Settings is opened from the first screen was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Theme
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Theme with three buttons: System, Light, Dark.
Click Light, then Dark, then System.
Look whether the colours of the whole app change each time and whether the choice is still selected after closing and reopening Settings.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Accent colour
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Accent colour and its group of colour buttons.
Click a different accent colour.
Look whether buttons, links and highlights across the app take the new colour.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Chat text size
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Chat text size and open its drop-down.
Choose Large, then Small.
Open a chat with several messages and look whether message text grows and shrinks.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Motion
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Motion with two buttons: System and Reduced.
Click Reduced.

Find the row labelled Code theme and open its drop-down.
Pick a different code theme.
Open a chat that shows a code block and look whether its colours change.

items.where: Settings > Appearance > Wrap long code lines
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Wrap long code lines and turn its switch on or off.
Open a chat with a code block that has a very long line.
Look whether the long line wraps onto the next line or runs off to the side.
items.needs: a chat with a long line of code

items.where: Settings > General > Default model
steps: Open Settings and choose General.
Find the row labelled Default model and open its drop-down; the first option is Last used.
Pick a model name (a model marked Upgrade to use is locked to your plan).
Open a new chat and look whether the model picker starts on the chosen model.

items.where: Settings > General > Reasoning effort
steps: Open Settings and choose General.
Find the row labelled Reasoning effort and open its drop-down.
Choose a different effort level (levels above your plan are marked and cannot be picked).
Open a new chat and look whether the effort picker in the composer shows the chosen level.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > General > New chats start in
steps: Open Settings and choose General.
Find the row labelled New chats start in and open its drop-down (options Chat and Work).
Choose Work.
Click the new-chat control and look whether the new chat opens in Work mode.

items.note: The row shows a plan-entitlement hint from planCapabilityEntitlementHint; the exact gating was not traced.

items.where: Settings > General > Composer > Send with Enter
steps: Open Settings and choose General, then scroll to the heading Composer.
Turn the switch on the row labelled Send with Enter on or off.
Read the hint under the row (it says Off: Enter starts a new line and the key combination sends).
Open a chat, type two lines, press Enter, and look whether the message sends or a new line is added.
items.needs: none
