items.where: Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts > View shortcuts, or Settings > Keyboard
steps: Open Settings and choose General, then find the row labelled Keyboard shortcuts and click View shortcuts (or choose the Keyboard item in the settings list).
Read the list of shortcuts and search with the field labelled Search shortcuts.
Click the control labelled Change keys for a rebindable shortcut and press a new key combination.
Turn off a shortcut with its on/off switch and look whether the list updates and the key stops working.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Notifications
steps: Open Settings and choose Notifications.
Find the event rows (for example Reply ready, Scheduled task finished, Security alerts) and open the choice for each.
Choose a channel combination (Browser, Email, Mobile push, or Push where shown) or Off.
Trigger or wait for that event and look whether it arrives on the chosen channel only.
items.needs: a second device or email inbox to confirm delivery; mobile push needs the phone app
items.note: Channel names are Browser, Email, Mobile push and Push (per event); the exact menu for picking channels was not fully traced.

items.where: Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours
steps: Open Settings and choose Time and focus.
Find the row labelled Quiet hours and turn on its switch labelled Enable quiet hours.
Set the start and end time using the fields labelled Quiet hours start and Quiet hours end.
Read the note under the row (it says notifications are held, and approvals and failures still arrive) and compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: Whether notifications are actually held during the window needs a real notification to check; that was not traced.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Run on startup (desktop app only)
steps: In the desktop app, open Settings and choose General under the group Desktop app.
Find the row labelled Run on startup and turn its switch on.
Optionally open the Mac app menu (the app name menu) and look for the item Launch at Login, which should show a tick.
Quit and reopen the Mac, or log out and back in, and look whether AGI opens by itself.

items.note: The desktop settings row is shown only when the app runs in the desktop host; the Launch at login label in apps/desktop/src is the internal Tauri build and is not the public app.

items.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Quick Ask shortcut (desktop app only)
steps: In the desktop app, open Settings, choose General under Desktop app, and find the row labelled Quick Ask shortcut.
Open its drop-down (it lists shortcut choices, and No shortcut) and pick a different key combination or No shortcut.
Press the chosen combination from another app and look whether the Quick Ask window appears.
Open the Mac app menu or File menu and look for the item Quick Ask to compare the shortcut shown.
items.needs: the Electron desktop app on a Mac
items.note: The window's position on screen was not traced; the hint says it is for messaging AGI from anywhere on the desktop.

items.where: Settings > General > Sidebar items
steps: Open Settings and choose General, then find the row labelled Sidebar items.
Click a destination name (the hint says Hide anything you do not use from the left rail) to switch it off; click again to switch it on.
Close Settings and look at the left rail; the switched-off item should disappear and reappear when switched back on.
Check whether there is any control for collapsed-by-default or auto-hide (none was found).

labels.text: Hide anything you do not use from the left rail.

items.where: Settings > General > Full name (email is under Settings > Account)

In the Full name box, change the name and click Save profile.
Wait for the word Saved, then reload the page.
Check the new name is still shown. Open Account and check the email row is there, then compare with Expected (name, photo, email).

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Instructions for AGI
steps: Open Settings and click Personalization.
Scroll to the heading Instructions for AGI and type text in the box under it (a counter shows the character limit).
Make sure the switch beside Apply instructions for AGI is on.
Start a new chat, send a message, and check the reply follows the instruction.
Turn the switch off, send another message, and check the instruction no longer applies.
items.needs: none

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone (Response style, Response length, Characteristics)
steps: Open Settings and click Personalization.
Under the heading Style and tone, open Response style and pick a value; then open Response length and pick a value.
Under Characteristics, change Warmth or Headers and lists if you want.
Start a new chat, send the same question, and compare the reply's tone, length and formatting with the choices.
Click Reset response style to undo the changes and check the reply changes back.
items.needs: none
items.note: Files found; behaviour not judged.

items.where: Chat composer > Response style > Create Custom Style
steps: Open a chat and click the Response style control in the message box.
Click Create Custom Style.
Enter a name, paste a sample of your own writing, and add an instruction, then save.
Select the new style, send a message, and compare the reply with your sample's style.
Open the same menu and check the style is still listed, and that Edit and Delete work for it.
items.needs: a sample of your own writing
items.note: Exact text of the form field labels and the save button was not read; only the trigger and Create Custom Style were confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Persistent memory
steps: Open Settings and click Personalization.
Under Memory, check the switch labelled Persistent memory.
In the memory editor, type in the box labelled Add a new fact and add a fact; use the Search memory box to find it.
Edit a fact, then delete one and confirm in the dialog Delete this memory? (button Delete memory).
Turn Persistent memory off, start a chat, and check the saved facts are not used; compare with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The memory editor lives in packages/ui/unified-chat, not in the settings file.

items.where: Settings > Personalization > Search past chats
steps: Open Settings and click Personalization.
Under Memory, find the switch labelled Search past chats and turn it on.
Start a chat, ask about something you discussed in an earlier chat, and check the reply uses it.
Turn Search past chats off, ask the same question in a new chat, and check the earlier chat is no longer used.
Start a temporary chat and check it is not used for references; compare with Expected.
items.needs: at least one earlier saved chat
items.note: The temporary-chat exclusion is only stated in the Privacy copy (Not saved to history or search); it was not verified in the code path.

items.where: Projects > open a project > project settings > Memory > Use memories from outside this project
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar and open a project.
Open the project's settings dialog.
Under Memory, tick or untick Use memories from outside this project.
Click save in the dialog, then start a chat inside the project.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Chrome
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities.
Find the Chrome section and read its status (Install extension, Paired and answering, or Paired, not answering right now).
Click Unpair this browser? and confirm in the dialog.
Check the status changes to not paired.

steps: Open Settings and click Privacy.

Turn one on, reload, and check it stays on; turn it off again.

Return to Authenticator app and click Turn off two-factor to compare with Expected: it can be turned off.

steps: Open Settings > Security > Authenticator app.

Click Unlink on one device, then Unlink device in the prompt.
Compare with Expected: the device is removed and its access is revoked when it next connects.

steps: Open Settings > Capabilities and find the Remote Control section.
Click Pair a phone to see the pairing code, then cancel or close it.
Find the Chrome section and read whether the browser is paired.
Click Unpair, then Unpair in the prompt.
Compare with Expected: the paired device is listed and can be unpaired.

Compare with Expected: this device or app is signed out.

steps: Open Settings > Security.

Read the prompt Log out of all devices? and click Log out everywhere.

items.where: Settings > Notifications > Security alerts

Trigger a security event (e.g. a password change) and compare with Expected: a notice arrives by the chosen channel.

Compare with Expected: groups show members, can be created, and roles can be granted to a group.
items.needs: an owner or admin account
items.note: No sync button was found on this screen. Directory groups are replaced by the next identity-provider sync, set up under Identity > Directory sync (SCIM 2.0).

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles, then Members > Role for <member name>
steps: Click Roles in the Workspace administration left column.
Read the Roles card and click Edit on a role to see its permission boxes.
Click Members in the left column.
Open the Role for <member name> drop-down on a member row and choose another role.
Confirm in the dialog and check the row shows the new role line.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a member account to change
items.note: The member role drop-down's visible text is Viewer role, Member role and Admin role; the accessible name is Role for followed by the member name.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Roles > New role
steps: On Roles, click New role.
Type a Role name and an optional Description.
Tick permissions under Permissions. You can only grant what your own role holds, then click Create role.
To give the role to a member, go to Members, find Additional roles, tick the role and click Save roles.
To give it to a group, open the group under Groups, tick the role and click Save group.
Compare with Expected: the role's permissions apply to the member or group. Edit and Delete are on each role row.
items.needs: an owner or admin account
items.note: The code has a rule that checks whether a role is held by members or groups before it can be deleted; the exact Delete rule was not read in full.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Seats & billing
steps: Click Members in the Workspace administration left column.
Find the Seats & billing card and read the Licensed, In use and Available figures.
In a member row, open the drop-down Seat type for <member name> and choose Standard seat or Premium seat.
Click Change seats to add seats (it opens the pricing page) or Manage billing.
Compare with Expected: the three seat figures change when a seat is taken or released, and seats can be added through Change seats.
items.needs: an owner or admin account in a paid workspace with seats
items.note: Adding seats goes to the pricing page, not to a control inside the console; Seat type rows appear only when seat billing is on.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Members > Workspace ownership
steps: Sign in as the workspace owner and go to Members.
Scroll to the Workspace ownership card (only the owner sees it).
Choose a name in Member to receive ownership and a role in Your role after the transfer.
Click Transfer ownership, then click the confirm button in the Transfer ownership? dialog.
Read the result line Ownership was transferred. Your role is now ..., then check your role on the Members list.
Compare with Expected: the new owner holds the owner role and you hold the role you chose.
items.needs: an owner account and a second member account in the same workspace

labels.text: Ownership was transferred. Your role is now

items.note: The confirm button text in the dialog was not read; the dialog title is Transfer ownership?.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Identity > Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC) > Add connection
steps: Click Identity in the Workspace administration left column.
In Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC), type a company domain in Email domain and click Add connection.
On the new connection card, read Domain not verified and the values Record type, Record name and Record value.
Publish that TXT record in your DNS host (this step is outside the app), then click Verify domain.
Compare with Expected: the status changes to Domain verified, and sign-in for that domain is not routed until verification succeeds.
items.needs: an owner account and a domain you control with DNS editing access

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Identity > Single sign-on (SAML / OIDC)
steps: On Identity, open the connection card for a verified domain.
Pick SAML 2.0 or OIDC when you add it, with IdP metadata URL or OIDC discovery URL filled in.
Copy the values under Paste these into your identity provider: (ACS URL, SP entity ID) into your identity provider.
Click Activate on the card.
Compare with Expected: the status reads Active with the text Users with an email address on this domain sign in through your identity provider.
Optionally sign in with a test identity-provider user on that domain to check.
items.needs: an owner account, a verified domain, and an identity-provider test account (SAML or OIDC)

labels.text: Paste these into your identity provider:

items.note: The sign-in test through the identity provider happens outside the console and was not traced in code.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Identity > Directory sync (SCIM 2.0)
steps: On Identity, scroll to the Directory sync (SCIM 2.0) heading.
Under Connections, choose a Provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, OneLogin or Generic SCIM 2.0) and click Add connection.
Under SCIM tokens, choose a connection, type a Token name and click Mint token.
Copy the token shown with the note Copy this now, it will not be shown again, and enter it with the SCIM base URL in your identity provider.
Compare with Expected: users created, changed or removed in the identity provider appear, updated or removed here, and Recent IdP activity lists the sync events.
items.needs: an Enterprise plan (the page says it requires an active Enterprise subscription) and an identity-provider test tenant

labels.text: Copy this now, it will not be shown again

items.note: The provider-side create, update and deprovision actions depend on the identity provider and were not verified.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Audit > Workspace API keys > Create key; then Identity > Service principals
steps: Click Audit in the Workspace administration left column.
Scroll to Workspace API keys, type a name in Workspace API key name, pick an expiry, tick scopes and click Create key.
Copy the new key shown once.
Click Identity and find the Service principals card, which lists the principal created with the key.
Click Disable on that principal, then Enable to restore it; use Revoke on the key row under Audit to revoke the key.
Compare with Expected: the key keeps working after its creator leaves, and disabling or revoking stops it.
items.needs: an owner or admin account
items.note: Service principals are created with the first workspace API key, not from their own form.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Models
steps: Click Models in the Workspace administration left column.
Under Providers, click Block beside a provider, or Approve on another.
Under Models, type in Filter models and click Block beside a model, or Approve.
Click Save model policy and read the Blocked badge beside the model.
Compare with Expected: then try that blocked model in chat and check that the request is refused.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a chat model to test
items.note: The refusal itself happens on the server during chat; the exact refusal message was not read.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Features and defaults
steps: Click Policy in the Workspace administration left column.
Under Features and defaults, switch off a feature such as Work or Skills, then click Save features and defaults.
Under Exceptions, choose Exception applies to (A person, A directory group or A role), pick the subject, set the feature to Off and click Save exception.
Sign in as a member who is affected and try that feature.
Compare with Expected: the switched-off feature is refused for everyone without an exception, and the exception member is treated as set.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a member account to test
items.note: The card text says the workspace policy must be saved first; enforcement in the CLI is separate and not checked from this screen.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Connectors > Catalog connectors
steps: Click Connectors in the Workspace administration left column.
Under Catalog connectors, find a connector row.
Set Read-only tools and Write tools for that connector to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked.
Click Save policy.
Compare with Expected: the connector's read-only and write tools follow the chosen level; try a write tool in chat to check the approval step.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a deployment that has catalog connectors
items.note: If no catalog connectors are configured, the card shows No catalog connectors are configured and there is nothing to set.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Connectors
steps: Click Connectors in the Workspace administration left column.
Under Catalog connectors, click Block beside a connector, or Approve to allow it.
Turn the Allow custom connectors switch off if you want custom connectors blocked.
Click Save policy.
Compare with Expected: a blocked connector shows as Blocked and is not offered in chat, schedules or agent runs.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a deployment that has catalog connectors
items.note: Connector rows show the connector id with dashes replaced by spaces; a blocked connector is refused on the server, not just hidden.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Features and defaults (Skills and Plugins switches); and Connectors > Plugins
steps: On Policy, under Features and defaults, switch off Skills or Plugins and click Save features and defaults.
Sign in as a member and try to use or install a skill or plugin.
On Connectors, under Plugins, type a plugin key in Plugin key and click Approve or Block.
Read the lists Approved plugins and Blocked plugins.
Compare with Expected: the switched-off feature is refused, and a blocked plugin cannot be installed.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a member account to test
items.note: There is no per-skill control in the code; skill control is by the Skills switch and plugin control is by plugin key.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Plugins
steps: Click Plugins in the Workspace administration left column.
Under Publish a plugin or a skill, click Upload a plugin or skill and choose a .zip file.
Wait for Scanning and publishing to finish, then read the Workspace plugins list.
Set the install option for a plugin (Required, Installed by default, Available to install or Not available), then check it.
Compare with Expected: members find the published plugin under Plugins; it is kept apart from the public directory.
items.needs: a plugin or skill .zip file, and an owner or admin account
items.note: The separation from the public directory was not checked in code; this screen only publishes and sets install options for the workspace's own plugins.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Sharing
steps: Click Sharing in the Workspace administration left column.
Read the Shared projects card to see which projects are shared with the workspace.
Open a project's member list to set access per member (Can view, Can edit or No access).
Click Stop sharing on a project and confirm in the dialog.
Compare with Expected: every shared project is listed, per-member access changes, and a stopped project no longer appears to members.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a project already shared with the workspace
items.note: The admin list is shared with the project sharing controls; the exact labels for per-member access come from that file.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Public sharing
steps: Click Policy in the Workspace administration left column.
Find the Public sharing card and its switch labelled Allow public sharing.
Switch it off and click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and try to create a new public or outside share link.
Compare with Expected: new share links are refused while the switch is off; existing links stay up until revoked.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a member account to test
items.note: The code uses one switch for outside sharing and public publishing (see S87.21); no separate outside-sharing switch was found.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Public sharing
steps: Click Policy in the Workspace administration left column.
In the Public sharing card, switch off Allow public sharing and click Save policy.
Sign in as a member and try to publish a chat or an artifact to a public link.
Compare with Expected: publishing is refused while the switch is off.
Switch it on again and check that publishing works.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a member account to test
items.note: Same switch as S87.20; the card text reads Members may publish a chat or an artifact to an anonymous public link.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Memory
steps: Click Policy in the Workspace administration left column.
Find the Memory card and switch off Allow memory.
Click Save policy.
Sign in as a member whose personal setting has memory on, and check that memory is not used.
Compare with Expected: the card says Off for every member, whatever their personal setting.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a member account with memory

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Retention window
steps: Click Policy in the Workspace administration left column.
In the Retention window card, change Retention window in days and click Save policy.
Switch on Enforce the retention window in the Enforce retention card and confirm the dialog.
Read the line that says chats idle for N days are permanently deleted, except under legal hold.
Compare with Expected: the window is saved; after enforcement a nightly sweep deletes older chats, but chats under legal hold stay.
items.needs: an owner or admin account; use a test workspace only, because enforcement deletes chats
items.note: The Data screen's Retention by data type covers other data (projects, files, artifacts), not chats; the legal-hold part is on Data.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Data > Data region
steps: Click Data in the Workspace administration left column.
Find the Data region card and read Stored in <region>.
Open the drop-down with Choose a region… and pick another region, then click Request move and confirm.
Read the note that says data stays in the current region until the copy is verified.
Compare with Expected: the region is requested and data is kept in the chosen region once the move completes.
items.needs: an Enterprise plan (the card says choosing a region requires an active Enterprise plan)
items.note: The plan file says EU infrastructure is unfinished; an EU option may show (not available yet) and be disabled.

items.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Data > Encryption key
steps: Click Data in the Workspace administration left column.
In the Encryption key card, choose a Provider (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault), type the Key identifier and Region, then click Connect key.
Read the status sentence that says workspace data is sealed with your key.
Click Rotate and confirm Rotate key, or click Revoke, enter a reason and confirm Revoke key.
Compare with Expected: the key is connected, rotates or revokes from this card, and data follows the key status.
items.needs: an owner or admin account, and a cloud key (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault) for a real connection
items.note: The card shows a refusal message instead of the controls when the feature is not offered to this workspace; the exact refusal text was not read.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > IP allow list
steps: Sign in as a workspace owner or admin, open Settings, choose Workspace, then click Workspace administration.
Click Policy in the left list and scroll down to the IP allow list row.
Type your own address, or a block such as 203.0.113.0/24, in the box and press Enter. Add your own address first so you do not lock yourself out.
Click Save policy.
From a network outside the listed addresses, try to sign in to the workspace and check that the sign-in is refused, as Expected says.
items.needs: An owner or admin account, and a second network (for example a phone hotspot) to test refusal
items.note: The refusal is applied on the server (apps/web/lib/ip-allow-list-gate.ts); the screen only saves the list, so the refusal itself is seen by signing in from outside the list. The opening menu for Settings was not confirmed in code.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Audit > Audit trail
steps: Sign in as an owner or admin, open Settings, choose Workspace, then click Workspace administration.
Click Audit in the left list.
In the Audit trail card, open the Filter by action dropdown (it starts at All actions), then the Filter by outcome and Filter by severity dropdowns, and pick a value in each.
Look at the table with the headings When, Actor, Action, Resource, Surface and Outcome; the rows should match the filters. If nothing matches you see No events match these filters.
items.needs: An owner or admin account, and some audit events in the workspace (for example a role change or an invitation)
items.note: The filters found in code are action, outcome and severity only; no time-range filter was found, although Expected lists time range.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Audit > Audit trail > Export JSONL
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Audit.
Optionally set the filters in the Audit trail card first, because the export follows them.
Click Export JSONL and wait for the file to download; open it and compare its lines with the rows on screen.
Go back to the Audit trail table and check that a new event for the export now appears, as Expected says it is recorded.
items.needs: An owner or admin account, and a place to save a downloaded file
items.note: No date-range picker was found for the export; it uses the filters only. SIEM streaming sits on the same Audit page (Audit destination endpoint, Start streaming). The Audit export switch on the Policy page turns export off. The recording of the export was not confirmed in the UI code.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Usage
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Usage.
Click 7 days, 30 days or 90 days (30 days is selected first).
Read the Managed cloud usage totals, then the tables By member, By product area, By model and By provider.
Click Export daily CSV to download the file.
Compare the totals, the tables and the CSV, as Expected says.
items.needs: An owner or admin account, and some managed Cloud usage in the chosen period
items.note: The figures are managed Cloud credits and settled requests only, as the page states.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Usage > Monthly spend limit
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Usage.
Scroll to Monthly spend limit. Type a number in Cap (credits) and a percentage in Alert at.
Choose Off, Notify or Block in the enforcement dropdown, then click Set limit.
Read the bar and the line that says the credits used this month, which shows past the alert once the threshold is crossed.
With Block set, use Cloud turns until the cap is reached and check that new turns are refused, as Expected says.
items.needs: An owner or admin account, and Cloud usage to reach a small test cap
items.note: A second place exists: the Policy page has a Monthly spend cap row (aria label Monthly spend cap in credits) saved with Save policy. The alert percentage is the Alert at field.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Billing
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, then click Workspace administration and Billing.
Read the Plan and seats card: Plan, Seats used and Members.
If the workspace has an enterprise contract, scroll to Enterprise contract and its Invoices section.
Click Billing settings to reach payment, invoices and plan changes, and compare what you find with Expected.
items.needs: An owner or admin account; an enterprise contract is needed to see the contract and invoice parts
items.note: The console shows plan and seats as read-only text; no add-seat or plan-change control was found in this file, and the page says payment and invoices are in billing settings. The contract section appears only for contract-priced plans.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Data > Legal holds > Export records
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Data.
If no legal hold exists, place one as in S87.37 first.
On the hold row, click Export records and wait for the download.
Open the file and check that it holds the workspace conversations and messages, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: An owner or admin account and at least one legal hold
items.note: The only export found is per legal hold. The e-discovery service lists conversation and message types; files and artifacts were not confirmed, and no entry in the trail for the export was confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Data > Legal holds > Place hold
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Data.
Under Legal holds, fill in the Legal hold name and Legal hold scope (Whole workspace or One member), pick the person in Held member if needed, type a Legal hold reason, then click Place hold.
Check that the hold appears under active holds with a Placed date.
Click Release hold on that hold, then click Release hold in the confirmation box.
Check that the hold now shows Released and that the deletion figures under the backlog (Held from deletion) reflect it.
items.needs: An owner or admin account; a second member account to test the One member scope
items.note: Place a hold is a sub-heading above the form, not a button; the button is Place hold.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Policy > Explain a member’s policy
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Policy.
Scroll to the section that asks Explain a member’s policy (shown to admins only).
Choose a person in Member, optionally a feature in Feature to check (optional), choose a surface in From, and optionally a Country code (optional).
Click Explain.
Read the result: what this person may not use, which rule turned it off, and whether the request passes; compare with Expected.
items.needs: An owner or admin account, and at least one member with a restricted policy to see a refusal
items.note: The heading is written in the file as Explain a member’s policy, which shows as a curly apostrophe.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Audit > Workspace API keys > Create key
steps: Open Settings, choose Workspace, click Workspace administration, then click Audit, and scroll to Workspace API keys.
Type a name in Workspace API key name, tick one or more scopes, and choose an expiry in Workspace API key expiry (30 days, 90 days, 1 year or No expiry).
Click Create key and check the new row shows its scopes and an Expires date.
Click Revoke on that row, then click Revoke key in the confirmation box.
Check that the row now shows Revoked with a date, as Expected says.
items.needs: An owner or admin account; Create key stays off until a name and at least one scope are set
items.note: The API keys card sits on the Audit page (apps/web/app/workspace/audit/page.tsx). The API reference link and the endpoints the keys call were not tested or confirmed.

items.where: Settings > Memory > How memory works
steps: Sign in, open the account menu and choose Settings.
Open the Memory section.
Click the link How memory works.
Check that a help article about memory opens and matches what Memory does.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Memory tab name was not checked in WebSettingsModal. The Policy page also links How workspace policy works (apps/web/app/workspace/policy/page.tsx), which needs a workspace admin.

items.where: Settings > Help > Help center
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Help.
Click Help center (it opens in a new tab).
Type a word such as billing into Search help articles.
Check that matching articles are listed and that clicking one opens it.
items.needs: none
items.note: The search box heading is Search the help centre in the same file.

items.where: Settings > Help > Raise a ticket
steps: Open Settings from the account menu, then choose Help.
Click Raise a ticket.
Type a Subject and What happened, then click Raise ticket.
Check that the ticket appears in the list, then open it and use Send reply to add a follow-up and check that the reply shows in the thread.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The Contact support link in HelpSection.tsx goes to the public /support page, not this in-app form.

items.where: Settings > Help > Raise a ticket (in-app bug report); Settings > Help > Report a bug (public page)
steps: Open Settings, then Help.
Click Raise a ticket, type a Subject and What happened, and read the line Attach diagnostics.
Click Raise ticket and check that the ticket is listed with its status.
Optional: click Report a bug in the Help list and compare the public page with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Attach diagnostics: your build, platform and the last few errors this browser recorded.

items.note: The Report a bug link goes to /support#bugs, a public page. The in-app form is the one that attaches build and platform.

items.where: Account menu > Send feedback
steps: Open the account menu from the sidebar.
Click Send feedback.
Choose General feedback, type in Details, then click Send feedback.
Check that the dialog says Thanks, your feedback was sent.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The plan marks this item as unfinished at mount. The dialog is mounted with hideTrigger in WebChatPage.tsx and WebAppShell.tsx, and the menu item calls it, but I did not test that it opens.

items.where: Account menu > Send feedback > Feature request
steps: Open the account menu and click Send feedback.
Choose Feature request.
Type in Details and click Send feedback.
Check the thank-you message and that the feedback type is Feature request.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Same mount caveat as S88.05.

items.where: Settings > Help > Raise a ticket > Review diagnostics > Download diagnostics
steps: Open Settings, then Help, then click Raise a ticket.
Type a Subject and What happened. Leave Attach diagnostics ticked.
Click Review diagnostics and read the box of diagnostics that would be attached.
Click Download diagnostics, then compare the file and the box with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Attach diagnostics: your build, platform and the last few errors this browser recorded.

items.note: Sharing happens only when the ticket is raised with the checkbox ticked.

items.where: Any chat reply that fails: the error line under the reply
steps: Send a chat message while the service is failing, or use a failing model route.
Read the error line under the reply.
Check that it ends with a Reference: code you could quote to support.
items.needs: a way to make a request fail
items.note: The reference text comes from the translation template {{text}} Reference: {{reference}}. A tester cannot make a failure on purpose from the app, so this may need an engineer to cause one.

items.where: Settings > Help > System status
steps: Open Settings, then Help.
Click System status (it opens in a new tab).
Read the overall status word and the list of checks.
Compare with Expected: the page should show when results were checked and show Checks passing or a failing state.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Help page also has a Check service status button in apps/web/app/help/page.tsx. The Composer footer shows Unavailable right now only for a model that is down.

items.where: A banner at the top of the app, shown only during a live incident
steps: Sign in and watch the top of the app while an incident is open.
Read the notice text, then click its dismiss control.
Compare with Expected: the notice should say the problem and its status.
items.needs: a live incident, which the tester cannot start
items.note: The notice appears only when the server health checks fail. The dismissal is saved in this browser under agi-dismissed-service-notices (apps/web/shared/components/ServiceNotices.tsx). I did not find a visible label for the dismiss control.

items.where: A banner at the top of the app, shown up to 72 hours before a planned maintenance window
steps: Sign in when a maintenance window is scheduled within 72 hours.
Read the notice; it should change from upcoming to underway.
Compare with Expected: the notice should give the planned time.
items.needs: a scheduled maintenance window, which the tester cannot create
items.note: Window text comes from apps/web/lib/server/service-notices.ts (ANNOUNCE_AHEAD_MS, maintenanceNotice). I did not find the exact visible copy, so no label is given.

items.where: Any page after a new release: the banner What's new: <headline> > Read more
steps: Sign in after a new release is published.
Look for the banner that starts with What's new:.
Click Read more and read the release notes page.
Check that the release notes show what changed.
items.needs: a release newer than the last one this browser saw
items.note: The banner depends on the last seen release stored in this browser (agi-last-seen-release). It appears only once per release.

items.where: Chat > the model picker in the composer, and the notice shown in chat when the model is retired
steps: Open a chat and open the model picker from the composer footer.
Look for a model marked Leaving or Unavailable right now.
If a chat is saved with a retired model, read the notice that says the model is no longer available.
Compare with Expected: the notice should name the replacement model and offer a way to pick another.
items.needs: a model that is being retired, which the tester may not have
items.note: Retirement dates are not visible to a tester without a live retirement. The Leaving text is built in ComposerFooter.tsx from a short label.

items.where: Settings > Memory > Import memory from other AI providers
steps: Open Settings, then Memory.
Click the button that opens the import dialog, the one titled Import memory from other AI providers.
Click Copy prompt, paste a reply into Paste memories, or use Upload file.
Check the preview of memories to import before saving, with Already saved marked where it applies.
items.needs: text or a file from another AI assistant

labels.text: Import memory from other AI providers

items.note: The button that opens this dialog was not read from MemorySection.tsx (the open call is useImportMemoryDialog). The save button label was not checked.

items.where: Footer > Privacy choices
steps: Scroll to the footer and click Privacy choices.
Read Your requests and the Access, Correction and Erasure request types.
Submit a request and check that it appears under Your requests with its status.
items.needs: a signed-in account to see your own requests (signed-out requests go by email)
items.note: The request form's submit label was not checked.

items.where: Footer > Cookies > Change your cookie preferences
steps: Scroll to the footer and click Cookies.
Click Change your cookie preferences.
Turn a cookie category off, save, and reload the page.
Check that the choice stays off and that the page respects it.
items.needs: none
items.note: The first-visit consent banner is in apps/web/shared/components/CookieConsent.tsx. The save button label was not checked.

items.where: Chat > an assistant reply > its more actions menu, the item that reports the message
steps: Open a chat and find an assistant reply.
Open its more actions menu and choose the report item.
Read the confirmation message.
Compare with Expected: it should say the report goes to trust and safety.
items.needs: a chat with a reply

labels.text: Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it.

items.note: The menu item's own label and the opener button were not confirmed in MessageBubble.tsx, only the click handler (around line 4065) and the Flag icon.

items.where: Open /copyright/report in the browser (no sign-in needed)
steps: Open the copyright report page in the browser.
Read the title Report infringing or impersonating content.
Choose What you are reporting, fill in the link and the contact details, tick the accuracy statement, and submit.
Check the confirmation that gives a reference and says nothing has been removed yet.
items.needs: a shared conversation or artifact link on this site

labels.text: The information in this notice is accurate.

items.note: I did not find a footer or menu link to this page. The owner should confirm how people reach it.

Click "Legal" in the footer's legal links.

items.where: Type /developers after the site address (no menu link found) > Projects > New project
steps: Open /developers in the browser or the Desktop app.
Click New project in the Projects card.
Type Production in Name and 500 in Monthly limit in credits, then click Create project.
Look at the Projects list: the new project appears, with a spend line that ends in 'this month' and shows the limit you typed (or 'no monthly limit' if blank).
items.needs: a paid account with API access (other plans get no keys)
items.note: Organizations are not created in this panel: a workspace is created in Settings > Workspace under 'Create your workspace' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/TeamSection.tsx). Projects belong to the active workspace.

items.where: Settings > Account > API keys > New Key
steps: Click the account menu (labelled Account menu for your name), click Settings, then Account, then the API keys row.
Click New Key. Type a name, pick a project or keep Default project, choose Expires (Never, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year), and tick scopes (Read model catalog, Run inference, Read usage).
Click Generate Key, then Copy to Clipboard. The full key is shown only once.
Check the list: each key shows its prefix followed by '...', Created, Last used once used, and Expires or Never expires.
Click the trash icon labelled Delete <name>, then Delete Key, and check the key is gone from the list.
items.needs: a plan with API access (other plans see an upgrade message instead of the form)
items.note: The screen says Delete, not Revoke. The same card also appears on /developers.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Audit (Workspace API keys) and Identity (Service principals)
steps: Open Settings, click Workspace, then Workspace administration.
Click Audit, scroll to Workspace API keys, type a name, pick an expiry, tick at least one scope and click Create key. Copy the key shown.
Click Identity and scroll to Service principals. Find the principal the key created.
Click Disable on a principal and check it now says Disabled and its button reads Enable.
Back on Audit, click Revoke on a workspace key, confirm Revoke key, and check the key shows Revoked.
items.needs: a workspace owner or admin on a Team or Enterprise plan (the create form shows only for accounts that can manage keys)
items.note: The service principals panel has no create button; a principal is created with the first workspace API key. Principals can be disabled or enabled but not revoked there; revoke is on workspace keys.

items.where: Developer console (/developers) > Reference > Models
steps: Open /developers and scroll to the Reference card.
Click Models. Check the page heading reads Models and a list of model cards appears.
Open a model card and read its Context line and its capability chips.
Click the Plan access filter 'In your plan' and check which models remain.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The catalogue lists models the account's plan can reach. No filter for what one specific API key can call was found.

items.where: Settings > General > Custom commands > New command
steps: Open Settings, click General, and scroll to Custom commands.
Click New command. Type a Name (lower case, no spaces), a Description, and a Template that contains the input token.
Click Create command and check it appears in the list.
Click into the chat box, type / and the command name, add some text and send.
Check the reply follows the template with your text in place of the input token.
items.needs: a signed-in account (commands sync to the account)
items.note: A command has one input slot ({{input}} in the template), not named arguments. The Prompts and evaluations card on /developers is a separate versioned-prompt feature.

items.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and choose Days, Weeks or Months.
Read the tables By product area, By model and By project for the chosen period.
Compare: the By model table lists each model with its usage over time.
items.needs: a paid plan (the history section is hidden on the Free plan)
items.note: Usage is shown in credits. Cost in money is not shown on this screen.

items.where: Developer console (/developers) > Rate limits
steps: Open /developers and scroll to the Rate limits card.
Read the list 'Request limits by endpoint': each row gives an endpoint, a number of requests per window, and whether it counts per account or per IP for an API key.
Read the card text: each response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset.
Send a request with an AGI API key and read those headers to see how close you are to the limit. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: an AGI API key and any HTTP client, to see the per-response headers
items.note: The card shows the static limits only. The remaining count is in response headers, not on the page.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Usage (Monthly spend limit); personal cap at Settings > Usage > Monthly spend limit
steps: Open Settings, click Workspace, then Workspace administration, then Usage.
Scroll to Monthly spend limit. Type an amount, set Spend limit enforcement to Block, and click Set limit.
Check the card shows the cap you set and the enforcement choice.
For a personal cap, open Settings > Usage and find Monthly spend limit; set and check it the same way.
items.needs: a workspace owner or admin account for the workspace cap; a paid plan for the personal cap
items.note: The enforcement choices are Off, Notify and Block. Whether the API refuses calls at the cap was not checked here.

items.where: Developer console (/developers) > Webhooks > Add endpoint
steps: Open /developers, scroll to the Webhooks card and click Add endpoint.
Type an https address in Endpoint URL and optionally a Description.
Under Events, tick the events you want to receive.
Click Add endpoint and read the Copy the signing secret now dialog.
Check the new endpoint appears in the Webhook endpoints list.
items.needs: a paid account with API access, and an HTTPS address you control to receive events

items.where: Developer console (/developers) > Webhooks > endpoint row > Deliveries
steps: Open /developers, scroll to Webhooks, and make sure an endpoint is listed.
Click Send test event on the endpoint, or use an event that already happened.
Click Deliveries on the endpoint row and read Recent deliveries: each row shows a status such as Delivered, Failed or Retrying after N attempts.
Click Resend on a delivery row and check its status updates.
items.needs: a registered endpoint that can receive HTTPS requests

items.where: API (site menu, apps/web/features/marketing/components/system/nav.ts) > SDKs.
steps: Open the API docs page (type /api-docs after the site address, or use the API entry in the site menu).
Scroll to the section titled SDKs.
Read it: it says there is no AGI SDK and that OpenAI's official libraries are the client.
Look at the Python and TypeScript tabs under it and check they show example code for the gateway.
Compare with Expected: the docs cover OpenAI's libraries, not a separate AGI SDK.

items.note: The page states there is no AGI SDK, so the 'official client SDK' Expected is met only by OpenAI's libraries.

Read the paragraph: the OpenAPI bundle describes every endpoint and the credential each one takes.
Click OpenAPI bundle and check a JSON document opens.
Scroll to the top, click Authentication and scopes, and read which credential each endpoint accepts.

items.where: API docs page > code tabs curl, Python, TypeScript

Click the tabs curl, Python and TypeScript in turn and read each sample.
Scroll to SDKs. and click the Python and TypeScript tabs there.
Compare with Expected: each tab shows a copyable request to the gateway.

items.note: Whether the samples have a copy button was not checked.

items.where: API docs page > Moving to the gateway. > From the OpenAI API / From the Anthropic API / Between models
steps: Open the API docs page and scroll to Moving to the gateway.
Read the three sub-headings: From the OpenAI API, From the Anthropic API and Between models.
Open the text under From the Anthropic API and read the steps to change the client.
Compare with Expected: there is a guide for each other provider and one for moving between models.

steps: Open the API docs page and scroll to Deprecations.
Read the text: each model carries a deprecation date, which is empty until a retirement is scheduled.
Read the table Scheduled model retirements if it appears; otherwise the page says No model retirements are scheduled.
Open /developers > Reference > Models and look for a model marked Retiring with a date.
Compare with Expected: retirements appear in advance with a date.

items.where: Settings > Help > Contact support, then Settings > Help > Your support tickets > Raise ticket
steps: Open Settings and click Help.
Click Contact support to open the support page and read the Raise a ticket button there.
Back in Help, scroll to Your support tickets and fill in Subject and What happened.
Click Raise ticket and check the new ticket appears in the list with its Raised date and priority.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Plugins > Add > Upload plugin
steps: Open Settings and click Plugins.
Click Add, then Upload plugin.
Choose a .zip of a plugin that has a skills folder, and submit the dialog.
Check the plugin shows under Installed and can be opened.
items.needs: a plugin .zip file with a skills folder (a manifest folder is optional)
items.note: Create a plugin is the other option in the Add menu. Both appear only when the directory offers them to this account.

items.where: Settings > Plugins > open your plugin > Submit to the directory
steps: Open Settings, click Plugins, and open a plugin you created.
Click Submit to the directory.
Read the confirmation text and click Submit for review.
Check the plugin shows a pending submission with a Withdraw action.
items.needs: a plugin you created; an admin must approve it in the plugin moderation page before it is listed
items.note: Approval happens in the admin plugin moderation page, outside this tester path. A new version of an approved plugin uses Submit this version.

items.where: Settings > Slack app > Add to Slack, then in Slack open a direct message with the AGI app
steps: Sign in and open Settings from the account menu.
Click 'Slack app' in the Customize group and click 'Add to Slack' under 'Slack workspaces you added' to add the app to a Slack workspace.
In Slack, open a direct message with the AGI app (first link your account by messaging the app, as 'Your Slack accounts' says) and send a question.
Look for the assistant's reply in that same direct message and compare with Expected.
items.needs: A Slack workspace where you can add apps, and a Slack account you can message; the owner must first complete the Slack app setup from the plan's 'Known to be unfinished' note
items.note: The Settings screen exists, but the reply depends on the owner's Slack app setup and migration 0333, which the plan says are not done; the 'Settings' menu item text was found only in a test file (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountFooter.test.tsx), so the component that renders it was not located.

items.where: Settings > Slack app > Slack workspaces you added, then /invite the app to a Slack channel
steps: Open Settings, click 'Slack app', and make sure the workspace is listed under 'Slack workspaces you added' (click 'Add to Slack' if not).
In Slack, type /invite with the AGI app's name in a channel.
Under the workspace, check the per-channel control labelled 'What AGI may do in' that channel and leave it on a mode that answers.
In that channel, post a message for the agent and watch for the agent's reply or report in the channel. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A Slack workspace where you can add apps and invite them to a channel, and a second member who can post in the channel if needed
items.note: The channel policy control is rendered by apps/web/features/slack/components/SlackChannelPolicies.tsx with aria-label 'What AGI may do in'; the visible label text was not confirmed, and the owner's Slack app setup is listed as unfinished in the plan.

items.where: In Slack, a channel where the AGI app is invited: @mention the app with a request; then Settings > Slack app > Waiting for your approval if a step needs approval
steps: In a channel where the AGI app has been invited, type a message that mentions the app and asks for a task.
Wait for the reply in the channel thread and check whether it includes a task link in its footer.
If the task needs a tool, open Settings > Slack app and look under 'Waiting for your approval' for the pending item.
Compare the task created with Expected: the mention should become a task the agent runs.
items.needs: A Slack workspace with the app invited to a channel, a linked Slack account, and the Tasks feature available on the account's plan
items.note: Task creation depends on the channel policy and on whether tasks are available for the account (slackTaskAvailable in apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant.ts); the task link appears in the Slack reply footer, not in the desktop app.

items.where: In Slack, the sender name on the app's replies in a channel or direct message; the linked accounts are listed under 'Your Slack accounts' in Settings > Slack app
steps: After the app has replied in a channel, look at the sender name and avatar on that reply in Slack.
Confirm the sender is the AGI app's bot user and not your own Slack name.
Open Settings > Slack app and compare with the list under 'Your Slack accounts' to see which human accounts AGI answers as.
items.needs: A Slack workspace with the app invited to a channel, and a second person's account in that channel if you want to compare
items.note: Identity is set by the bot token (xoxb- prefix, bot_user_id) in apps/web/lib/slack/slack-api.ts and posting in apps/web/lib/slack/slack-messages.ts; the tester sees it only as the sender name in Slack, and the 'Your Slack accounts' copy says AGI answers 'as you' for linked accounts, which may read as confusing next to the bot identity.

items.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > View History (the history icon on a schedule card, tooltip 'Run History')
steps: Sign in and click 'Scheduled' in the sidebar.
On a schedule that has run, click the history icon (tooltip 'Run History', aria-label 'View History for' the schedule name).
Look at the 'Run History' panel for the runs and their results.
Compare with Expected: work the agent did from a channel or host should show up here for review.
items.needs: A schedule that has run at least once; for the Slack-originated part, a Slack setup as in S106.13
items.note: The code audit says this is done, but it is not confirmed that runs started from Slack appear in this panel; Slack approvals appear under Settings > Slack app instead.

items.where: Chat header > "Share conversation", then open the share link as a second account. The viewer shows "Shared by <name>", the message count and "Expires".
steps: Sign in with account A, open a conversation, and click "Share conversation" in the chat header.
In the dialog, choose a workspace or organization share and create the link.
Sign in with account B in the same workspace (or open the link in a new window) and open the link.
Look under the title for "Shared by <name>", "<n> messages" and "Expires <time>". Compare with Expected: publisher, author, source, versions and "copied from" were not found on this page.
items.needs: A second account in the same workspace
items.note: Only the sharer name, message count and expiry are shown; no version, source or "copied from" text was found in the code, and the exact share-link button label in the dialog was not verified.

items.where: An AI reply > "More message actions" > "Report this response". Report is offered only on AI replies, not on public share pages.
steps: Sign in, open a conversation that has an AI reply.
Hover or click the AI reply, then click the "More message actions" button.
Click "Report this response". The item changes to "Reporting…" and then "Reported".
Compare with Expected: the report is sent to /api/content-report with category harmful. Confirming it reaches operators needs the operator dashboard (see S107.23).
items.needs: A conversation that already has an AI reply
items.note: No report control was found on public share pages, and the code only sends category harmful. Infringement reports are not offered here.

items.where: Settings > Plugins > open a plugin you created > "Submit to the directory". Public information: the "Partners" page (site navigation) says "List a plugin in the directory".
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose "Plugins".
Open a plugin you created so its detail page shows.
Click "Submit to the directory" and confirm in the dialog.
Look for the submission note and the review note on the plugin page. Compare with Expected: the publisher is named and the submission goes to review.
items.needs: A plugin you created that is submittable
items.note: The exact Settings path to the directory was inferred from the nav labels, not confirmed in the directory's own code. The user-added publisher source was not found; the Partners page is a public marketing page, not an in-app screen.

Open the content tab, which holds the "Rights notices" list.
Pick a notice, read its details, and choose a status; for an unpublish, click "Unpublish" and confirm the dialog.
Compare with Expected: the notice is reviewed here and the public item is taken down, with the decision recorded in the audit log.
items.needs: A staff operator account
items.note: The tab's visible label for the content tab was not found, so the tester should look for the content tab by its contents. The admin console also lists a "Content report queue" and "Content takedown" entry in apps/web/features/admin/pages/AdminConsolePage.tsx, which the audit did not confirm as the same path.

Type a request such as 'Research [company name]: business, financials, recent news and competitors' and send.

Send a campaign request in chat.
Compare with Expected: audiences, campaigns, assets and analytics. Only written advice is produced; no campaign, audience or analytics screen was found.
items.needs: none
items.note: Braze and Adobe Marketing Agent directory entries are Coming soon, so analytics and campaign actions are not available.

items.where: Chat > type a buying question and send (no button)
steps: In a new chat with a model that can search the web, type a buying question with compare or which and a price word, for example 'Compare two or three specific headphones under $400 and tell me which to buy', and send.
Wait for a card titled with the comparison, showing each product with its price, store and a buy link.
Check the Spec table under the cards and the 'Prices checked' line.
Compare with Expected: side-by-side specs, prices and merchants.
items.needs: a model that can search the web
items.note: The card appears only when the model calls the comparison tool; the tester cannot force it from a menu.

items.where: Chat > type a trip request and send (no button)
steps: In a new chat, type 'Plan a day trip in Rome' and send.
Wait for an itinerary card with numbered stops on a map and a route.
Open a route link: the labels read Walking directions in Google Maps or Driving directions in Google Maps.

Compare with Expected: itinerary, places and routes. Reservations are not made here; the assistant only points to Settings, under Connectors, to connect a booking connector (Booking.com and Expedia show Coming soon).
items.needs: none
items.note: Reservations need a booking connector that is not released; the card appears only when the model calls the itinerary tool.

items.where: Menu bar icon (Desktop) > New Chat, Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Window to Chat, Dictation
steps: Turn on the menu bar icon: Settings > General desktop settings > Menu bar (the toggle, which is on by default in the code is not confirmed).
Click the Desktop icon in the macOS menu bar.
Look for the items New Chat, Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Window to Chat and Dictation, each with its shortcut shown beside it.
Click New Chat and check that a new chat opens; compare with the one-click quick actions in Expected.
items.needs: macOS with the desktop app running
items.note: The tray menu is built from a template in tray.ts, and the Menu bar toggle label is in apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopSettingsSection.tsx. I did not confirm whether the icon is shown when that toggle is off, and the Desktop label in the Open item comes from PRODUCT_NAMES, so I left it out.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone
steps: Sign in on the desktop app and open Settings, then the Capabilities tab.
Scroll to the Remote Control section and click Pair a phone.
Confirm the on-screen pairing code and scan the QR code with the phone (in AGI Mobile: AGI Code > Add device).
Watch the status in the Remote Control section: it should show the phone as connected; use Disconnect phone to stop. Compare with the phone pairing in Expected.
items.needs: a paid account, a phone with AGI Mobile, a camera on the phone to scan the QR code
items.note: The section appears on the Capabilities settings tab (confirmed by WebSettingsModal tests). The code says Remote Control needs a paid plan, and the phone side labels come from pairing.ts. I did not read the phone app's behaviour for starting or approving work.

items.where: Press Alt+Shift+Space (Quick Ask shortcut, from any app), or File > Quick Ask
steps: Open another app or web page so it is in front.
Press Alt+Shift+Space (the default Quick Ask chord; it can be changed in Settings > General desktop settings > Quick Ask shortcut).
A small panel (about 480 by 620 pixels, always on top) appears over the other content; type a prompt into it.
Check that the prompt is accepted from the panel without the full main window opening; press Escape to hide the panel again.
items.needs: none (a signed-in account is needed to get a reply)

labels.text: Message AGI from anywhere on your desktop.

items.note: The Quick Ask shortcut hint text is in apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopSettingsSection.tsx; the label above is the File menu item in appMenu.ts. Sending a prompt from the panel was not traced in code.

items.where: Press Alt+Shift+V (Dictation shortcut, from any app), or menu bar icon > Dictation
steps: Click into a text field in another app (for example Notes) so it has focus.
Press Alt+Shift+V to start dictation.
Speak, then press Alt+Shift+V again to finish.
Check that the spoken words reach AGI (the main window or Quick Ask) or are typed into the app in front when Settings > General desktop settings > Dictate into the app you are using is on.
items.needs: a microphone, Desktop app permission for the microphone

labels.text: Dictate into the app you are using

items.note: A system voice command was not found: I searched apps/desktop/electron and packages/contracts for Dictat and Voice Shortcut and found only the shortcut and menu route. The Settings nav name for the desktop section was not found, so the path uses its heading instead.

items.where: Press Cmd+Shift+2 (Screenshot to Chat shortcut, from any app), or File > Screenshot to Chat, or menu bar icon > Screenshot to Chat
steps: Open the content you want to capture on the screen and leave it visible.
Press Cmd+Shift+2 (the default; the first listed option for this shortcut).
Wait for the app to hide briefly, then open the AGI chat (main window or Quick Ask) and check that the screenshot is attached to the composer.
If the composer was not ready, look for the notice Screenshot copied to clipboard and paste with Cmd+V into the composer. On a permission problem look for the notice Screenshot failed.
items.needs: macOS Screen & System Audio Recording permission for the desktop app
items.note: The chord and default come from packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts; the on-screen notices are in screenshot.ts.

items.where: Bring another app's window to the front, press Cmd+Shift+1 (Window to Chat shortcut), or menu bar icon > Window to Chat
steps: Bring one app window (not the AGI window) to the front, and click it so it is the frontmost window.
Press Cmd+Shift+1 (the default Window to Chat chord).
Check the AGI chat composer: it should hold an image of only that window, not the whole screen.
If no other window is in front, look for the notice No other app window is in front to capture.
items.needs: macOS Screen & System Audio Recording permission; a second app window to capture
items.note: The Settings path to change this chord is in DesktopSettingsSection.tsx (row labelled Window to chat shortcut), but the nav label for that section was not found, so the path uses its heading instead.

items.where: Chat > open a document artifact from a reply (it opens in the artifact panel) > edit the text in the panel
steps: Ask the assistant in chat to write a document, for example a short memo.
Click the document card under the reply so it opens in the artifact panel.
Click into the document text and change a sentence.

Open the artifact's menu and click Restore only if you need to compare versions; otherwise look for the edited text remaining after you close and reopen the panel, and check that a new version was recorded.
items.needs: none
items.note: The rich document editor opens only when the document round-trips as Markdown (ArtifactDocumentEditor.tsx:53-60); I did not find a visible save-as-new-version label, so the version step is unverified.

items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: Searched apps/web/features/chat and apps/web/lib for a document-to-presentation control and found none; presentation artifacts exist (ArtifactPreview.tsx, title fallback 'Presentation') but no convert button. Production uploads also need UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:264-282).

items.where: Chat > attach an .xlsx file > ask for a chart inside a Word report > open the result in the artifact panel and choose Download as Word (.docx)
steps: Attach a spreadsheet (.xlsx) to a new chat message using the attach control in the composer.
Ask for an analysis with a chart, and a Word report that contains the chart.
When the report appears, open it in the artifact panel.
Open the artifact menu and click Download as Word (.docx); open the file and check that the chart is inside the report.
items.needs: a file to upload (an .xlsx); the sandbox path must be switched on by the owner (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION)
items.note: Code audit says the chart path needs the E2B switch-on and the upload scanner; the attach control's visible word was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat > ask for a research report > ask for an interactive page from it > open the page in the artifact panel > Publish
steps: Ask the assistant for a research report on a topic and wait for it to finish.
In the next message, ask for the report as an interactive page with charts and navigation.
Open the page in the artifact panel and check that it has charts, navigation and controls.
Open the artifact's menu and click Publish; check that a link is produced.
items.needs: none
items.note: The conversion is triggered by request wording (visual-intent.ts keywords); I found no dedicated one-step button.

items.where: Chat > voice mode > say a longer task out loud > Tasks in the sidebar
steps: Start voice mode from the chat.
Say a task that needs a longer piece of work, for example a research summary.
Wait for the voice assistant to confirm it is starting a task.
Open Tasks in the sidebar and check that the task is listed and running in the background without you retyping it.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The voice-mode entry control's visible words were not confirmed in VoiceModeSurface.tsx.

items.where: Chat > voice mode > ask for a document out loud > open the document from the voice session
steps: Start voice mode from the chat.
Say a request for a document, for example a Word file about a topic.
Wait until the document card appears in the voice session.
Open the document card and check that it opens as an artifact and can be downloaded.
items.needs: a microphone
items.note: Tool definition is in apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts:135; the voice entry control's visible words were not confirmed.

items.where: Schedules > open a scheduled task > Triggers for <task name> > Gmail
steps: Open the scheduled task page and open an existing scheduled task (or create one).
Find the trigger panel for the task and choose Gmail as the trigger type.
Read the note that says it runs for each new email and uses the Gmail address connected in Connectors.
Send a test email to the connected address and check that a tracked task run appears.
items.needs: an outside account (Google) with Gmail connected in Connectors
items.note: Forwarded-email and address-based thread selection were not found in the code; the 'Schedules' entry word was not confirmed in the sidebar.

items.needs: a Slack workspace; the owner must switch the sandbox on (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION) before the coding session can run
items.note: Slack settings exist in apps/web/features/settings/sections/SlackSection.tsx, but I found no visible path from a team mention to a coding session in /code; the feature depends on an owner switch-on.

items.where: Chat > finish a task > under the reply click Save as skill, or on a plugin draft card click Save as a skill > Settings > Skills
steps: Finish a task in chat (for example a repeated process with clear steps).
Under the final reply, click Save as skill (or on a draft card, click Save as a skill).
Open Settings and choose Skills.
Find the new skill in the list and invoke it in a new chat to check that it runs.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Skills entry is in the shared settings navigation; the parent group heading was not checked.

items.where: Visible on the phone app's chat list and in the same chat on web; the phone side is outside this folder
steps: On web or desktop, start a new chat and get one reply.
Open the AGI phone app with the same account and find the same chat in Chat history, with its full history.
On the phone, send a follow-up message.
Back on web, reload the chat and check that the phone's follow-up and its reply appear.
items.needs: a phone with the AGI mobile app signed in to the same account
items.note: I checked the web sync route (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts) and the sidebar item, not the phone app code.

items.where: Code > choose the folder the CLI session used > open the CLI session from the list
steps: Start a coding session in a folder from the terminal with the AGI command-line tool.
Open the desktop app and click Code in the sidebar.
Choose the same folder; if asked, click Allow running commands.
Open the session listed for that folder and send a follow-up; check that it continues the terminal session.
items.needs: the AGI command-line tool installed and a folder used in both places
items.note: The terminal command name was not confirmed; the session list is in apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionsSection.tsx and its visible heading was not found.

items.needs: VS Code installed; a folder with a desktop-app coding session
items.note: Searched LocalSessionsSection.tsx, apps/cli and apps/desktop/electron for a visible VS Code or open-in-IDE control and found none by visible text.

items.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control (pairing a phone); Linked devices lists paired computers
steps: On the computer, open Settings and choose Capabilities, then Remote Control, and pair the phone if it is not paired.
On the phone, send a new request to the paired computer.
On the computer, approve the request if an approval appears, and let the run finish.
On the phone, check that the result appears in the chat.
items.needs: a paired computer and a phone with the AGI app signed in to the same account
items.note: I did not check whether a flag hides Remote Control in this build.

items.where: Chat > composer > Project picker > choose a project > ask a question in that chat
steps: In a new chat, open the project picker in the composer.
Choose the project that holds the notebook's instructions and sources.
Ask a question that the project's sources cover.
Check that the answer uses the project's sources and instructions.
items.needs: a project with sources and instructions
items.note: The picker's visible words were not confirmed; the label above is the picker's project label in the code.

items.where: Chat > an answer's menu > Save to project > choose the project; then open the project and check Project sources
steps: Open a conversation with an answer you want to keep.
On the answer, open its menu and click Save to project.
Pick the project name in the list.
Open the project and check Project sources; then start a chat in that project and ask about the saved answer.
items.needs: a project to save into
items.note: The answer menu's trigger word was not confirmed; the save label is in MessageBubble.tsx.

items.where: Chat > send a message after usage is used up > the paywall card under the composer > Switch to <model name>, Buy credits or Upgrade to <plan>
steps: Send messages until a usage limit blocks a send.
Read the card under the composer and check which options it offers.
Click Switch to <model name> if it is offered (or Buy credits or Upgrade to).
Check that the chat continues and the reply comes from the new model.
items.needs: an account whose usage is used up (for example a Free account)
items.note: The labels are built from code templates, and the usage-block switch is in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; how to reach the limit was not confirmed.

items.needs: a published artifact on the account
items.note: PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx has a Published artifacts heading and a live-again message, but no settings nav entry for it was found in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts or apps/web/features/settings/components/web-settings-navigation.ts; the republish control is Publish in ArtifactPreview.tsx.

items.where: Open a shared artifact link from another account > Save a copy to my chats
steps: Sign in with a second account (not the owner).
Open a public or shared artifact link created by the first account.
Click Save a copy to my chats.
Open My chats and check that the copy opens with the same content and can be continued.
items.needs: a second account and a shared link from the first account

labels.text: Save a copy to my chats

items.note: The label is a fallback string in a translation call; the shared-conversation path (apps/web/app/chat/from-share/[token]/page.tsx) was not walked through.

items.where: Settings > Workspace > Share project with organization (sharing page at /workspace/sharing)
steps: Open Settings and choose Workspace.
Find the sharing section and click Share project with organization on one of your projects, with an access level if asked.
Sign in as a second member of the same workspace and find the shared item under Shared with your organization.
Open it and check that it opens with the access level you chose.
items.needs: a workspace with a second member in the same workspace; sharing rights depend on the member's role
items.note: The link from Settings to /workspace/sharing was not confirmed; the sharing section is mounted by apps/web/app/workspace/sharing/page.tsx.
